Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sells Fury vs Joshua As Biggest Fight Ever
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is out there calling Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua on December 11 in Cardiff the biggest fight in British boxing history, and nobody is buying it. Unlike Chris Eubank vs Nigel Benn or Carl Froch vs George Groves II, fans are barely talking about what happens inside the ring.

Instead of breaking down styles, boxing fans are stuck listening to Hearn complain about Dana White being involved and gripe about how terrible the main card undercard looks. Hearn even admitted he has nothing to do with the three main card support bouts and trashed putting unknown heavyweights like Da’Mazion Vanhouter ahead of Welsh two-time world champion Joe Cordina. That tells you everything about where the buzz actually is.

“When we talk about the biggest fight in British boxing history, Rick, it’s not even close,” said Hearn on Rick Reeno’s Mr. Versace podcast.

The energy is missing for a simple reason. This fight needed to happen between 2015 and 2018, or at the latest, when both men held all the heavyweight belts. Back then, fans wanted to see who was truly the top heavyweight in the world.

Since that window closed, both guys took heavy damage. Joshua got stopped by Andy Ruiz Jr. in 2019, lost twice to Oleksandr Usyk, and got blown away by Daniel Dubois. Even in his July comeback against Kristian Prenga in Jeddah, Joshua hit the canvas twice in the first round before pulling out a second-round knockout.

Fury doesn’t look much fresher at 38. After losing back-to-back fights to Usyk, Fury came back in April after more than a year out of the ring and looked old and slow, grinding out a decision over Arslanbek Makhmudov.

Eubank and Benn brought real hatred to the ring, and Froch vs Groves II had fans desperate for answers after a disputed first stoppage. Hearn can count casual Netflix viewers all he wants, yet hardcore fans know this matchup waited way too long.

Sports.title: A Determined Darius Fulghum Defeats Diego Pacheco
Sports.content:
Carson, California – Darius Fulghum had told Matchroom promoter Eddie Hearn and Diego Pacheco that they had made a mistake in choosing him as an opponent, and Saturday night he proved why. Fulghum controlled the inside with his jab and overpowered Pacheco in the clinches. Darius (16-1-1, 13 KOs) used his previous experience as a wrestler to maneuver and control the exchanges during the inside clinches.

At the post-fight press conference, he made note of everyone highlighting how great Diego’s jab was but no one speaking on his jab, saying, “I have a pretty good jab too.” Fulghum outlanded Pacheco in total punches, 197 to 147, landing an efficient 34.3 percent (Compubox).

Diego (26-1, 19 KOs) struggled offensively, being unable to land consistently, only landing a few big shots throughout the fight. He was unable to establish his jab consistently, despite having a four-inch reach advantage. Darius was a man on a mission, determined to redeem himself for his poor showing last November against David Stevens. He was grateful to Golden Boy for giving him a second opportunity at a big fight, saying, “You know the big thing going into the fight tonight, you know, like I said, this exact time last year. November of last year was one of the low points in my life. People wrote me off, you know. Saying he ain’t this and that. He ain’t that good, and I felt it, you know, and I was lost, man. It took those moments to really lock me back into the sport and really prove who I say I am. I’m “DFG,” the greatest. It was my mission to go out there and do my thing. Put my heart on the line. Give every ounce of me in the ring to come out victorious.”

It showed in the ring. Fulghum wanted it more; he was hungry and determined to win and go out on his shield.

All three judges scored it in Darius’ favor: Fernando Villareal and Jack Reiss both had it 115 to 112, and Pam Hayashi scored it 114-113. Hearn agreed with the judges’ scorecards and believes sometimes a loss like this is needed to regroup and become better. He stated that there is a rematch clause, and he believes Diego should exercise his right to it. After the fight, Pacheco said, “It wasn’t my night tonight. I didn’t feel like myself at the beginning, but I guess you get nights like that in boxing. Congratulations to Darius; he did what he had to do, but I would definitely love to run it back.”

Diego now finds himself in the situation Fulghum did last November; a poor performance will bring criticism and naysayers doubting his boxing skills.

How he responds remains to be seen. Darius had a strong showing against Bektemir Melikuziev, outlanding him by a punch 170 to 169 while boxing him on the inside and giving him a bloody nose. After defeating Pacheco, he has to be considered among the best in the division. Oscar De La Hoya posted via Instagram that a world title is next for Darius.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Sees Boots Ennis Fighting Canelo at 168
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is already trying to cash Jaron Ennis out in a 168-pound fight against Canelo Alvarez before his fighter has even proven himself at 154. Hearn went on Rick Reeno’s Mr. Versace podcast and claimed Ennis would jump straight over the middleweight division if he becomes undisputed at junior middleweight.

“We have a plan with Boots, and we always had that he would go 47, 54, 60, and 68,” Hearn said to Ring Magazine. “So, I know that if Boots became undisputed at 54 and you said to him, ‘Canelo Alvarez for the championship at 68,’ this guy’s a pure competitor. I think he’d be jumping around all over the divisions to be in fights like that.”

That is classic promoter hype designed to rush Ennis into a massive payday without making him fight dangerous guys at 160 first.

Ennis still has to beat Josh Kelly on February 27 in Atlanta with three belts on the line, and Kelly is not exactly a killer. Hearn claims DAZN and PBC will magically have a deal done by fight night so the winner faces Sebastian Fundora for the final strap. Anyone who follows boxing knows how easily deals between rival networks fall apart. Even if Ennis beats Kelly and Fundora, neither guy prepares him for real super middleweights.

Jumping 14 pounds is a massive gamble, even after Terence Crawford pulled it off against Canelo. Ennis looked good beating up Xander Zayas at 154, where he can punish smaller guys for walking in. Doing that against Canelo is a totally different story because Canelo has spent years taking punches from full-sized 168-pounders and light heavyweights. Ennis would be giving up way too much natural size and strength just to chase a big check.

Hearn admitted he still wants to see Ennis fight Vergil Ortiz Jr. at 160 if Ortiz wins a title there. That is the fight fans actually want, and it would show whether Ennis can take a punch from a real banger before moving up again. Skipping middleweight to grab a Canelo lottery ticket looks like a shortcut.

Canelo has his own business to handle at 168, and Ennis has done nothing at super middleweight to earn that spot. Until Ennis beats Kelly, actually gets Fundora in the ring, and proves he belongs with bigger men, all this Canelo talk is pure noise.

Sports.title: Canelo Eyes Willy Hutchinson While Osleys Iglesias Waits
Sports.content:
If Canelo Alvarez stays at 168 pounds for his next fight, IBF champion Osleys Iglesias is clearly the guy he needs to be fighting. Instead, trainer Eddy Reynoso is already floating a move back up to 175 to face newly crowned WBC light heavyweight belt-holder Willy Hutchinson, right after Canelo just recaptured the WBC super middleweight title from Christian Mbilli.

“Yes, without a doubt, Hutchinson is an option for Canelo. We’ll see,” Reynoso told ESPN KnockOut. He claimed he has been watching Hutchinson for several fights and likes Canelo’s chances, with March 2027 being tossed around for the final bout of Canelo’s Riyadh Season contract.

You can see why Reynoso would want this fight. Hutchinson doesn’t possess single-punch power in either hand the way the Cuban Osleys have. So the worst Canelo could fear is getting outboxed for 12 rounds the way Terence Crawford and Floyd Mayweather Jr. did.

Hutchinson just picked up the vacant WBC strap by outpointing Joshua Buatsi earlier this month, and he has already told talkSPORT that Canelo is too small for him. However, the WBC says Hutchinson owes two mandatory defenses, so it is fair to wonder how that fight even gets made without belt politics getting in the way. If Canelo asks the WBC to allow him the opportunity to face Hutchinson first, there’s a chance they’ll grant his request.

Canelo’s track record at 175 tells you everything about why his team might like this route. He stopped a faded Sergey Kovalev in 2019, then got schooled by Dmitry Bivol in 2022. Against Mbilli at 168, Canelo had enough left to get the win, but he fought in brief spurts.

Taking on a bigger, younger champion like 28-year-old Hutchinson gives Canelo a built-in alibi if things go wrong. If he loses at 175, he can point to the weight he was giving up and still get credit for daring to be great.

If he stays at 168 and loses to a dangerous puncher like Iglesias or even Hamzah Sheeraz, there is nowhere to hide. Fans will rake over the coals for losing, especially if it’s against Hamzah. He’s not held in high esteem by many fans for giving up his WBO belt when ordered to face Janibek Alimkhanuly.

If Canelo wants real credit at super middleweight, he should unify against Iglesias instead of picking another low-risk trip up to light heavyweight. As good as Hutchinson looked beating Buatsi in their rematch, he still isn’t widely known by many Americans. They would see him as a cherry pick by Canelo just based on being unfamiliar with Hutchinson.

Sports.title: Fans Remind Vergil Ortiz That Zayas Actually Fought Ennis
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. called Xander Zayas arrogant and said he didn’t like him in a recent DAZN Boxing clip. Plenty of fans heard jealousy in those remarks. The fighter Ortiz singled out is four years younger, has already unified two world titles at 154 pounds, and took the Jaron “Boots” Ennis fight that Ortiz’s own team couldn’t close.

“Yeah the dude that stepped in and fought the fight you were suppose to take. Because what!?” wrote @boxing_eric in the replies. Another commenter, @DrBoxingTalk, pointed to the exact same two things missing from Ortiz’s resume: a unified championship and a bout with Ennis.

Beyond the belts, many fans view Zayas as a proactive go-getter who stays healthy, keeps an active schedule, and jumps at major opportunities without dragging his feet. Ortiz, by contrast, has lost long stretches of his prime to recurring illness, fight postponements, and promotional friction. While Ortiz was sidelined or stuck in legal disputes, Zayas kept showing up and moving forward.

Ortiz, 28, holds a spotless record and has good reason to rate his wins over Serhii Bohachuk, Israil Madrimov, and Erickson Lubin. He also had a legitimate interest in fighting Zayas. Golden Boy proposed a 50/50 split for a December 2025 bout in California or Nevada. Zayas considered the offer unfavorable, and the two sides never reached a deal.

The Ennis situation is where Ortiz’s own decisions deserve a closer look. Ortiz tried to make the fight without Golden Boy while disputing his promotional contract. The company secured a court order that blocked him from signing with a third party for the bout. Ennis moved on, and Zayas stepped up to defend both his WBA and WBO belts in Brooklyn.

Zayas was 23 when he took that risk. He won the vacant WBO title against Jorge García Pérez and added the WBA belt by edging Abass Baraou in San Juan. He could have spent years milking those titles against soft opposition before facing Ennis. Instead, he put both straps on the line in his very first fight as a unified champion and was stopped in seven rounds.

Calling Zayas arrogant is easy. The tougher question for Ortiz is how a fighter four years younger collected two belts, stayed active, and landed a date with Ennis while Ortiz is still waiting for his first full world title.

Sports.title: Will Shakur Stevenson Give Up His WBO Belt Over Muratalla Money?
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson faces a major financial crossroads ahead of Monday’s 3 p.m. ET WBO deadline, where the money on the table may not match the risk of fighting Raymond Muratalla. After earning massive purses in his last three outings, Stevenson has made it clear he is strictly chasing top dollar.

Without Saudi funding underwriting the event, traditional promoters must finance a mandatory defense carrying high danger and limited commercial upside. Facing Muratalla (25-0, 17 KOs) simply will not generate the revenue Stevenson could have commanded had he stayed with Zuffa Boxing and finalized a clash with Devin Haney.

Following the WBO’s October 27 order, both camps had 20 days to make a deal. With no agreement or extension announced as of Sunday night, Stevenson’s promotional free agency after leaving Zuffa leaves him exposed to a purse bid where Top Rank, Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn, and other promoters decide what the fight is worth.

The WBO’s auction rules offer little comfort to a fighter used to massive paydays. The sanctioning body sets a $150,000 minimum bid for light welterweight title fights, with a 75/25 split favoring the champion in his home country. Even when winning bids clear that floor, 75 percent of an unsubsidized bid is a steep drop from the Zuffa money Stevenson walked away from. Monday’s cutoff simply ends negotiations before the WBO sets a separate date for offers.

“Now is not the time to mess up the plan,” Hearn told BoxingScene about Stevenson’s next move. Hearn has pitched an undisputed run at 140 pounds featuring Gary Antuanne Russell and Dalton Smith, yet someone still has to fund the mandatory hurdle in front of them. A purse bid forces Hearn and rival promoters to show how much cash they will risk on one fight without locking Stevenson into a multi-fight deal.

That hesitation comes down to the opponent. Muratalla vacated his IBF lightweight belt to move up to 140 after beating Andy Cruz and Robson Conceicao. For Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs), defending the WBO title he won from Teofimo Lopez in January against a heavy-handed former champion is genuinely dangerous. At the box office, however, Muratalla lacks the star power to drive pay-per-view buys or justify an eight-figure guarantee without outside funding from the Saudis.

It remains unclear whether Stevenson will keep his WBO strap or give it up. Vacating lets him bypass a tough matchup for less money, leaving the WBO to match Muratalla for the vacant belt. If Stevenson keeps the title and refuses the mandatory defense, the WBO can strip him. Either route costs him the championship leverage needed for unifications at 140, forcing him to weigh whether keeping the belt is worth a pay cut after leaving bigger Zuffa money behind.

Sports.title: Harlem Eubank Wants Devin Haney Next, Yet Books Greg Outlaw
Sports.content:
Harlem Eubank is talking about Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez, which takes some nerve for a 32-year-old welterweight who has lost two of his last three fights and hit the canvas three times in his last outing. Instead of proving he belongs anywhere near that tier, Eubank is retreating to his comfort zone at the Brighton Centre on February 5, 2027, to face WBA No. 13 contender Greg Outlaw live on DAZN.

Calling this a fresh start for a world title run is a tough sell. Eubank lost to Jack Catterall, came home to Brighton to pick up a routine decision over Josh Wagner, and then dropped a 12-round decision to David Papot in July. Going back to the south coast for a fourth time looks less like a championship march and more like hitting the safety button between defeats. Even MF Pro didn’t bill the fight as a title eliminator.

Outlaw’s WBA ranking looks good on a promotional poster until you actually read his record. The 33-year-old from Maryland is riding a seven-fight win streak, yet he has spent a decade fighting almost exclusively on small club shows around Maryland and D.C. The only recognizable name on his 21-fight resume is Jonathan Montrel, whom he beat in 2022, while his two losses came against Andrew Rodgers (4-9-2 at the time) and Juan Meza Angulo. Worse still, Outlaw hasn’t fought since February 2026, meaning he walks into Brighton after a full year on the shelf.

“There’s a lot of guys in the States on the world scene that I am looking to fight. (Devin) Haney, (Teofimo) Lopez. This is the first step next year, and we are really looking to push on,” said Eubank in the fight announcement.

For Eubank (22-2, 9 KOs), beating Outlaw (19-2, 11 KOs) is the bare minimum after getting dropped three times by Papot and fading down the stretch. Haney and Lopez aren’t lining up to fight a guy rebuilding in Brighton against an inactive regional fighter. Eubank has won all three of his previous outings at the Brighton Centre, and anything less than a dominant win here should put the world title talk to rest.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Is Begging for an Early Knockout Against Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly is begging for trouble if he actually wants Jaron “Boots” Ennis to jump on him early in their February 27, 2027, three-belt junior middleweight unification fight in Atlanta. Kelly believes he can catch Ennis coming in the same way Xander Zayas briefly did in the third round.

What he ignores is that Ennis walked straight through Zayas’ best shot and stopped him anyway, and Kelly lacks Zayas’ punching power to keep Boots off him.

“So, if he’s going to commit early like that, it’s good for me,” said Kelly to Fighthype after an interviewer told him Ennis was predicting an early stoppage. Asked what gave Zayas his opening, Kelly put it down to Ennis’ own success. “He was having so much success. He didn’t think about what was coming back. So, he’s going to have to be a little bit smarter with me, I guess.”

That sounds brave, but Kelly barely survived back-to-back grueling fights against Bakhram Murtazaliev and Caoimhín Agyarko that easily could have gone the other way, and neither fighter is in Ennis’ league.

Kelly pointed to his win over Murtazaliev as proof he can make Ennis respect what is coming back, recalling a second round shot that drew a nod before dropping Murtazaliev in the fourth. What Kelly leaves out is that it was a flash knockdown from a shot Murtazaliev never saw. Murtazaliev got right back up, chased Kelly around the ring, and dropped him in the ninth in a fight many felt Murtazaliev won.

Against Agyarko, Kelly suffered heavy nose damage and three facial cuts in a razor-close decision win over a lighter puncher than Ennis. Going back further, the last time Kelly faced a heavy-handed pressure fighter in David Avanesyan in 2021, he fell apart and got stopped in six rounds with his face a bloody mess.

Kelly said unseen shots do the most damage and claimed he can adjust from round to round. Based on how he has looked since Avanesyan, getting on his bike like he did against Murtazaliev will not save him. Ennis cuts off the ring too well, and Kelly will not last six rounds if he fights just to survive.

Ghana News.title: Customers report service outages at major US banks
Ghana News.content:
Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, have reported trouble accessing services.

Chase Bank - the largest banking institution in the US - said a "software bug" in its hardware systems may have been behind the glitch and noted the impacts may have affected other banks. It added the issue was "temporary" and not "systemic" or "cyber-related".

Problems appeared to be easing for many customers by early Monday evening.

The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems last week, including a massive Microsoft outage, as well as a telecommunications issue and network failure that grounded all US flights.

Problems started throughout the afternoon on Monday. There were almost 5,000 reports of Chase Bank's services being down, according to the Downdetector website.

Chase Bank told it's customers that "some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete" but they still had "access to their accounts and funds".

The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company's webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US.

The exact nature of the bug was unclear. The BBC has contacted Chase Bank.

Another institution, US Bank, said some its systems were not directly affected but clients using the Zelle, a digital payment platform, received error messages saying their payments could not be sent.

Zelle has said its service is "operating as it should" and issues at other banks could be affecting payments.

Customers also reported issues with Truist, PNC and Capital One but all these companies told the BBC they have not been impacted.

As of 1800 ET (2300G), Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had seen a fall in the number of reported outages.

Ghana News.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
Ghana News.content:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.

Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.

"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.

The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.

Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.

Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries.

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would bea cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."

The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place.

According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

Ghana News.title: One dead as firefighters battle Railways Area blaze at Kwame Nkrumah Circle
Ghana News.content:
A man has been burnt to death after a fire swept through the Railways Area behind the State Transport Corporation (STC) station at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra.

The extent of the damage and the circumstances surrounding the victim’s death were yet to be fully established as firefighting operations continued for hours.

Several wooden structures were engulfed in the Monday night blaze, sending thick smoke billowing into the sky and prompting an emergency response from the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS).

The fire broke out close to the parking areas of VIP and OA Transport Services, near the Kwame Nkrumah Interchange.

A member of the GNFS Communications Team, Assistant Divisional Officer I Alex King Nartey, confirmed the death of an adult male, whose identity had not been established at the time of reporting.

He told Joy News journalist Collins Frimpong that multiple fire appliances had been dispatched to the scene, with firefighters working to contain the blaze and stop it from spreading to nearby structures.

Although the cause of the fire remains unknown, Mr Nartey criticised some squatters at the scene for continuing to smoke despite the raging inferno.

Ghana News.title: Three fire tenders deployed as fire hits Tema Community 1 Market
Ghana News.content:
Firefighters are battling to contain a fire outbreak at the Tema Community 1 Market, near the Community 1 Police Station.

Three fire tenders have been dispatched to the scene as personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) work to bring the blaze under control and prevent it from spreading to adjoining shops.

The outbreak was reported on Monday, November 16, 2026, with the GNFS confirming the deployment in an update shared on social media platforms.

The cause of the fire, the number of shops affected and the extent of damage had not been established at the time of reporting. There were also no immediate reports of casualties.

The incident has renewed concerns about fire safety at the busy market, which has experienced previous outbreaks.

In February this year, a fire at the same market destroyed two shops and partially damaged four others. No casualties were recorded in that incident, according to the Ghana National Fire Service.

Ghana News.title: Photos from Day 1-3: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026
Ghana News.content:
The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 brought together three days of business exhibitions, product displays, shopping bargains, networking and live entertainment at Ghud Park, Accra Mall, from November 13 to 15.

- Day 1 – Friday, November 13: The fair opened with more than 80 businesses showcasing products and services across food and beverages, fashion, beauty, agriculture, technology, electronics and household products. Joy Prime's KMJ and content creator Quecy Official engaged exhibitors and patrons, while Nkyimkyim Band provided musical entertainment.

- Day 2 – Saturday, November 14: Business exhibitions and shopping continued, with Ghanaian music duo Lali X Lola and King Jerry delivering energetic performances. Patrons sang and danced, while some vendors even carried their products onto the dance floor, creating an exciting blend of business and entertainment.

- Day 3 – Sunday, November 15: The final day attracted shoppers seeking last-minute bargains, product discoveries and business connections. The Kekeli Borborbor Group and Shakers Band added cultural and musical excitement, bringing the three-day exhibition to a colourful close.

The fair featured more than 80 brands, including Ecobank, MTN, GEPA, Glico Life and numerous Ghanaian SMEs showcasing locally made foods, beverages, clothing, cosmetics, agricultural products, technology and household essentials.

Organised by the Multimedia Group in partnership with Ecobank and powered by JoyPrime, the event provided SMEs with opportunities to increase brand visibility, attract customers, generate sales and establish business partnerships.

It ended as a vibrant celebration of Ghanaian entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation, successfully combining commerce, networking, shopping and entertainment.

Ghana News.title: Nvidia dismisses ‘Bring Jensen Back’ campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
Ghana News.content:
President Trump and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang at a White House event this year

Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort.

Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's ​access to AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since his departure, supporters have launched an online petition demanding his return.

Musk and Sweeny are among the more than 175,000 who have signed the open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by a make up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive.

They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".

President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.

"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models.

The move came ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jingping this week.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted to China.

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".

Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

'China plays games with us, so we play games with China'

On Monday, Trump said he did not know whether the women Huang had an affair with was a spy for China.

"They say she's a spy. I don't know that she was a spy at all. I mean, I really don't, I don't know that," he said.

Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.

Trump said he did not think Huang had put national security at risk. "You know, China plays games with us. So we play games with China," he said.

The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.

'A handshake with Jensen'

Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract," he posted on X.

"Without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

Fellow tech boss Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, sidestepped the question of Huang returning to Nvidia at a conference, saying: "I don't think I know enough to answer that question."

But Altman, who himself was reinstated to his job after being fired back in 2023, said Huang was a "hero of mine".

Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at the company's helm.

Hundreds of billions of pounds have been wiped off the firm's stock market value in recent days, but it is still worth some $3.87 trillion. Its share price was down in early Monday trading.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.

For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

Ghana News.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
Ghana News.content:
This article contains distressing details and references to suicide

A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.

Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Dr Barbara Sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein." The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.

Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.

He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.

Freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by Mark Epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.

Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

He said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".

He said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide."

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General that Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.

Freeman said he would have expected in an investigation of a death by hanging in custody for there to be a photograph before the body was taken down.

According to a DoJ investigation into Epstein's time in prison, the guard who found Epstein immediately called for a second colleague to help, lowered Epstein's body to the floor and began attempts to resuscitate him.

Epstein's death came a month after he was briefly placed on suicide watch, the DoJ report said.

When asked who might have killed Epstein if his interpretation of the evidence was correct, Freeman said he had "no idea".

"That is not something I have an opinion about. That isn't any part of any investigation that I've done," he said.

Challenged on whether his views veered into conspiracy theory, Freeman said: "I have the luxury of being able to say, don't take my word for it, let everybody look at it."

"If you think I'm still a conspiracy theorist because I'm looking at something that looks like a strangulation and say, I think it is a strangulation and I don't think it could be a hanging, show me where I got it wrong."

"I'm wide open to that. I'm an academic. I'm quite happy to hear people's theories on things that are informed," he said.

Epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. He escaped a heavy jail sentence as a result of a plea deal.

Eleven years later, Epstein was charged with running a network of underage girls for sex. He was awaiting trial in 2019 when he was found dead at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York City.

Ghana News.title: Dikan brings the story of Nkrumah to more than 6,000 people
Ghana News.content:
Dikan’s screenings of 'The Eyes of Ghana' brought the story of Kwame Nkrumah, told through his cameraman Chris Hesse, to more than 6,000 people, according to the institution.

Pictured: Chris Hesse and Founder/ Executive Director of Dikan, Paul Ninson

The programme combined four screenings at Dikan with events at four other locations, ending at the National Theatre on 13 November 2026.

Alongside its own screenings, Dikan organised showings at Adjaye Associates, Africa Feature Institute, Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and the National Theatre.

It served as both a venue and the organiser taking the documentary to audiences elsewhere. The attendance figure covers the full programme across those five locations.

At Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park on 31 October, the connection between the film and its setting was immediate.

The Eyes of Ghana follows Chris Hesse’s effort to save films from the era of African independence

A documentary about the man who recorded Ghana’s first president was being shown at the place dedicated to the president’s memory. Admission was free, with registration through Dikan.

The memorial screening approached Nkrumah’s story through someone who had stood behind the camera. As the president’s personal cinematographer, Hesse recorded the years of African independence in the 1950s and 1960s.

His account brings the work of making and protecting that visual record into the history of the political leader it depicts.

Directed by Ben Proudfoot, the documentary follows Hesse’s effort to rescue and repatriate more than 1,300 films from that period.

The task extends beyond finding surviving footage. The film follows the work of bringing historical material back into public view, decades after the events it recorded, with Hesse’s experience as a filmmaker and custodian of those images at its centre.

Ghanaian filmmaker Anita Afonu is part of that story. Her work and friendship with Hesse lead to plans for a public screening at the Rex. Within the documentary, recovering films and preparing to show them become connected tasks.

Dikan’s programme subsequently brought the finished documentary to viewers, giving them access to the account of Hesse’s work and the history it contains.

The final screening at the National Theatre on 13 November also offered free admission and registration through Dikan. It followed the Memorial Park event and closed the institution’s run of the documentary.

Across the programme, viewers had opportunities to see the film at Dikan itself and at the other locations.

For Dikan, whose wider work includes archives, education and exhibitions, the subject connected directly to its interest in preserving African knowledge and making it available for learning.

Its screening announcement made that connection explicit. Through the programme, a film about the survival of Ghana’s historical record became part of the institution’s public work, with audiences attending screenings both within and beyond its premises.

'The Eyes of Ghana' is now available to watch free on IShowSpeed’s YouTube channel.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ethiopia Moyale clashes disrupt livelihoods as territorial dispute deepens
World.content:
Moyale, Ethiopia – Fighting involving police and armed groups affiliated with Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regional administrations has disrupted daily life and trade in the southern Borana Zone, as efforts to resolve a longstanding territorial dispute have yet to produce a lasting settlement.

The violence, which escalated in the border town of Moyale in October, has spread to surrounding areas, including the neighbouring districts of Arero and Wachile, leaving communities insecure and uncertain when normal life will resume.

The disruption has affected livelihoods across several parts of the zone, particularly the livestock trade – a major source of income for rural communities. Residents have reported interruptions to business activities and transport services.

A resident of Moyale town, who asked not to be named for security reasons, told Al Jazeera that people remained fearful as tensions persisted between forces affiliated with the two regional administrations.

The resident said gunfire, especially at night, had heightened personal safety concerns, while violence had restricted movement around the town and made routine activities increasingly difficult. Businesses, people raising livestock and transport operators had also been affected, leaving residents uncertain about when the situation would return to normal.

A territorial dispute reignites violence

According to Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED), the latest escalation began on October 18, when Somali regional police clashed with ethnic Oromo militia members following the opening of a Somali regional administration office and the raising of its flag in a disputed locality of Moyale.



The conflict monitor’s East Africa senior analyst, Jalale Getachew Birru, reported that a 13-year-old Oromo girl was killed during the confrontation. However, accounts of how she died differ: some people said she was caught in crossfire, while others claimed she was killed after trying to remove the flag.

Members of the Ethiopian National Defence Force intervened and stopped the initial fighting, according to ACLED. The following day, Oromo residents staged a demonstration against the office opening and the girl’s death, blocking the main road and forcing businesses to close.

Elders and security officials from both sides later agreed to remove the Somali regional flag and suspend the office’s opening. However, the agreement did not prevent further confrontations. ACLED reported that Somali residents also demonstrated against the arrangement on October 20, closing the main road and disrupting transport services.

Fighting escalated again on October 22, when Somali regional police clashed with Oromia regional police and Oromo militia members in several locations in Moyale. ACLED also reported clashes involving Oromo and Somali militias in parts of Arero and Wachile districts.

The violence is rooted in longstanding disagreements over administrative boundaries, political representation and access to land and natural resources. These disputes have repeatedly fuelled tensions between Borana Oromo and Somali communities along the regional border.

Federal government under pressure to intervene

A security official familiar with the situation in Moyale told Al Jazeera that clashes were continuing and that attempts to broker an agreement between representatives of the Oromia and Somali regional administrations had failed. He said resolving the crisis required direct and immediate involvement by the federal government.

The federal government’s role has consequently become a central question in efforts to contain the violence. Although members of the Ethiopian National Defence Force intervened during the initial October 18 confrontation, ACLED documented further clashes involving regional police and militia members from October 22 onwards.

The crisis has also drawn attention beyond Ethiopia’s borders. On November 9, Kenya’s Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi said he had spoken with his Ethiopian counterpart and urged the government in Addis Ababa to help restore stability so that people who had fled into Kenya could return home.

Reporting by Kenya’s The Star newspaper said Mudavadi put the number of Ethiopians who had crossed into Kenya at approximately 40,000 at the time. He said the Ethiopian government had assured Kenya that it would work towards restoring normality.



Unresolved boundaries and political tensions

Cameron Hudson, a political and security analyst and former director for African affairs at the US National Security Council, said the crisis reflected wider challenges facing Ethiopia’s federal system and its management of regional disputes.

Hudson said federal forces were already preoccupied with security challenges elsewhere in the country. He also pointed to a perception among Somali communities that Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed and his Prosperity Party favour the Oromo, Abiy’s ethnic group.

Hudson said previous mediation efforts had largely failed because the territorial dispute along the regional border remained unresolved.

The historical background includes a referendum organised on October 24, 2004, to determine the administration of 463 small communities along the Oromia-Somali regional border, according to Ethiopia’s National Election Board.

However, research by Boku Tache, published in a doctoral thesis at the Norwegian University of Life Sciences in 2008, found that the referendum was conducted in Liban and parts of Arero, while the Moyale case remained unresolved.

The research also examined how displacement, competing claims over grazing land and access to traditional resources contributed to tensions between Borana and Somali communities. These historical disputes continue to provide important context for the current confrontation.

Hudson added that successive Ethiopian governments had failed to engage local communities to address the underlying causes of territorial tensions, instead responding after violence had erupted.

The humanitarian consequences have extended beyond Ethiopia. On October 28, the United Nations refugee agency (UNHCR) said local authorities estimated that up to 50,000 people had crossed into Kenya since October 22 to escape the fighting. The agency said registration and verification were continuing, meaning the figure remained provisional.

Many of those arriving in Kenya were women and children, according to the UNHCR, which identified food, drinking water, emergency shelter, sanitation and healthcare as urgent needs.

For residents in the affected areas, immediate priorities remain the restoration of security and the resumption of livelihoods. With the territorial dispute unresolved and the two regional administrations yet to reach a lasting agreement, uncertainty continues over when affected communities will be able to return to normal life.

“The federal government is ultimately responsible for addressing violence, even along regional borders,” Hudson told Al Jazeera.

World.title: Paraguay ex-president moved to military jail amid special treatment reports
World.content:
Santiago Pena has been accused of corruption following the collapse of Ueno Bank earlier this month.

Paraguay’s former President Santiago Pena has been transferred to a military prison on a judge’s orders, following reports that he was granted special amenities while awaiting trial for a financial corruption scandal.

On Monday, Judge Osmar Legal ordered Pena to be moved from the Presidential Escort Regiment, a military base in the capital city of Asuncion.

There, media reports indicated he had a large dining room, furnishings, a private gym and a bathroom, sparking public backlash.

His new lodgings are inside Vinas Cue military prison. Pena, however, is to be held separately from the facility’s other prisoners for his safety.

Allegations against the former president are at the centre of a corruption scandal related to the collapse of a major financial lender, Ueno Bank, used by more than half of the country’s adult population.

The political crisis erupted into the public spotlight on November 3, when Paraguay’s central bank took control of Ueno after declaring it insolvent.

In doing so, it froze account activity for nearly three million people. In the months before its collapse, Ueno held roughly $850m in public funds, including money for retirement pensions.

The scandal led to the end of Pena’s presidency. A member of the conservative Colorado Party, a leading force in Paraguay’s politics, Pena saw his political allies distance themselves from him in the wake of the lender’s collapse.

His attempts to resign were rejected, as Paraguay’s Congress instead pursued impeachment proceedings against him. He was removed from office on November 6.



As criminal investigations unfolded, scrutiny fell on Pena’s role as a shareholder in Ueno’s parent company. Pena has denied wrongdoing and said he sold his shares in 2025.

Prosecutors, however, have accused Pena of using his position in office to direct public funds to the bank while it made insider loans to owners.

He faces charges including breach of trust, criminal association and administration for personal gain. Angry protests accompanied Pena’s removal, and he was ordered to be held in pretrial detention.

His former vice president, Pedro Alliana, has since been sworn in to lead Paraguay’s executive branch.

In a news conference on Monday, Alliana said he had dismissed a military official, Colonel Jose David Daiub, accused of giving Pena special treatment while in detention.

“Our priority is to guarantee the country’s stability, restore confidence, and provide concrete and rapid solutions,” said Alliana.

Paraguayans, he added, “deserve to know the truth”. Pena’s transfer to a military prison came on his 48th birthday.
