World.title: EU agrees to resurrect cooperation deal with Syria
World.content:
Decision aims to bolster the bloc’s ties with Damascus following the Assad government’s collapse in December 2024.

European Union foreign ministers have agreed to revive a nearly 20-year-old cooperation deal with Syria, as the bloc presses to strengthen ties with the war-scarred country.

“Syria needs investment and a successful transition,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Monday.

“The aim is to give Europe and Syria a framework for trade, political dialogue and closer cooperation as soon as possible.”

The EU-Syria association agreement was first made in 2008 under then-President Bashar al-Assad, but it was never fully signed by either side, owing to concerns over the Assad government’s human rights record.

Kallas said EU foreign ministers meeting in Brussels had “supported moving ahead” with that deal and launching talks for an updated one.

A discussion paper prepared by the bloc’s diplomatic service ahead of the meeting outlined one of Brussels’ most ambitious efforts yet to normalise ties with Syria, less than two years after Assad’s fall.

Kallas said diplomats would now work through the technical and legal details to finalise the agreement, which would create a framework for free trade, political dialogue and broader cooperation between Brussels and Damascus.

“Everybody said that we need to engage with Syria because if we don’t engage, then this vacuum will be filled by other players,” Kallas said.

Kallas said the EU would set out new conditions for Syria to secure an updated deal.

“We should have clear conditionality regarding human rights,” she said.

“We should have also the nonrecognition of occupied Ukrainian, Georgian territories that they have recognised under Assad’s regime.”

The move is the latest in the 27-nation bloc’s efforts to bolster ties with Damascus and its new leader, President Ahmed al-Sharaa.



The EU in 2025 removed its crushing sanctions on Syria’s economy in a bid to help its recovery after almost 14 years of civil war.

At the start of 2026, Brussels announced a two-year funding package worth 620 million euros ($680m) for the country.

The 53-year-long rule of the Assad family ended on December 8, 2024, after an 11-day offensive that took Syria and the world by surprise.

It also halted a lengthy civil war that left lasting scars on the country and saw some 6.8 million Syrians, about one-third of the population, flee abroad.

More than one million Syrian refugees have already returned home since Assad’s fall, while millions more among the diaspora weigh the decision to do the same and rebuild their lives in their homeland.

World.title: US Pentagon rejects allegations linking deputy to a Goldman Sachs banker
World.content:
The Department of Defense has defended Steve Feinberg amid claims that he encouraged defence contractors to use a specific banker.

Share US Pentagon rejects allegations linking deputy to a Goldman Sachs banker on social media

The Pentagon has denied reports that Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg pushed defence contractors to work with a specific Goldman Sachs banker with whom he had longstanding ties.

In a statement sent to Al Jazeera on Monday, the Pentagon said the allegations were “baseless”.

“Any claim that the Deputy directed companies to use Goldman Sachs is categorically false. He worked with financial firms across the industry throughout his entire career,” Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in the statement.

“He has no favorites, and neither does the Department of War.”

The publication Bloomberg first reported the allegations, citing anonymous sources familiar with the matter.

According to Bloomberg’s report, Feinberg guided defence contractors like Lockheed Martin and RTX towards working with Goldman Sachs banker Jim Donovan during their negotiations with the Pentagon.

Donovan and Feinberg reportedly knew each other. Bloomberg said Donovan has previously worked for the investment firm Feinberg co-founded, Cerberus Capital Management, which claims to oversee $70bn in assets.

Bloomberg’s report has raised concerns about a conflict of interest during the lucrative Pentagon negotiations.

Defence contracts are often million, if not billion, dollar deals. Guiding a company that is competing for a contract to work with a specific banker could be seen as a way of rigging the negotiations.

It would also put the banker in line to potentially receive large commissions from the contracts in question.



According to Bloomberg, both RTX and Lockheed Martin hired Donovan after Feinberg’s suggestion.

The Pentagon, however, has accused Bloomberg of seeking to lend credibility to unsubstantiated allegations.

“Despite the Department’s categorical denial, Bloomberg appears more interested in advancing a baseless smear than establishing the facts. Your sources are playing you, and Bloomberg should know better,” Deputy Pentagon Press Secretary Jacob Bliss told Al Jazeera.

“The Deputy is a man of honor and integrity. Unfortunately, some would rather see him fail than succeed.”

Feinberg was nominated by President Donald Trump for his position in one of the Pentagon’s top posts.

The Senate confirmed him in a vote of 59 to 40, and he was sworn in as the 36th deputy defense secretary on March 17, 2025, according to the Pentagon.

Lockheed Martin and RTX, both aerospace and defence companies, have longstanding ties to the Pentagon.

In August, for instance, the Department of Defense announced a multibillion-dollar deal with Lockheed Martin and another defence giant Northrop Grumman to boost production of parts for the Patriot PAC-3 and THAAD missile interceptor systems.

According to Bloomberg’s reporting, Donovan, the banker, was a part of several deals in recent months involving Lockheed Martin and RTX.

They include a $59bn contract with Lockheed Martin for Patriot missiles and two missile contracts worth approximately $45bn with RTX.

It is unclear who the anonymous sources for Bloomberg’s story might be.

Under Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Pentagon has opened multiple investigations into leaks of sensitive information and taken steps to limit journalists’ access to military officials and other Pentagon resources.

World.title: Germany thrash Netherlands to book quarterfinal spot
World.content:
An impressive Germany swept aside off-colour Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin to pip the Dutch to first place in UEFA Nations League Group A2.

Germany needed a win to stand a chance of reaching the quarterfinals, starting the night in third place behind Greece, who had won 1-0 in Germany in September, by virtue of their head-to-head record.

Jurgen Klopp’s side produced a fine attacking display to inflict the heaviest defeat on the Dutch in 67 years, as Xavi Hernandez’s side looked very ragged as they shipped four goals in 17 second-half minutes.

Greece’s win over Serbia left the top three sides level on 11 points, but Germany took the top spot on head-to-head while the Dutch finished second, qualifying for the last eight on goal difference thanks largely to their 7-0 win over Greece on Friday.

After a quiet opening 20 minutes, Kai Havertz headed straight at keeper Bart Verbruggen from a Joshua Kimmich free-kick, while Donyell Malen headed a Cody Gakpo cross from the left of the area over the bar from close range soon after.

Berlin-born Derry Scherhant fired a half-volley against the outside of the Dutch post on 32 minutes after collecting a cross from the right byline, but it turned out to be a range-finder as Scherhant scored his first international goal from a similar position on 44 minutes. After cutting in from the left of the area and working space, he flashed an unstoppable shot past Verbruggen and into the far top corner.

Scherhant almost grabbed his second a minute after the interval as he jinked and bundled his way through on goal on the left of the area only to lash a left-footed effort over the bar with only Verbruggen to beat.



Denzel Dumfries headed over the bar at the other end after running onto a bouncing cross at the back post after ghosting past Scherhant on 48 minutes. Meanwhile, the lively Brajan Gruda came close to a spectacular second at the other end after some neat control and cutting in from the right before flashing a shot past the upright from the edge of the Dutch box.

Soon after, Gakpo tested ter Stegen with a low strike from outside the box, but Germany made him pay as Florian Wirtz doubled the lead with a stunning strike into the top corner from the edge of the D with his left foot on the hour.

Nico Schlotterbeck glanced home a header from Gruda’s curling free-kick from the left within five minutes to make it 3-0, and the fourth arrived soon after as Gruda was allowed to glide into the area on the right and get to the byline before dinking the ball back into the middle for the unmarked Wirtz to lash home his second goal with a volley off the underside of the bar.

Gruda nearly added a goal to his two assists as his rising shot was stopped by Verbruggen after another silky run, but the 22-year-old eventually marked his second cap with his second international goal on 77 minutes when he fired home the rebound after Scherhant’s shot came back off the inside of the post.

It led to Verbruggen calling an impromptu huddle outside his area as the visitors sought to end their misery, and they saw the game out without further alarm.

Germany will be seeded in Friday’s draw for the last eight, which will be contested over two legs in March.

World.title: California files lawsuit against OpenAI alleging lack of proper safeguards
World.content:
Attorney General Rob Bonta says Hugging Face attack was ‘entirely predictable’ result of emphasis on rapid growth.

California has filed a lawsuit against the technology firm OpenAI, alleging that the company endangered the public by developing an artificial intelligence model without the appropriate safeguards.

The lawsuit, announced by Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday, centres on an incident that unfolded in July, when one of OpenAI’s experimental models gained access to the internet.

It proceeded to launch a days-long cyberattack on the AI hosting platform Hugging Face.

In the California complaint, Bonta argues that the incident indicates that OpenAI pursues growth over guardrails, leading to potentially dangerous errors.

“The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritises growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents,” Bonta said in a statement.

The lawsuit is the first brought by a state in response to the July incident. It alleges that OpenAI violated California’s consumer protection laws and created a public nuisance through its actions.

The complaint, filed in a state court in San Francisco, calls for civil penalties against OpenAI and an injunction to bar it from engaging in actions that constitute “unfair competition”.

“The simple truth is that the attack was entirely foreseeable in light of OpenAI’s decision to test models it knew to be dangerous in a flawed and exploitable testing environment without proper oversight,” the complaint reads.

The Hugging Face incident became a catalyst for anxieties in the US about the explosive growth of the AI industry and the relatively light oversight it receives from the government.



President Donald Trump’s administration has largely opposed blanket regulations on the AI industry, warning that such rules could stifle the industry’s growth.

In December 2025, for instance, Trump issued an executive order attempting to limit the ability of individual states to pass laws that might govern AI development.

“United States AI companies must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulation. But excessive State regulation thwarts this imperative,” the order reads.

“My Administration must act with the Congress to ensure that there is a minimally burdensome national standard — not 50 discordant State ones.”

Polls, however, show that a majority of Americans want to see greater oversight of AI development and are wary that the technology could fuel economic and social disruptions.

The Associated Press and the NORC Center for Public Affairs Research, for instance, found in October that 64 percent of US adults believe AI is developing too rapidly. Roughly 81 percent said the technology should be kept under human control, rather than be left to operate independently.

Several high-profile resignations in the AI sector — notably that of Jacob Coxon in September — have also spurred concerns about the lack of oversight.

“They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives,” Coxon, formerly a researcher at the AI firm Anthropic, wrote in a social media post about his departure.

“Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources.”

In Monday’s lawsuit, California officials accuse companies like OpenAI of failing to “adequately secure and monitor” their AI tests. It also alleged that the company had obstructed state investigators when they attempted to look into incidents like the Hugging Face hacking.

“OpenAI thwarted the Attorney General’s efforts to investigate these incidents, including by refusing to provide detailed information about the full universe of incidents known to the company,” the lawsuit said.

OpenAI has responded to July’s incident by stating that it would reinforce its safety measures and acknowledging the need for greater transparency.

In September, it also published a framework for “tracking, investigating, and disclosing instances of model misalignment” to better inform lawmakers and the public.

World.title: Asian love ballads test Eurovision’s winning song formula.
World.content:
Fans gathering ahead of the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia finale on Saturday in Bangkok.

Simon Robinson, one of the fans who traveled to Bangkok for the Eurovision Song Contest on Saturday, said that his history with the competition is nearly as long as its seven-decade run.

He was eight years old when he first watched it with his family in Yorkshire, England, when Britain's Mary Hopkin finished in second place behind Ireland’s Dana.

“I really liked the concept of bringing Europe together after the war,” said Mr. Robinson, 63, who now lives in Melbourne, Australia. He described the contest’s annual broadcast as a social activity for his family and neighbors.

“Eurovision helped to create the European identity,” he added.

Other fans had their own motivations for traveling to see the contest’s first Asian edition.

Some are Europeans living in Asia, on the hunt for nostalgia, while others are Americans who were eager to experience their first Eurovision.

Lee Hudson, an American television executive based in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, said that he gets emotional when he talks about Eurovision, which he has watched since 2012.

“The only reason I know any music from European countries is because I heard them on Eurovision,” he said. “Eurovision Asia makes sense because the musical cultures are distinct.”

Mr. Hudson said he still listens to Loreen’s “Euphoria,” which won the competition for Sweden in 2012.

It was also the first Eurovision that Drew Andrea watched from his home in Sydney. A year later, he got a passport to fly to Sweden for the 2013 edition, and has attended every final since. Coming to Bangkok for Eurovision Asia was much more affordable, he said.

“Asia understands the brief — the kitschy costumes, the dance music,” he said.

His top picks among the Asian performers were the Philippines’ Carmelle and Vietnam’s Toc Tien. “I think they hit the nail on the head with the song, staging, costume and traditional elements,” he said.

Luca Cian, a professor of marketing at the University of Virginia who grew up in Italy, said that Eurovision built a global fan base by offering a shared cultural experience.

“Millions of people across Europe watch it at the same moment,” he said. “Families have watch parties with food and drinks. There are public discussions. Rituals create community.”

Carmen Chung, a British accountant, said she hijacked her family’s holiday in Bangkok to attend Eurovision Asia with her brother Garry Chung, a banker who lives in Hong Kong. “We were raised on Eurovision,” she said of their childhood in Yorkshire.

European acts, she said, tend to copy whatever style of music won the previous year. “This year, because there are no expectations, everyone has just done their own thing,” she said. She and her brother said they were rooting for Bangladesh’s Beatmosphere, a beatboxing group that will perform an a cappella love song.

Martin Green, the director of the Eurovision Song Contest, said that about half of the tickets for Saturday’s final were purchased by “super fans” from outside Asia. Organizers have kept the inaugural show modest, with 11 participating countries and a 5,000-seat venue.

Mr. Andrea said he didn’t mind the small scale.

“I’m O.K. with humble beginnings as long as it keeps growing every year,” he said.

World.title: Here’s the latest.
World.content:
Pinned

The Eurovision Song Contest crowned its first Asia champion in Bangkok on Saturday, in an event that tested whether a high-camp singing competition with an ardent fan base could appeal to audiences in a new market.

Carmelle of the Philippines was declared the winner of the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia, beating out artists and original songs from 10 other countries: Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia, Mongolia, Nepal, South Korea, Thailand and Vietnam. The show was live-streamed on YouTube and broadcast by television stations across the region.

Eurovision has been a fixture of the European cultural calendar since it began in 1956. Past winners include Sweden’s ABBA and the Canadian chanteuse Celine Dion, who represented Switzerland in 1988.

Asian artists have readily embraced the kitschy outfits and spectacular sets that are part of Eurovision tradition, with costumes that include traditional dress, as well as feathered capes and sequined corsets. Malaysia’s performer plans to enter the stage in a giant teardrop.

But the Eurovision format has not been tested in Asia. Fans and regional partners have expressed concern in recent weeks that budget constraints, production issues and weak audience demand could imperil the spinoff. Organizers say the contest could take time to build an audience.

“It would be profoundly arrogant to think that just because we have a heritage brand and a huge global audience for the European show, that we would walk in and demand it to be the same here,” said Martin Green, the European Broadcasting Union’s director of the Eurovision Song Contest. “Like any new thing, it needs to find its roots.”

Two previous attempts to take the competition to Asia were abandoned by the European Broadcasting Union, which owns Eurovision, and its partners in the region. A Eurovision spinoff in the United States, NBC’s American Song Contest, ran for one season in 2022.

The Asian edition kicking off on Saturday is far smaller than its European counterpart. Eurovision organizers said they were in talks with more countries to join future seasons. They include China, Japan and India, whose music industries have global reach.

“Bringing the world together through music is a fundamentally good idea,” Mr. Green said. “Europe shouldn’t keep it to itself.”

World.title: Here’s the latest.
World.content:
Pinned

The nationwide ground stop that brought all air travel to a halt across the country and stranded thousands of passengers has been canceled, according to the Federal Aviation Administration, though delays from the outage are expected to persist in the coming days.

The order on Friday halted nearly all departures and stranded thousands of passengers at airports across the country. Hundreds of flights were diverted to other airports and more were canceled, even as some internationally bound flights managed to secure permission to take off. Many passengers were taken off flights or told to go home. Chaos spread at airports as travelers sought answers from airline and airport employees.

Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, warned that it would take “some time” for air travel nationwide to recover from the ground stop. Speaking at a news conference on Friday night shortly after flight traffic had been restored, Mr. Duffy predicted that flight schedules would be fully back to normal by the time the Thanksgiving travel season begins.

“I believe that it’s going to take us some time to get back to capacity,” he said, adding: “We’re going to have some makeup to do.”

Mr. Duffy decried Congress, accusing lawmakers of dragging their feet when it came to fully funding upgrades he warned were vital to prevent similar failures from happening again.

“It’s going to continue to fail,” Mr. Duffy told reporters, adding: “How many times does this have to happen for Congress to give the money to fix it?”

Mr. Duffy said that the antiquated radar and telecoms systems that controllers rely on to transmit data and other information between facilities began to falter at 3:36 p.m. The aging system, which has undergone a number of upgrades, became overloaded, officials said.

Appearing alongside him, Markwayne Mullin, the secretary of homeland security, stressed that there was never any indication that the communications failures had been triggered by a cyberattack, but he added, “we are still looking, and we’re not going to rule it out.” He emphasized that lives were never in danger.

But the incident appeared to inject new fuel into Mr. Duffy’s now monthslong campaign to secure at least $30 billion in extra funding for air traffic control modernization.

Last year, Congress approved $12.5 billion to upgrade aging air traffic facilities and technology, funds Mr. Duffy has repeatedly referred to as a “down payment” when asking for tens of billions more. On Friday night, Mr. Duffy appeared to up the ante, telling reporters that he didn’t just want another $30 billion for the project, but another $50 billion. He argued that it should be delivered in emergency funding before the end of the year, after which control of Congress — and the budget — switches from Republicans to Democrats.

Some Democratic lawmakers have already raised questions about how efficiently and effectively the F.A.A. has spent the money they have been given thus far. But Mr. Duffy has long argued that his department cannot be expected to complete a meaningful overhaul of the nation’s air traffic control system without a massive influx of funding.

Friday’s nationwide ground stop was only the third that the F.A.A. has issued this century. It ranks as the second-longest, after the ground stop issued on Sept. 11, 2001, in the wake of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center in New York. There was a shorter one on Jan. 11, 2023, because of an outage in the F.A.A.’s system to alert pilots to safety issues.

More than 2 million people pass through airport security checkpoints on a typical day, according to Transportation Security Administration data. On Thursday, the agency screened nearly 2.5 million people. According to FlightRadar24, an aviation tracking site, there were more than 1,000 airborne aircraft bound for U.S. airports during the nationwide ground stop. According to the flight tracking app Flighty, there were more than 30,000 departures and arrivals scheduled for the remainder of the day.

It could take days for air travel to fully normalize after an event of this scale, said Vikrant Vaze, a Dartmouth professor specializing in commercial aviation logistics.

“It’s going to take a lot of gymnastics” to get every airline’s aircraft, passengers and crew members back in the correct positions, he said.

Here’s what else to know:

If your flight is canceled: You are entitled to a refund if your flight is canceled in the United States, regardless of the reason, or if a flight is significantly delayed or changed and you decide not to take it. Here are other travel tips that might be helpful. Read more ›

A busy travel month: The ground stop happened about two weeks before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest times of the year for air travel. On average, U.S. airlines are expected to fly about 2.7 million passengers each day over the holiday period, according to industry trade group Airlines for America.

Handling the chaos: Radio transmissions between air traffic controllers and pilots at major airports offered a peek at how they navigated the ground stoppage. Read more ›

The last ground stop: The last nationwide ground stop came in the early morning of Jan. 11, 2023, and lasted around 90 minutes. The disruption came after a system to alert pilots of real-time dangers went down. Read more ›

Christine Chung , Niraj Chokshi , Luke Broadwater , Dustin Volz , Lisa Lerer and Robert Chiarito contributed reporting.

World.title: Five EU countries announce migrant deportation centre in Rwanda
World.content:
Five EU countries will open a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda next year as part of a broader push to boost removals.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to open a "return hub" ready to accept transfers in 2027, the Dutch and Danish governments announced in statements.

The countries said the scheme would apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation, with the Dutch government adding it will provide an alternative if deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

Deportees will be able to either integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country, the nations said.

The scheme will apply to people who have exhausted their legal avenues to stay in the five nations - unlike a scrapped British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed. Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually junked by the incoming Labour government in 2024.

Downing Street has not ruled out the UK joining the scheme, saying they will watch it "with interest".

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez said the plan to open a centre in Rwanda had no "future or humanity", according to AFP news agency.

"I don't see any future or humanity in that. It's not the solution," Sanchez told the Spanish broadcaster Telecinco, AFP reported.

The five countries say the plan to send migrants abroad is in line with EU and international law, but human rights bodies say it could violate migrant rights.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of hubs outside of the bloc.

In a joint press conference in Vienna on Monday, Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker said the five countries wanted to relieve European asylum systems and stop traffickers arranging deadly trips across the Mediterranean.

In a written statement, the Dutch government said the five countries will "only return single men" as part of the first phase of the deal, adding that the focus for the Netherlands "will be on persons from countries of origin in the same region as Rwanda".

Once in Rwanda, people will be able to integrate into society, which means they will have the right of residence, as well as access to education, healthcare, the labour market and the legal system.

Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta said the country is commmited to working with European partners to provide a "safe, legal and dignified solution for migrants".

He added that they would also work on "correcting the global imbalance in economic opportunities", which he called a "key driver of irregular migration".

Ahead of the announcement, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency the hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants.

The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

With elections approaching in several EU nations, administrations have been under pressure to show they can control migration.

Concerns around security, struggling economies and disillusionment with governing parties have all had a major role in shaping attitudes towards people leaving their home countries.

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."

The independent EU Agency for Fundamental Rights argued any third country hosting a return hub should "respect fundamental rights", including that people should not be sent to a country where they face serious risk of persecution.

The agency added that unaccompanied children should not be sent to a return hub, which the Dutch government has confirmed will not take place.

According to the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, there were almost 110,000 irregular border crossings into the EU in the first 10 months of 2026, which represents a 29% decrease compared to the previous year.

In October, about 18,100 crossings were detected, which is about 6% less than October 2025 but 22% more than in September "largely because of a sharp rise in arrivals on the Western African route to the Canary Islands".

World.title: Houthi rebel advance in Yemen may further destabilise global economy
World.content:
The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden.

Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world.

Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula.

The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears.

Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.

In normal times, it accounts for around 12% of global trade, with anywhere between 70 to 150 ships a day making the transit.

But not any more. Although the Houthis say they are no threat to maritime traffic, they are currently at war with Saudi Arabia, making it extremely hazardous for the Saudis to send their oil tankers past the now rebel-controlled coast.

World.title: Nvidia dismisses 'Bring Jensen Back' campaign as Trump backs effort to reinstate ex CEO
World.content:
Nvidia has dismissed a campaign calling for Jensen Huang to be handed back his job as allies, including US President Donald Trump, backed the effort.

Trump said on Monday that he "would certainly not mind" if Huang was reinstated, adding to a list of supporters who are backing a "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

Fellow tech bosses, including SpaceX's Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, have also supported Huang's return.

But the BBC has been told the board of the AI chip giant is not interested in bringing him back after he resigned last week following revelations he had two affairs, including one that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

Meanwhile on Monday, the Trump administration said it will further restrict China's âaccess to AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

The reported affairs created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a central company in AI and the US battle against China for dominance. Since his departure, supporters have launched an online petition demanding his return.

Musk and Sweeny are among the more than 175,000 who have signed the open letter calling for the board to reinstate Huang while an ongoing internal probe is conducted.

The "Stand with Jensen" campaign claims to have been launched by a make up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters, all demanding the return of the former chief executive.

They expressed concerns the ex-Nvidia boss "was removed without meaningful due process".

President Trump gave his views on Huang's future on Monday, saying he "would certainly not mind" seeing the former boss given his job back.

"I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that," he told reporters as he left the White House.

The Trump administration on Monday also issued new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres, which allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train AI models.

The move came ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jingping this week.

The new rules will require companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips in an effort to cut down on them being illegally diverted to China.

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy. However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss was discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to the Financial Times, external, though Nvidia's board is not considering reappointing him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

President Trump has spoken in glowing terms about Huang since the scandal erupted, and also said he believed Huang when the former Nvidia boss told him he had "no idea she was a spy".

Trump's view is at odds with his Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

The scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed. China has denied that Alice Huang is a spy.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

World.title: Landmark Crimea bridge hit as Russia reports biggest Ukrainian drone attack of war
World.content:
Russia says it has recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, in which a landmark bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea sustained minor damage and several oil refineries were hit.

The Russian military intercepted and destroyed 2,049 drones and four Flamingo long-distance missiles over 24 hours, officials said. Around 600 flew towards the capital alone, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin added.

Kyiv, meanwhile, came under a record 17 air raid alerts in a single day. At least seven people were killed by Russian strikes and attacks on energy infrastructure caused blackouts for 50,000 people.

The intense strikes come days after US, Ukrainian and Russian envoys held talks aimed at ending the war.

The war in Ukraine began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that drones had struck the Crimean Bridge connecting Russia with the annexed peninsula, leading to traffic restrictions.

The structure - also known as Kerch Bridge - was built by Russia after it invaded and annexed the peninsula in 2014. It was inaugurated by Russian President Vladimir Putin to great fanfare in 2018 and is carefully protected with multiple layers of aerial and maritime defences.

Russian pro-war military commentators said on Telegram that rather than a direct attack, the bridge had suffered from the impact of drone warhead debris. Neither Ukraine's domestic security service nor its main military intelligence directorate has responded to a BBC request for comment.

Atesh, a partisan Ukrainian group operating inside Russian-held territory, said on social media that authorities in Crimea were "bracing for further strikes" on the Kerch Bridge and that they felt Moscow did not appreciate the seriousness of the situation.

Ukrainian drones also hit several energy facilities, including an oil refinery in Ilsky, in the southern Krasnodar region, where falling drone debris sparked a fire and injured six people, including children.

Last week, President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of carrying out a concerted operation against Ukraine's bridges in order to "divide Ukraine... and make life as difficult as possible for people" on both sides of the Dnipro River which cuts across the country.

Despite the high-level diplomacy and visits by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to both Putin and Zelensky, peace remains a distant prospect.

Moscow is uncompromising on its demands for Ukraine to cede territory and give up efforts to become a Nato member.

The Kremlin has now also started to talk again about the need to rethink Europe's "security architecture", often intended by Moscow to mean a scaled-down Nato presence in countries close to Russia.

The apparent willingness of the US to engage in this conversation has set off alarm bells among Ukraine's European partners, which are concerned their continent's security could be redrawn by Washington and Moscow without their involvement.

A team of six - Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and a representative of the EU institutions - will represent Europe in future talks with Russia, Ukraine and the US.

But the Kremlin continues to be dismissive of European input.

"We have also said more than once we need to understand... how much their position will help the peace process," said spokesman Dmitri Peskov.

EU representatives kept pushing for "unconditional support" for Ukraine and "enhanced pressure" on Russia, Peskov said, adding that "this sort of wording rather suggests their reluctance to facilitate the peace process".

World.title: When will we see Robert Pattinson as Bond in cinemas?
World.content:
Robert Pattinson has been announced as the next James Bond, becoming the seventh actor and first in more than 20 years to take up the mantle of Britain's famous spy.

The new Bond film is expected to go into production in 2027, before its reported release in 2028. No exact dates have been announced.

It will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for Prisoners, Arrival and the upcoming Dune 3, which also stars Pattinson.

World.title: Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed
World.content:
This article contains distressing details and references to suicide

A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.

Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Dr Barbara Sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of Epstein's autopsy, who ruled that Epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "I stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for Mr. Epstein." The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.

Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.

He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.

Freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by Mark Epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.

Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

He said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on Epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".

He said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide."

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General , externalthat Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.

World.title: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
World.content:
Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation.

The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.

Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges.

Five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan were strangled at the family home on 24 January 2023. The defence argues she had severe postpartum psychosis.

"I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing.

Prosecutors wanted a May trial date, but Judge William Sullivan decided on March instead. The judge is due to retire in June.

Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

The district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges. The BBC has contacted the district attorney's office for comment.

World.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 17 dead
World.content:
South African police are investigating the murders of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night.

Eight men were fatally shot in a minibus in KwaZulu-Natal province. Police declared them dead when they arrived at the scene. Hours later, nine people were found shot dead inside a shack in western Pretoria.

Police say the two incidents are unrelated. The motive for the shootings has not yet been established.

South Africa is struggling to contain violent crime, including gang-related killings. The country has one of the world's highest murder rates.

Police say they responded to reports of a shooting â outside Pietermaritzburg town in KwaZulu-Natal and found a white seven-seater vehicle riddled with bullet holes.

Inside were eight men with multiple gunshot wounds.

"It has not been established how the incident happened, and police are collecting pieces of evidence to determine the possible motive of the killings and the identity of the suspects," police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said.

The police have launched a manhunt for the suspects.

In a separate shooting in the Jeffsville informal settlement in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, police found the bodies of six men and three women.

They are believed to have been killed inside a four-room shack between 22:00 and 23:00 on Sunday. The bodies were scattered across the rooms, with several spent cartridges discovered outside the shack.

Community members initially mistook the gunshots for thunder and lightning.

"The provincial commissioner of police in Gauteng [province, which includes Pretoria] has mobilized the necessary resources, including the crime intelligence and the deputy provincial commissioner tracking team to search for the suspect," police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.

It's not the first mass shooting in the area. In January, five men were shot dead outside a local shop in broad daylight.

Illegal firearms are widespread in South Africa, where gun violence remains a persistent problem, increasingly involving mass shootings.

In September, 28 people were killed in two separate cases.

Eighteen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar near Johannesburg and opened fire on 25 September. Fourteen others were injured.

In a separate shooting the following day, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town. A further 11 were injured.

Much of the violence has been linked to turf wars between gangs involved in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa described organised crime as "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year, the military was deployed alongside police to five provinces with the highest murder rates, including Gauteng, in an effort to tackle armed violence.

According to the latest police statistics, 5,427 people were murdered nationwide between April and June 2026, an average of about 60 killings a day. This was a 6% decline compared with the same period a year earlier.

Additional reporting by Christian Parkinson in Johannesburg

World.title: Mbah commissions Premium Trust Bank branch in Enugu, says security, infrastructure investments attracting investors
World.content:
Governor Peter Mbah of Enugu State, on Monday, unveiled the first branch of Premium Trust Bank in the state, describing the development as a demonstration of growing private-sector confidence in the state’s economy and investment prospects.

Mbah reiterated his administration’s determination to restore Enugu’s historic position as a major economic hub through deliberate investments, private-sector partnerships and policies designed to accelerate economic growth.

This was even as the bank’s Group Managing and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Emmanuel Efe Emefienim commended Mbah for improved business environment and reaffirmed the bank’s commitment expanding its national footprint and supporting businesses, small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs) and financial inclusion.

Mbah recalled that Enugu’s economic significance predated Nigeria’s amalgamation, noting that the discovery of coal in 1909 established the city as an important commercial and administrative centre.

He said his administration was growing the state’s economy in line with its development blueprint anchored on growing the state’s economy from $4.4 billion to $30 billion within eight years, eliminating poverty and making Enugu a preferred destination for living, working, business and tourism.

He emphasised that the administration’s strategy was to create an enabling environment for private capital to drive economic expansion, stressing that government alone could not deliver the desired level of growth.

The governor identified security as one of the major considerations for investors,recalling that the administration inherited security challenges, including the disruption of economic activities associated with the Monday sit-at-home order.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the interventions have helped restore confidence and reduce the risks associated with doing business in Enugu.

The governor further disclosed plans to establish a 660-megawatt coal-fired powerplant, expressing optimism that reliable and affordable electricity would stimulate industrialisation and create opportunities across the state’s economic value chain.

He also cited the expansion of Enugu’s air connectivity, including international routes, as part of efforts to improve access to global markets and attract investment.

Congratulating the bank’s management, disclosed that Premium Trust Bank was already a partner of the state government and the headline sponsor of the National Sports Festival scheduled to hold in Enugu. He noted that the bank’s expansion into Enugu was consistent with the administration’s development philosophy of government-enabled, private-sector-driven growth.

The governor expressed optimism that the bank would establish additional branches in the state, potentially expanding its presence to 10 branches as economic activities and investment opportunities increase.

Earlier, Emefienim said the bank’s decision to establish a presence in Enugu was informed by confidence in the state, its people and its economic future.

He disclosed that the Enugu branch was the bank’s fourth branch opening in November, bringing its nationwide network to 38, with plans to establish four additional branches before the end of the year.

According to him, the expansion reflects the bank’s commitment to bringing financial services closer to individuals, entrepreneurs, SMEs and corporate organisations across the country.

“Our decision to establish a presence here is a strong belief in this state, its people and its future.

“More importantly, it is a demonstration of our readiness to partner with the state government, individuals, entrepreneurs, SMEs, corporates and the good people of Enugu in building a stronger and more prosperous economy,” he said.

The bank’s managing director commended the Mbah administration for its investment infrastructure, security, technology, ease of doing business and investment promotion, noting that the initiatives were helping to create an environment conducive to enterprise and investment.

He said that while the government had the responsibility of providing an enabling environment, financial institutions and private businesses also had critical roles to play the provision of capital, innovation and financial solutions.

Describing the new branch as more than an additional banking facility, Emefienim said it would serve as a platform for expanding financial inclusion and supporting individuals and businesses in achieving their financial goals.

He identified entrepreneurs seeking to expand their businesses, traders requiring efficient payment solutions, professionals planning their financial future,students pursuing education and families working towards financial security as some of the categories the bank intended to serve.

On support for SMEs, he described the sector as a major driver of economic growth and job creation, stressing that businesses required financial partners capable of understanding their needs and providing solutions to support their expansion.

He highlighted the bank’s Silver Premium Business Account, designed to help businesses manage operating costs, improve efficiency and access collections,digital payment solutions and other banking services.

Emefienim also introduced Blaze, the bank’s lifestyle and digital financial platform,which he said was designed to simplify transactions, improve banking convenience and expand access to financial services.

Reaffirming the bank’s commitment to the state, he said Premium Trust Bank was prepared to build a long-term relationship with Enugu and contribute to the growth of businesses and the wider economy.

“We are here for the long term. We are here to support enterprises. We are here to create opportunities. We are here to help businesses grow and help individuals achieve their financial goals,” he said.

He attributed the bank’s growing national presence to its emphasis on sound corporate governance, innovation, service excellence and prudent management.

World.title: IGP visits Otti, lauds Abia govt’s support for Nigeria police
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has lauded the Abia State Government’s support for the Nigeria Police Force.

Mr Disu stated this on Saturday when he and his wife visited Governor Alex Otti of Abia State at the governor’s country home in Nvosi, Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area.

Governor Otti disclosed this in a statement he issued on Sunday.

The police chief was in Abia to attend the traditional marriage ceremony of his orderly, Victor Nnah Sunday, held in Amangwu, Abaki-Ndoki, Ukwa East.

“I appreciate the IGP’s kind words about our administration’s support for the Nigeria Police Force in Abia State and his commitment to strengthening security and protecting lives and property,” Mr Otti said in the statement.

“I thanked him for the visit and commended the professionalism and responsiveness of the Police, particularly their swift interventions whenever the State called on them.

“I also congratulated the former Commissioner of Police in Abia on his elevation to the rank of Assistant Inspector-General of Police, acknowledging his contributions to security in the State.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The governor said his conversation with the police chief also touched on the importance of national unity and inclusiveness.

“I commended the IGP for building relationships across ethnic and geographical boundaries, emphasising that we must look beyond our differences and recognise that we are one people with a shared destiny.

“I appreciate the IGP’s visit and look forward to sustained collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force in our collective commitment to a safer and more secure Abia State,” Mr Otti added.

World.title: Reps panel gives NSCDC boss 24 hours to explain alleged abuse by mining marshals
World.content:
The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has directed the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) to appear before it within 24 hours to answer allegations of misconduct, extortion and unlawful arrests involving the mining marshals.

The committee’s directive followed complaints by mining operators and the family of a deceased NSCDC officer, who accused personnel of the special security unit of abuse of power, financial impropriety, intimidation and human rights violations.

The lawmakers issued the ultimatum on Monday during an investigative hearing on the operations, funding and activities of the mining marshals, following a motion moved by Ali Amburura (ADC, Sokoto).

The chairman of the committee, Gaza Gbefwi (LP, Nasarawa), said the investigation would examine allegations of harassment and unlawful detention of licensed mining operators, a suspected ₦2 billion transaction linked to the bank account of a former state commander, and possible compromise among personnel deployed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The lawmakers, according to him, will also investigate the unit’s vehicle procurement and funding sources.

Mr Gbefwi said the committee was acting within its constitutional oversight powers under “Sections 88 and 89 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, to establish the legal status of the mining marshals, their funding arrangements and whether their operations complied with the law.”

The mining marshals were established in March 2024 with more than 2,200 personnel inaugurated to curb illegal mining, stop revenue losses, and secure Nigeria’s solid minerals sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Created through a joint effort between the Federal Ministry of Solid Minerals Development and the Ministry of Interior, the unit serves as a specialised security force under the NSCDC to enforce mining laws and protect national assets.

However, the committee chairman said the government’s responsibility to protect mineral resources did not give security personnel the authority to disregard the law or violate citizens’ fundamental rights.

Family seeks justice over officer’s death

One of the major issues presented at the hearing was the death of Deputy Superintendent Agada Agada, an NSCDC officer attached to the mining marshals, who was allegedly killed by fellow officers while on duty at a mining site.

Representing the deceased officer’s family, their lawyer, Obasi-Obi Nwabueze, accused the NSCDC of giving conflicting explanations about the circumstances surrounding his death.

Mr Nwabueze said medical affidavits obtained from doctors who attended to the officer contradicted the account that he died following an attack by bandits.

According to him, Mr Agada “sustained a gunshot wound to the right side of his chest and was taken to two medical facilities before being transferred to the Federal Medical Centre, Keffi, where he eventually died.”

The lawyer said the family obtained the medical accounts after petitioning the Nigeria Police Force, adding that affidavits from the medical personnel who treated the officer were available to support their claims.

He further alleged that two NSCDC officers were indicted over the incident, while three officers were arrested during the police investigation.

However, he claimed that the investigation was subsequently obstructed after the police officer handling the case was allegedly arrested and the case file withdrawn.

Mr Nwabueze urged the committee to intervene to ensure that the police conclude their investigation and that anyone found responsible for the officer’s death is prosecuted.

He also requested protection for the deceased’s relatives and other witnesses, alleging that some had received threats and faced intimidation.

Mr Agada, he said, left behind a widow and two children, aged ten and seven.

Responding, Mr Gbefwi expressed sympathy to the family and assured them that their petition would be forwarded to the relevant authorities for appropriate action.

He also requested an executive summary of their submissions to help the committee document the allegations and determine the necessary steps.

Mining companies allege unlawful arrests, extortion

The committee also heard complaints from licensed mining operators, who accused the Mining Marshals of using their enforcement powers to intimidate businesses and detain workers without lawful justification.

Rachel Ogbonna, director of Communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, told the lawmakers that the company’s quarry had remained sealed for more than a year despite its possession of what she described as valid mining licences and operational documents.

She alleged that 12 employees of the company were arrested and taken to an NSCDC detention facility along Airport Road.

According to her, the company’s chairman and director were subsequently detained after visiting the facility with relevant documents to establish why their workers had been arrested and secure their release.

Ms Ogbonna further alleged that the detainees were denied access to their lawyers and that the company’s director was prevented from receiving essential medication while in custody.

She described the alleged actions as violations of fundamental rights, arguing that the Mining Marshals’ responsibility to enforce mining regulations and combat illegal activities did not place them above the law.

She asked the committee to investigate the unit’s financial management, particularly its budgetary allocations, special intervention funds and expenditure on publications, publicity materials and other operational activities.

In a separate complaint, a security operative, Odey Polycarp, accused the mining marshals, allegedly led by Onoja Attah, of arresting and detaining members of his workforce for several days while demanding ₦100 million for their release.

Mr Polycarp told the lawmakers that the workers were arrested in a residential neighbourhood where no mining or quarrying activities were taking place.

He questioned the justification for their arrest and alleged that they were repeatedly beaten during detention, leaving them traumatised and fearful for their safety.

He urged the committee to investigate the alleged demand for money, the circumstances surrounding the arrests and the treatment of the detainees.

He also called for sanctions against any personnel found responsible for extortion, unlawful detention or physical abuse.

The allegations presented at the hearing have placed the operations of the mining marshals under scrutiny, particularly their treatment of licensed operators, the exercise of their enforcement powers and the mechanisms for holding personnel accountable.

The committee is expected to hear from the NSCDC leadership and other relevant authorities as it examines the complaints and investigates the unit’s financial and operational framework.

World.title: Visually impaired protest exclusion from government programmes
World.content:
Members of the Association of Technology Inclined Visually Impaired Persons of Nigeria(ATIVIPN), Ondo State chapter, have protected alleged bias and exclusion from government programmes and benefits.

During a peaceful march on Monday at the Ministry of Women Affairs in Akure, the stare capital, the group demanded official recognition and inclusion in government programmes.

The visually impaired persons also accused the state Ministry of Women Affairs of neglecting their association despite submitting relevant registration documents and several letters seeking recognition.

They also alleged that only the Nigeria Association of the Blind (NAB) was recognised by the state government, leaving other visually impaired persons outside its intervention programmes and benefits.

Speaking during the protest, the state Chairman of the association, Omiyale Babatunde, said members had been excluded from government interventions since the beginning of the year.

Mr Babatunde said the association had submitted its Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) certificate and other registration documents but accused the ministry of failing to act on them.

He said some members were educated but remained unemployed and appealed to the state government to provide opportunities for them to contribute to society.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We have to be included. We need jobs. Some of us are educated, we need something doing, we need palliatives,” he said.

Mr Babatunde, who disclosed that he had been a member of the NAB since 2018 before leaving the association, alleged that its leadership had failed to address the concerns of visually impaired persons in rural and urban communities.

Also speaking, the Youth Leader of the association, Bello Yusuf, said the group was demanding recognition as an independent association and inclusion in government activities for persons with disabilities.

Mr Yusuf said the association was established in April 2026 following disagreements with the NAB, which he accused of bias, alleged diversion of palliatives and failure to cater for visually impaired persons at the grassroots.

“We need inclusion and recognition. That is our main point here. We are no more part of NAB because of the bias they actually bear, the cheating and diversion of palliatives,” he said.

He explained that the association had submitted its registration documents and other necessary papers to the ministry but had yet to receive official recognition.

He said the group had written several letters to the ministry and informed it of its intention to protest before deciding to stage Monday’s demonstration.

Responding to the protesters, the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Women Affairs, Kolawole Kayode, assured them that their complaints would be addressed within seven days.

Mr Kayode, who acknowledged receiving two letters from the association, appealed to the protesters not to lose confidence in the ministry, promising that its executives would receive a positive response before the expiration of the ultimatum.

“We are working on it. I want to assure you that before the end of the seven days of the ultimatum you gave us to address your issue of inclusion, your executives will definitely hear from us,” he said.

However, Mr Yusuf warned that the association would return for another mass protest if the government failed to address its demands within the seven-day period.

He said the group would intensify its peaceful demonstration and block access to government offices to press home its demands.

World.title: Uyo Book Club plans colloquium on Attah’s 88th birthday
World.content:
A literary club in Akwa Ibom State, the Uyo Book Club will hold a colloquium on Friday to honour former Governor Victor Attah of Akwa Ibom as part of activities marking his 88th birthday.

The event, scheduled for 11 a.m., will take place at the Watbridge Hotels and Suites, Uyo, with discussions focusing on Mr Attah’s contributions to the development of the aviation sector in Akwa Ibom.

The theme of the colloquium is “Attah’s Vision in the Aviation Sector”.

Udeme Nana, a communication scholar, former head of the Department of Mass Communication at the Akwa Ibom State Polytechnic, Ikot Osurua, and founder of Uyo Book Club, announced this in a statement.

Mr Nana, who served as Mr Attah’s spokesperson from 1999 to 2007, said the event would provide an opportunity to examine the former governor’s vision for the state’s aviation sector and its lasting impact.

Mr Attah served as governor of the oil-rich Akwa Ibom State from 1999 to 2007.

Often referred to as the father of modern Akwa Ibom, Mr Attah conceived the Akwa Ibom airport project and commenced its construction before leaving office in 2007.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Successive administrations in the state completed the project and continued to upgrade the airport, building on the foundation laid by Mr Attah.

The airport, named after Mr Attah, has undergone significant expansion; it now boasts a terminal building described as one of the best in the country and a Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) facility.

Aviation vision

Explaining the choice of theme, Mr Nana said the airport project represented a significant development vision whose benefits extended beyond Akwa Ibom.

“The airport project was a game-changing vision which has served Akwa Ibom, Nigerians and travellers from other countries very well,” Mr Nana said.

He said experts in the aviation industry and other stakeholders who contributed to the project’s realisation have been invited to share their experiences and perspectives at the colloquium.

Those expected to speak include Mfon Udom, chairman of the Board of Directors of Ibom Air; Umana Okon Umana, former Minister of Niger Delta Affairs; Ita Awak, former director of Airworthiness Standards at the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority; and Augustine Okon, former chief executive officer of the defunct ADC Airline.

The speakers are expected to discuss the airport project’s conception, development, and significance, as well as the contributions of those involved in bringing the vision to life.

Promoting reading culture

Beyond the annual birthday colloquium, Uyo Book Club has become a platform for promoting reading, literary discussions, and intellectual engagement in Akwa Ibom State.

Established by Mr Nana as a community service initiative, the club seeks to reawaken interest in reading and encourage a culture of intellectual engagement in the state and beyond.

Since its formation, the organisation has inspired the establishment of book clubs in other cities, schools and communities across Akwa Ibom.

The club also provided a platform for Uyo to be recognised as Nigeria’s first Book Club City in 2021 and 2022.

Through its monthly in-person reading sessions, book-themed events, and virtual engagements, the organisation has built a growing community of readers, writers, students, and scholars.

According to the statement, the club has an active community of more than 7,000 members and reaches at least five million people annually.

It has also hosted and participated in more than 1,000 reading and book-related events, including its popular monthly reading sessions, which bring book enthusiasts together to discuss literary works and exchange ideas.

Previous tributes to literary icons

The club has previously organised colloquia to celebrate notable Nigerian literary figures, including Ken Saro-Wiwa, John Pepper Clark, Wole Soyinka, Chinua Achebe, Ray Ekpu and Christopher Okigbo.

The annual events form part of its efforts to celebrate influential personalities whose contributions to literature, journalism, scholarship and national development deserve recognition.

Mr Nana, a poet, is also credited with inventing the word ‘Digidiot’, which has been assessed for possible inclusion in the Collins English Language Dictionary.

Mr Nana said Friday’s colloquium would be free and open to the public.

The event is expected to bring together aviation professionals, public officials, scholars, writers, students, and other stakeholders to reflect on Mr Attah’s legacy, particularly his vision for developing aviation infrastructure in Akwa Ibom State.

World.title: Oborevwori presents ₦1.23 trillion appropriation bill, earmarks ₦320 billion for roads
World.content:
Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State on Monday presented a ₦1.23 trillion 2027 Appropriation Bill before the State House of Assembly, earmarking 65 per cent for capital expenditure, including ₦320 billion for road infrastructure.

Presenting the bill to the state assembly during plenary in Asaba, Mr Oborevwori said the budget was tagged “Budget of Sustained Prosperity and Enhanced Growth”.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the proposal comprised ₦806.8 billion for capital expenditure and ₦430 billion for recurrent expenditure.

The governor also said the proposed budget represented a 28.5 per cent reduction from the N1.729 trillion approved for the 2026 fiscal year.

According to him, the budget will prioritise completing ongoing civil and industrial projects, launching new high-impact programmes, and consolidating development achievements from the past three years.

He said infrastructure development, economic growth, and improved public service delivery remained central to his administration’s priorities.

He also said the two ministries of works would receive ₦320 billion for road infrastructure, while N50 billion and ₦74 billion were allocated to the health and education sectors, respectively.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He noted that government would also prioritise electricity reforms, agriculture, youth empowerment and social intervention programmes to improve residents’ living conditions.

“My administration remains committed to inclusive development, particularly addressing the needs of vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, irrespective of ethnicity, gender or social background.

“Infrastructure like roads, bridges and flyovers are also critical to my administration as they are drivers of economic development, community integration and improved access to markets,” he said.

The governor added that functional road networks were essential for connecting rural communities to urban centres, facilitating transportation and expanding economic opportunities.

“Without roads, there are no transport routes. Roads connect people, communities and markets,” he said.

According to him, feedback from town hall meetings and community engagements has identified road infrastructure as a major priority among residents consistently.

He said that improved connectivity would facilitate the movement of agricultural produce, reduce transportation difficulties and stimulate commercial activities across rural and urban communities.

Mr Oborevwori emphasised that his administration would intensify efforts to complete ongoing infrastructure projects while commencing new ones in the 2027 fiscal year.

Revenue generation

On revenue generation, Mr Oborevwori identified statutory allocations, internally generated revenue, mineral resources, Value Added Tax, capital receipts and proceeds from approved asset sales as major sources of funding.

He added that the budget was anchored on realistic revenue expectations, prudent financial management, and effective implementation of priority projects.

He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to consolidating previous achievements, expanding economic opportunities and ensuring that development benefits reached communities across Delta.

Speaker’s remark

Responding, the Speaker of the House, Dennis Guwor, assured the governor that the assembly would give the proposed budget thorough, objective and timely consideration.

Mr Guwor said the consideration would be guided by the approved 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework and Fiscal Strategy Paper, with emphasis on prudent resource allocation, accountability and projects that would positively impact residents.

He commended the governor’s performance in implementing the 2026 budget, particularly in road infrastructure, healthcare, education, social welfare and human capital development.

The speaker also praised the governor’s commitment to workers’ welfare, particularly his assent to the 13th Month Salary Law, describing it as a landmark initiative.

World.title: 2027: Bauchi NDC governorship candidate defects to APC
World.content:
The Bauchi State governorship candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Ibrahim Kashim, has defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC).

Mr Kashim’s defection followed his resignation on 16 October from the NDC.

He is listed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as the NDC’s flagbearer for the 2027 general election in Bauchi State.

Mr Kashim, a former Secretary to the Bauchi State Government (SSG) under Governor Bala Mohammed, formally announced his defection on Monday at the APC state secretariat in Bauchi.

He stated that his decision was driven by the need to align Bauchi State with the ruling party at the federal level to attract development and influence national policies.

According to him, the APC’s political structure, national reach, and institutional capacity make it a far stronger platform for advancing the state’s interests.

“The APC is currently the governing party at the federal level and has an overwhelming presence across Northern Nigeria. It is also the party with the political structure, national reach, and institutional capacity to provide a viable platform for the political and developmental aspirations we seek for Bauchi,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He argued that remaining outside the ruling party could limit Bauchi’s access to federal projects, investments, policy influence, and representation in the corridors of power.

“The question is not simply which party can put forward a candidate. The question is which party has the organisational strength, national reach, political influence, and institutional capacity to advance Bauchi’s interests. I am convinced that the APC offers the stronger platform,” he added.

Addressing his followers on Monday, Mr Kashim urged his supporters, political associates, and other stakeholders to join him in the APC, noting that his political ambition has always been anchored on improving governance and accelerating development in the state.

He listed youth employment, women’s empowerment, improved agricultural productivity, quality education, and stronger healthcare delivery among his core priorities.

Maintaining that his defection was not about partisan triumph, he called on Bauchi residents to back his decision so the state is not left behind in accessing federal opportunities.

“Our ultimate objective is not the triumph of one political party over another. It is the triumph of good governance over poor governance, development over stagnation, opportunity over deprivation, and hope over despair,” Mr Kashim said.

“I have chosen strategic engagement over political isolation. I have chosen a broader national platform over limited political reach. Above all, I have chosen what I sincerely believe offers Bauchi State a better opportunity for development and prosperity”, he stated.

World.title: 2027: Speaker cautions against intimidation as thuggery increases
World.content:
The Speaker of the House of Representatives, Abbas Tajudeen, has warned political parties and their supporters against intimidation and attacks on opponents as Nigeria approaches the 2027 general elections.

Mr Tajudeen urged political actors to engage one another constructively through ideas, policies, and evidence rather than resorting to insults, intimidation, and violence while campaigning for votes.

He made the call in his keynote address as a special guest of honour at the formal opening of the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on Monday. The speaker, who was represented by the House Leader, Julius Ihonvbere, spoke on the topic, “Responsible Communication and Parliamentary Democracy in the Digital Age.”

Mr Tajudeen said Nigeria’s democracy provides constitutional space for disagreement, representation, and peaceful political competition, urging political actors to avoid actions that could undermine the democratic process.

“Democracy remains a work in progress, facing challenges of institutional capacity, electoral confidence, public accountability, and political intolerance. Yet, its resilience lies in the constitutional space it provides for disagreement, representation, persuasion, and peaceful political competition.

“Democracy cannot thrive on institutions alone. It also depends on the quality of public discourse. Citizens need reliable information to make informed choices. Political actors must engage one another through ideas, policies, and evidence rather than insults, intimidation, and deliberate falsehoods,” he said.

The speaker also called for press freedom, urging that the media be allowed to scrutinise public officials without fear, saying this would promote transparency and strengthen Nigeria’s democracy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The media must be free to scrutinise those in authority while upholding professional standards. Public institutions, in turn, must recognise that transparency and accountability are obligations inherent in democratic governance,” he stated.

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cleared 18 candidates for the presidential election scheduled for 16 January 2027.
