The commission also cleared governorship candidates in 28 of the 36 states where governorship elections will be held on 6 February 2027. It has equally approved candidates for the National Assembly and State Houses of Assembly elections.

In line with its timetable and schedule of activities for the 2027 elections, INEC directed candidates to commence campaigns.

While presidential and National Assembly candidates began their campaigns on 19 August, governorship and State Houses of Assembly candidates commenced theirs a month later.

However, since the campaigns began, the country has witnessed a growing number of violent attacks on campaign rallies, town hall meetings and other political gatherings organised by parties seeking the mandate of voters.

Political activities across the country have increasingly been accompanied by reports of violence, intimidation and threats as the elections approach.

Campaign activities involving presidential candidates and opposition parties have faced security challenges in different parts of the country, including attacks on convoys, disruptions of political gatherings and confrontations involving party supporters.

In some instances, presidential candidates have alleged that their lives or those of their supporters were endangered. In others, political gatherings have been disrupted, vehicles damaged and participants injured or killed.

PREMIUM TIMES has documented a series of reported incidents of political violence, particularly those involving presidential candidates and opposition parties, since campaigns officially began in August, as well as their implications for the 2027 general elections.

The National Peace Committee, chaired by former Head of State Abdulsalami Abubakar, recently reported 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory during a monitoring period from 19 August to 27 October 2026.

The report identified political violence and thuggery as the largest category of violations, accounting for 33 incidents.

Separately, the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data (ACLED) project, an organisation that monitors political violence and conflict, reported more than 30 attacks targeting political campaigns, candidates, supporters, convoys and gatherings since the presidential and National Assembly campaigns began on 19 August.

According to ACLED, the incidents resulted in more than 10 deaths and several injuries.

Lawmaker calls for regulation of AI

Meanwhile, Osita Izunaso (APC, Imo West) has called for regulating artificial intelligence (AI) to prevent the spread of misinformation.

Mr Izunaso, who chaired the occasion, said he supported AI innovation but argued that the technology needed to be regulated to prevent its potential misuse.

“AI is a major issue right now, and globally, AI is not regulated in most climes, just like when new media started. Most jurisdictions did not find it necessary to regulate new media until now, when we say we cannot allow our children access to all manner of social media platforms. But we started late.

“As a parliamentarian, I’m also of the opinion that AI must be regulated before AI destroys the world. Now, when you see AI images, they look so real that sometimes you might not be able to discover which is AI and which is real.

“Don’t get me wrong, AI is good, but it has to be regulated before the goodness of AI becomes the calamity of the world,” he said.

World.title: Waste Crisis: Lagos trains sanitation workers on safety
World.content:
Gov Sanwo-Olu

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to improving the capacity, efficiency and professionalism of sanitation workers as part of efforts to address the state’s waste management challenges and ensure a cleaner environment.

The government gave the assurance on Monday at a capacity-building workshop for selected sanitation workers held in Alausa, Ikeja.

The Permanent Secretary, Office of Environmental Services, Omobolaji Gaji, represented by the Director of Sanitation Services, Dr Hassan Sanuth, said the workshop was designed to equip participants with the knowledge, practical skills and safety measures required to improve sanitation operations.

He said the initiative was also aimed at promoting a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable Lagos.

Gaji described sanitation workers as indispensable partners in the state’s efforts to maintain a clean and liveable environment, noting that their daily responsibilities, including street sweeping, drainage clearing and waste collection, were critical to protecting public health and preventing flooding.

He commended the workers for their dedication, observing that many of them commence their duties early in the morning, long before most residents begin their daily activities.

According to him, their contributions remain essential to maintaining environmental orderliness and ensuring that Lagos remains a city residents can be proud of.

The Permanent Secretary explained that the selected workers were identified in recognition of their commitment and dedication to duty, adding that the training represented a deliberate government investment in improving their welfare, competence and productivity.

He said participants would be exposed to safer working practices, the appropriate use of personal protective equipment, modern waste-handling techniques and improved approaches to sanitation service delivery.

Gaji added that the workshop would provide an opportunity for the workers to exchange experiences, discuss challenges encountered in the field and learn from one another.

He urged participants to actively engage with facilitators, ask questions and contribute ideas that could enhance their professional capacity and performance.

“This capacity-building programme underscores the Lagos State Government’s commitment to developing a more skilled, safety-conscious and efficient sanitation workforce capable of responding effectively to the environmental challenges of a rapidly growing metropolis,” he said.

He also appreciated the facilitators, partners and stakeholders whose expertise and support contributed to the programme, urging continued collaboration to strengthen environmental sanitation and public health in the state.

Gaji said a clean and sustainable Lagos required collective responsibility, stressing that sanitation workers remained at the centre of the state’s environmental management efforts.

He assured the workers that their contributions were valued, their dignity respected and their professional development remained important to the government.

In a lecture titled, “Safety Culture: A Need to Prevent Occupational Accidents,” the guest lecturer, Mr Adeyinka Adebiyi, urged sanitation workers to prioritise workplace safety in the discharge of their daily responsibilities.

Adebiyi noted that their duties exposed them to various occupational hazards capable of causing injuries, illnesses and, in severe cases, loss of lives.

He emphasised the need for strict compliance with safety procedures, proper use of personal protective equipment, effective risk assessment and responsible handling of waste materials.

He also urged the workers to remain vigilant, avoid unsafe practices and promptly report potential hazards to prevent avoidable accidents and health complications.

The capacity-building initiative is expected to improve sanitation service delivery, promote safer working conditions and contribute to a cleaner environment across Lagos State.

World.title: Obi, Kwankwaso have God’s grace to dislodge Tinubu — Babachir Lawal
World.content:
Babachir Lawal

A chieftain of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Babachir Lawal, has said Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Kwankwaso, his running mate, have God’s backing to defeat President Bola Tinubu in 2027.



Lawal, a former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, who made the declaration during an appearance on Arise Television late Sunday, cited the “widespread support” Obi and Kwankwaso enjoyed as a pointer to God’s grace upon their lives.

He said: “I have told everybody that talks to me that both Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso have the grace of God upon their lives, which makes people like them.



“The population likes them. They just show up in the market. They don’t hire people to come to their rallies. People just turn out at their own expense.”



He said his experience in politics had enabled him to recognise signs that could favour the opposition alliance, adding that he previously occupied a similar position during the Muhammadu Buhari administration.



“It’s not the first time I am in the position I am in now in politics. I have been in this position during Buhari’s time. Even this your president, I drove his system up to the primaries.

“So I am a very skilled and experienced person in the game. I can see the signs and we know the loopholes. And we are working on the loopholes,’’ he said.

Lawal expressed confidence that the NDC would defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC.

, saying the party had established structures and systems to achieve its objective.

“We have an inside chance of toppling this government. We are inside and we know we will beat this government.

“We know they are gone. We have put up structures and systems. I am 100 per cent confident,’’ he said.

Lawal added that the responsibility of the party’s technical team was to convert the popularity of its presidential candidates into electoral success by ensuring that votes were protected and counted.

“This grace that God has bestowed upon them, it’s our duty, the technical people, to harmonise and crystallise this thing into delivering it at the polling station and protecting the votes and ensuring it’s counted,” he said.

Lawal dismissed concerns over recent departure of Yunusa Tanko, former national coordinator of the Obidient Movement; Nana Kazaure, Doyin Okupe, and the former NDC’s deputy national publicity secretary, from Obi’s camp, saying politicians were free to leave parties when their expectations were not met.

He compared the development with the exit of some politicians from Tinubu’s inner circle, including Kashim Imam and Rauf Aregbesola.

“I was with Bola Tinubu, but I left. I can remember Kashim Imam; he has also left. I remember Rauf Aregbesola, who was also with Bola Tinubu. But he has left. These are big politicians. But they left Bola Tinubu.

“Leaving a political party is only natural. Nigeria is like a big company with many political parties. And people come in there with their own different ideas about what they can get out of it and what they can put into it,’’ the former SGF said.

He said while the majority of Nigerians joined politics to get something out of it, others participate to contribute to the system.

Lawal stated: “If you are the getting-out type and you go but don’t get anything, it’s only fair you move. That is life. You cannot be static.

“Moreover, the Obidient system is not about money. And people have families to feed, bills to pay. And if they join the Obidient Movement hoping to get the resources to settle these, they will be disappointed. So, it’s only fair. They have their reasons for leaving,”

Recounting his experience while serving as SGF, Lawal said some politicians tended to exaggerate their contributions to political campaigns.

World.title: Gombe approves N97bn road projects, N3.8bn emergency vehicles
World.content:
…SEC endorses 2027–2029 expenditure framework, updates social protection policy

..Government targets December resumption of Kolmani oil exploration

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe

GOMBE — The Gombe State Executive Council (SEC), presided over by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has approved seven road projects valued at billions of naira, covering approximately 97 kilometres across four local government areas of the state.

The council also approved the procurement of 40 emergency response and public utility vehicles, comprising 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers, at a combined cost of about N3.8 billion.

Other major decisions taken at the council meeting on Monday included the approval of the 2027–2029 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF), an updated Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 and measures to position the state to benefit from the anticipated resumption of oil exploration in the Kolmani area in December.

Briefing journalists after the meeting, the Commissioner for Information and Culture, Moses Kyari Bolda, said the decisions reflected the administration’s commitment to infrastructure development, improved public services and long-term economic growth.

On the road projects, the Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Shehu Yarima Abdullahi, said the council approved seven memoranda presented by his ministry for projects covering Yamaltu-Deba, Balanga, Shongom and Kaltungo Local Government Areas.

Among the approved projects is the 18.9-kilometre Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including a spur to Dalawaja, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at N23.98 billion, with a completion period of 24 months.

Similarly, the 38-kilometre Lapan-Labariya-Lasanjan-Latatar-Lakunturum Road, with a spur to Burak, was awarded to EEC International Limited at N49.3 billion, also with a 24-month completion period.

The council also approved the first phase of the Bangunji-Dadiya-Yelwa-Gombe/Yola Road project, covering approximately 15 kilometres, to be executed by EEC International Limited at N26.3 billion.

Other projects include the initial four-kilometre section of the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road, covering Degri to Sikam, awarded to Datum Construction Company Limited at approximately N4 billion.

The 10.5-kilometre Dogon Ruwa-Kaltin Road was also awarded to the company at about N10.1 billion, while the nine-kilometre Kurjale-Pata Road was awarded to EEC International Limited.

The seventh project, covering 1.5 kilometres of the Kunuwal Road Network, was awarded to Swas Grade Limited.

Abdullahi explained that the Degri-Sikam-Nyuwar Kindiyo Road would be implemented in phases, with the initial four-kilometre stretch from Degri to Sikam approved as the first phase.

He described the approvals as an expansion of the state’s infrastructure development programme, particularly the administration’s Network 1,100 Kilometres Road Initiative, designed to open up rural communities, improve access to markets and facilitate the movement of people, goods and services.

He added that the projects would strengthen inter-community connectivity, promote agricultural and commercial activities and improve access to essential public services.

Governor Yahaya, he said, was expected to perform the foundation-laying ceremony for the Talasse-Bangu-Boka Bundi-Walalunguda Road, including the Dalawaja spur, to formally signal the commencement of construction.

N3.8bn for emergency vehicles

In another development, the council approved the procurement of 20 firefighting trucks and 20 water tankers at a combined cost of approximately N3.8 billion.

The Commissioner for Finance, Muhammad Gambo Magaji, said the acquisition of the firefighting trucks would strengthen the operational capacity of the State Fire Service, particularly as the government expands fire service stations beyond the state capital.

He explained that the additional water tankers would provide temporary relief to residents while the ongoing revitalisation of the Gombe Regional Water Supply Scheme was being completed, including plans to transition its operations to solar-powered energy.

Magaji disclosed that all 40 vehicles would be converted from diesel-powered engines to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) to reduce fuel expenditure, improve operational efficiency and promote cleaner energy.

Kolmani oil exploration

Meanwhile, the state government said it had intensified preparations to position Gombe for the anticipated resumption of oil exploration activities in the Kolmani area, with drilling expected to resume in the first week of December 2026.

The Commissioner for Energy and Mineral Resources, Sanusi Ahmad Pindiga, said the government was working with Rift Oil Nigeria Limited, a consultant engaged to facilitate the state’s institutional engagement, recognition and registration as an oil and gas-producing state.

He disclosed that the consultant had completed 12 of its 14 planned deliverables, representing significant progress in developing the institutional framework and human capital required for the state’s participation in the oil and gas industry.

One of the major achievements, according to him, was the training of 100 graduates in artisan skills, including plumbing, carpentry, information and communication technology and welding.

The beneficiaries were also provided with starter kits and financial support to enable them establish businesses, become self-reliant and position themselves for employment and entrepreneurial opportunities arising from the anticipated expansion of oil and gas activities.

Pindiga said the consultant’s engagements had also facilitated the preparation of relevant documentation and institutional support mechanisms considered necessary for the state’s participation in the emerging petroleum industry.

He described the expected resumption of drilling in Kolmani as a significant economic opportunity, stressing the need to prepare the state’s institutions, workforce and communities to benefit from the development.

SEC approves 2027–2029 fiscal framework

In another major decision, the council approved the Gombe State Medium-Term Expenditure Framework for 2027–2029, which will provide the fiscal and economic projections guiding revenue generation and expenditure priorities over the next three years.

The Commissioner for Budget, Micah Sunday Hamman, said the framework would serve as the foundation for preparing the 2027 budget while strengthening fiscal discipline, resource allocation and effective implementation of government programmes.

He explained that the MTEF would provide a realistic basis for projecting revenue and expenditure, ensuring that government policies, projects and programmes were aligned with available resources and clearly defined development priorities.

The council also approved an updated Gombe State Social Protection Policy for 2027–2030 to strengthen the state’s social welfare system and provide coordinated and sustainable support for vulnerable and disadvantaged citizens.

According to Hamman, the policy would consolidate existing government interventions and establish a comprehensive framework for protecting vulnerable groups, particularly children and other citizens requiring social assistance.

He identified the five pillars of the policy as social assistance, social insurance, labour market interventions, systems strengthening, and protection against discrimination, violence, exploitation and social exclusion.

The commissioner said the framework would emphasise transparency, inclusion and evidence-based implementation to ensure that social protection interventions reached their intended beneficiaries and improved their living conditions.

The latest decisions, he added, underscored the state government’s determination to combine infrastructure expansion with sound fiscal management, improved emergency services, social welfare and strategic economic planning as Gombe prepares for its next phase of development.

World.title: Mimiko congratulates Aiyedatiwa on Silverbird award
World.content:
…Urges Ondo governor to deepen dividends of democracy

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

Former Governor of Ondo State, Dr Olusegun Mimiko, has congratulated Governor Lucky Orimisan Aiyedatiwa on emerging as the 2026 Silverbird Governor of the Year.

Mimiko described the award as recognition of the achievements recorded so far by the Aiyedatiwa administration and its efforts towards developing the state.

The award was presented at the 20th edition of the Silverbird Man of the Year Awards held at Eko Hotels, Lagos.

In a congratulatory message, the former governor urged Aiyedatiwa to see the recognition as a call to do more for the people of Ondo State and deepen the dividends of democracy.

He said the honour by the Silverbird Group showed that the governor’s efforts were receiving recognition beyond the state.

“This honour from the Silverbird Group is an acknowledgement that your efforts are being noticed and should, therefore, spur you to do more for the benefit of the greater majority of our compatriots in our dear state,” Mimiko said.

He described Ondo State’s selection for the award among the 36 states as encouraging, noting that it reflected efforts being made across different sectors and communities.

“It is encouraging to see Ondo State singled out among the 36 states for this award. It speaks to some work being done across sectors and locations in the state,” he added.

Mimiko prayed for greater strength and wisdom for Aiyedatiwa as he continues to steer the affairs of the state.

World.title: Anambra Patriots endorse APGA-APC alliance, adopt Tinubu for 2027
World.content:
By Chimaobi Nwaiwu

NNEWI — A political pressure group in Anambra State, Anambra Patriots, APS, has endorsed the alliance between the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, and the All Progressives Congress, APC, adopting President Bola Tinubu as its preferred candidate for the 2027 presidential election.

The group also declared its support for the re-election of Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, and urged Ndigbo to support his political direction, including his backing for Tinubu.

The convener of APS and Anambra State Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, disclosed the group’s position on Sunday during the Anambra Patriots Women Summit held in Awka, the state capital.

Ezeobi expressed dissatisfaction with those criticising Soludo for aligning politically with Tinubu rather than supporting former Anambra State governor and Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi.

He argued that politics should be driven by interests rather than sentiments, insisting that Soludo’s decision to support Tinubu was in the interest of Ndigbo.

“My problem with Ndigbo is that they don’t know how to play politics. We do politics of emotion instead of interest. In politics, you get what you contributed, not what you deserve. Politics is about interest,” he said.

According to him, Soludo’s support for Tinubu was not motivated by personal gains but by what he described as the need for greater political inclusion of the South-East in national affairs.

He said: “Prof. Soludo’s support for Tinubu is not for personal gain, but for the interest of Ndigbo. It is time for Ndigbo to come back to Nigeria. And Soludo is a professor; he has analysed Nigerian politics.”

Ezeobi also argued that Soludo should not be criticised for his political choice, saying other ethnic groups had members supporting Obi without attracting similar criticism.

He urged Anambra residents to recognise Soludo’s position as governor and support his political decisions, adding that backing Obi was not compulsory for every Igbo politician.

“Why is everybody seeing Soludo as an enemy because he is supporting Tinubu? If we accept Soludo as our leader and governor in Anambra State, we must follow him anywhere he is pitching his political tent. It is not compulsory that we must support Peter Obi. Politics is not about sentiments,” he said.

The commissioner also made several claims about the political relationship between Obi and Soludo, alleging that Obi had opposed Soludo’s governorship ambition on previous occasions.

He cited the 2013, 2021 and 2025 governorship election cycles in Anambra, claiming that Obi had supported different political moves against Soludo, which ultimately failed.

Ezeobi, however, maintained that Soludo had not insulted Obi but had only responded to comments he considered critical of Anambra State and APGA.

He further criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, describing it as the political platform of a Bayelsa politician, while questioning Obi’s influence within the party.

The commissioner said the APS had resolved to support Tinubu in the presidential election while backing APGA candidates in other electoral contests.

“Today, we are adopting President Tinubu as the candidate to support in the 2027 presidential election, and we have approved Governor Soludo-led APGA and Tinubu’s APC. We will vote APC in the presidential election and vote APGA in other elections,” he declared.

Also speaking, the Secretary to the Anambra State Government, Lady Chiamaka Nnake, a founding member of APS, urged residents to join Soludo in supporting Tinubu.

The acting APGA state woman leader and APS woman leader, Mrs Joy Orah, said she was mobilising women across the state’s 21 local government areas to support Tinubu and APGA in the elections.

Similarly, the Chairman of APS, Ozoh Ejiamatu Damian Enekwechi, urged the people of the state to follow Soludo’s political direction.

“We are only following our leader. That is what we are doing. We must follow our leader in the 2027 presidential election and other elections,” he said.

Meanwhile, Vanguard observed that strategic locations across Awka had been adorned with giant campaign billboards bearing the inscription: “Solu Tinubu — The Progressives Train is on Track: Join Now and in Our Own Interest.”

World.title: True fulfilment lies in impacting lives, says Ooni
World.content:
… Backs YASA Foundation’s drive for inclusive society

By Ogochukwu Agha

lagos—The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has urged Nigerians, corporate organisations and philanthropists to support initiatives that empower vulnerable people, saying true fulfilment lies in making positive impact on others.



The monarch spoke at the unveiling of the Yeye Afolashade Shona-Aluko (YASA) Foundation in Lagos, where he donated N5 million.



Describing the foundation’s humanitarian mission as worthy of support, Oba Ogunwusi said: “What gives the greatest happiness in this world is a life of impact and fulfilment. Everybody is chasing money. But when you attain a certain level of wealth, you discover that money does not necessarily bring happiness.



“The essence of life is what you can give to others.”



Senator Sylvia Mthethwa of Eswatini urged governments and institutions to promote inclusive development, asking: “Are we developing societies in which everybody has an opportunity to participate or contribute and prosper?”



She called for improved access to education, healthcare and employment for persons with disabilities.



The Ooni’s wife, Olori Temitope Enitan-Ogunwusi, commended the foundation’s founder, urging her to remain committed to humanitarian service despite challenges.



Earlier, Shona-Aluko said her youngest son’s disability inspired her intervention. She recalled employing eight specialised teachers to support him and other children at Ikeja High School for about nine years.



She said the experience exposed the difficulties faced by families unable to afford specialised education.



“YASA Foundation was born from a burden… a burden to give voice to the voiceless, strength to the weak, and to say boldly: ‘You are not forgotten,’” she said.



The foundation focuses on inclusive education, healthcare, rehabilitation, assistive devices, vocational training and livelihood support.



The event featured beneficiaries’ testimonies and recognition of Shona-Aluko by two international institutions.

World.title: Expert pushes unified emergency response system to save lives
World.content:
By Sola Ogundipe

Nigeria needs a unified emergency response system that connects patients to ambulances, appropriately equipped hospitals, medical specialists and health insurance providers through a single call, an emergency care expert and healthcare entrepreneur has stated.

Giving the warning in Lagos,during the inaugural ResQ Summit 2026, Dr. Aisha Onisarotu Atanda, who is the Chief Executive Officer of The Ambulance Company, ResQCore and TAC Care, said that the absence of such coordination continues to expose patients to avoidable delays and risks.

Atanda, who convened the Summit themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency System”, said an integrated emergency care network would eliminate the burden on patients and their relatives to independently arrange transportation, identify suitable hospitals, secure specialist intervention and negotiate access to treatment during life-threatening situations.

Speaking at the Rescue Summit 2026, themed “Building a Coordinated Emergency Care System”, Atanda said Nigeria already had organisations and resources providing different aspects of emergency care, but poor coordination prevented them from functioning as one effective system.

She said the current arrangement often left families struggling to determine which emergency number to call, secure an ambulance and identify a hospital capable of managing the patient’s condition, resulting in delays that could compromise survival.

“The problem we have at the moment is that many organisations operate in silos. Hospitals operate independently. Ambulance companies and health maintenance organisations are also doing their own thing, all with the right intention of improving emergency care.

“However, when these organisations operate in silos, patients and their relatives are left to navigate the system themselves. They have to figure out which number to call, contact an ambulance and then decide where the patient should be taken,” Atanda said.

She noted that the proposed model would ensure that once an emergency call was received, the patient’s location and condition would be established, an appropriate ambulance dispatched and a receiving hospital with the capacity to provide the required treatment identified.

Atanda said the initiative is particularly important in emergencies involving burns, complicated pregnancies and other conditions requiring specialised intervention, where taking a patient to the wrong facility could result in dangerous delays.

“The patient’s relatives may not have the expertise to know, for instance, that a burn victim needs to be taken to a specialist burns centre. As a result, valuable time is wasted accessing the wrong care when the patient could have been connected to the right facility through a coordinated system,” she added.

Atanda, who co-founded an ambulance service provider and subsequently developed technology for coordinating emergency services, said her organisation had also extended its activities to intensive care and surgical services through TAC Care at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH.

She said the objective was to demonstrate how an integrated emergency response model could work and encourage governments to adopt and strengthen similar arrangements.

On complaints about unanswered emergency calls and delayed ambulance response, Atanda said a properly coordinated system must guarantee round-the-clock communication and effective dispatch of emergency services.

“We operate a 24-hour communication centre where someone is available to receive calls, establish the caller’s location and coordinate assistance. The goal is to ensure that patients receive the support they need throughout their emergency care journey,” she said.

She added that private sector initiatives could demonstrate workable models that government agencies could subsequently integrate into the national emergency response framework.

On the cost of emergency treatment, Atanda acknowledged that quality healthcare remained expensive but argued that health insurance offered one of the most sustainable ways of reducing the financial burden on patients and their families.

“We cannot continue to rely on out-of-pocket payments for every healthcare emergency. It is simply not sustainable,” she said.

Beyond insurance, Atanda called for stronger government-private sector partnerships, noting that the government had the authority to formulate policies and wider community reach, while private organisations could contribute operational expertise and service delivery capacity.

“There should be policies that make health insurance compulsory, while the government can also pool resources and allocate funds specifically for emergency care,

“The faster a patient accesses appropriate care, the better the chances of survival and recovery. If it takes days before someone receives treatment, the likelihood of a positive outcome becomes significantly lower,” she said.

The emergency care advocate also called for stronger public preparedness, saying Nigerians needed to understand how to recognise emergencies, seek assistance and provide basic first aid before professional responders arrived.

She said public education and first aid training were essential because emergency responders might not reach victims immediately after an incident.

“When you call for help, it may take at least five minutes for emergency responders to reach you. What do you do during those minutes before help arrives?” she asked.

She urged Nigerians to acquire basic skills to recognise conditions such as seizures and strokes, understand the appropriate response and provide accurate information when contacting emergency services.

Atanda said her ambulance company provided first aid training for individuals, corporate organisations and healthcare professionals, but stressed the need to expand such programmes and make emergency preparedness part of everyday life.

“We need to make emergency response information part of our everyday lives so that people understand how to seek help when emergencies occur,” she said.

She maintained that building a functional emergency care system would require sustained collaboration, public education, accessible health insurance and a reliable network capable of connecting patients to appropriate care without unnecessary delays

World.title: 67th NCH: Nasarawa seeks actionable resolutions to improve healthcare delivery
World.content:
By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja

The Nasarawa State Government has called on health sector leaders across the country to translate commitments and policy decisions into measurable outcomes that will improve healthcare delivery, particularly at the grassroots.

The Governor of the State, Abdullahi Sule, made the call on Monday while declaring open the Technical Session of the 67th National Council on Health (NCH) in Lafia, the state capital.

This was contained in a statement signed by the Assistant Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Ado Bako.

Represented by the Deputy Governor, Dr. Emmanuel Akabe, Sule said the Council provided an important platform for stakeholders to develop practical solutions to the challenges confronting Nigeria’s health sector.

He expressed confidence that deliberations under the theme, “From Commitments to Results: Delivering Quality and Equitable Healthcare for All Nigerians,” would produce actionable recommendations to strengthen the country’s healthcare system.

The Governor described Nasarawa’s selection as host of the national meeting as a privilege and an opportunity to showcase the state’s peaceful environment, hospitality and economic potential.

He also reaffirmed the state government’s commitment to supporting national health sector reforms and ensuring a successful meeting. He urged delegates to take advantage of the state’s hospitality during their stay.

Earlier, the Nasarawa state Commissioner for Health, Dr. Gwamna Gaza, described the meeting as a historic opportunity for the state to host health sector leaders from across the country for the first time.

He stressed that decisions reached at the Council would have far-reaching implications for the country’s health sector, urging participants to remain conscious of the fact that they were also beneficiaries of the policies and reforms being formulated for Nigerians.

He also called for active participation and constructive contributions, assuring delegates that the state government and relevant institutions were available to address any challenges they might encounter during the meeting.

Presenting the procedures for the Technical Session, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and Chairman of the Technical Committee, Daju Kachollom, said the two-day meeting, scheduled for November 16 and 17, would provide the technical foundation for the main Council meeting on November 19 and 20.

She explained that the main Council meeting would be chaired by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate.

According to her, the Technical Committee would review proceedings and the implementation status of resolutions reached at the 66th Regular National Council on Health, consider memoranda submitted by the Federal Government, state governments and other ministries, and develop recommendations for consideration by the Council.

Kachollom, said the memoranda submitted for consideration were organised around the four pillars of the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint.

The pillars, she listed, were effective governance; efficient, equitable and quality health systems; unlocking value chains; and health security.

She said the submissions would address critical areas, including the implementation of the National Health Act, multisectoral health interventions, clinical research and development, as well as strengthening Nigeria’s capacity to detect, prevent and respond to public health threats. These threats, she noted, included cholera, Lassa fever, cerebrospinal meningitis and measles.

To ensure focused deliberations, the Permanent Secretary said summaries of the memoranda had been prepared as working documents, while authors would be given five minutes each to present their submissions, highlight key issues and outline recommendations.

“The Secretariat will subsequently consolidate the Technical Committee’s recommendations for consideration by the Council,” she said.

She also disclosed that the Ministry had adopted an electronic documentation system for the Council, with relevant meeting documents preloaded onto tablets provided to participants.

World.title: Is It Worth Crossing a State Line for a Detox Bed in Western North Carolina?
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

When someone decides to stop drinking or using, the next few days can be the most physically demanding part of the process. A bed close to home is the first choice for many families, and sometimes the right bed is farther away. For people in the mountains and foothills of western North Carolina, the nearest program with an open bed may sit across the state line or a few counties over. Weighing that choice calmly, before a crisis, gives you more options.

Why Withdrawal Should Not Be Handled Alone

Withdrawal looks different depending on the substance, and some forms carry real medical risk:

Alcohol: Withdrawal can bring tremors, rapid heart rate, severe anxiety and, in serious cases, seizures and confusion. It can become a medical emergency.

Benzodiazepines: Stopping suddenly after regular use can also cause seizures. Tapering under medical supervision is the usual approach.

Opioids: Withdrawal is intensely uncomfortable, with vomiting, diarrhea, muscle aches and insomnia. It is rarely life-threatening by itself, but dehydration and relapse are real hazards, and tolerance drops quickly, which raises overdose risk if someone returns to previous amounts.

Because symptoms can change quickly, nobody can predict at home how a particular withdrawal will go. That unpredictability is the main reason clinicians recommend professional supervision.

What Medically Supervised Detox Provides

According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse, inpatient care is usually for people who need 24-hour care to manage withdrawal, and there are medications and therapies that help with withdrawal symptoms. In a detox setting, that typically means:

Regular checks of vital signs

Medical staff who can respond if symptoms escalate

Medications prescribed and adjusted by a clinician, when appropriate

Nutrition, hydration and rest in a safe setting

A counselor or therapist who begins planning the next step

Detox addresses withdrawal. It is the beginning of treatment, so a good program also helps you line up what comes after, such as residential care or outpatient therapy.

The Practical Side of Going Out of State

Crossing a state line adds logistics, so sort them out early:

Distance and transport: Ask about the drive from your town and who can bring you. Do not drive yourself if you are intoxicated or in withdrawal.

Admission timing: Ask how quickly a bed can open and what to bring on arrival.

Insurance verification: Have your insurance card ready and ask the program to check your benefits before you travel.

Work and family: Plan what to tell your employer and how loved ones will stay informed.

Continuing care: Ask how the program arranges follow-up with providers near your home.

Residents of western North Carolina can also look at the Upstate of South Carolina, where several counties sit within a short drive of the state line. American Detox & Treatment Center provides medical detox and residential treatment for adults in Chesnee, near the state line, and is accredited by The Joint Commission. It lists medical detox for North Carolina residents on a page that describes communities it serves, including Asheville, Rutherford County and Charlotte, and puts the drive from Charlotte at about 65 miles.

A short trip can also mean a clean break from familiar surroundings. Some people find that stepping away from the places and routines tied to their use makes the first days easier to focus on, while others want family close by. Neither preference is wrong, so decide based on your own situation and your clinician’s advice.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I cannot tell how severe my withdrawal will be?

Assume it could be serious and call a program or your doctor first. A clinician can ask about your substance use history and recommend a safe setting. For severe symptoms such as seizures, confusion or chest pain, call 911.

Is detox the same as rehab?

No. Detox manages withdrawal and stabilizes you medically. Rehab, whether residential or outpatient, addresses the reasons for substance use and builds skills for staying sober.

Your Next Step

Call a program today and ask what a bed search, assessment and travel plan would involve. You can also compare licensed options by location at FindTreatment.gov, a SAMHSA service that lists state-licensed programs across the country.

World.title: Okerube WASH Project Gains Community, Government Support as SHEF, ACRC Deepen Engagement
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Bennett Oghifo

Efforts to address water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) challenges in Okerube, Lagos, received fresh impetus at the weekend as community leaders, government representatives and project partners agreed to deepen collaboration towards delivering and sustaining critical facilities in the underserved community.

The stakeholder meeting, held on Saturday, November 14, 2026, brought together representatives of Community Development Associations (CDAs), women and youth groups, religious leaders, the councillor representing the area and the Baale of Okerube to review progress on the WASH intervention being implemented by SHEF with funding support from ACRC.

The meeting also highlighted growing government involvement in the project, including the inspection of a proposed site for public toilets and progress towards providing additional water infrastructure and electricity.

Giving an update on community mobilisation, community mobiliser, Funmilayo Daniel, said significant progress had been recorded since the previous stakeholder engagement, particularly in securing land for the project and strengthening collaboration between residents and government authorities.

Daniel disclosed that the Lagos State Government had inspected a proposed site for public toilets following its commitment to support the provision of the facilities.

She, however, said the community’s request for road grading was yet to receive government approval, while requests for an additional borehole and transformer had been approved.

According to her, government contractors had also inspected the proposed transformer site and advised the community to construct a basement, which had already been completed.

Speaking on the implementation and sustainability framework, a lecturer at the University of Lagos and Co-Lead of the project, Seun Muraina, said the intervention was designed not merely to provide infrastructure but to establish a community-driven system capable of sustaining the facilities after installation.

She explained that ACRC supports action research and community-driven interventions across several African cities, including Lagos, with emphasis on enabling residents to identify challenges and participate in developing solutions.

Muraina identified citizen mobilisation, reform coalitions, elite commitment and state-capacity strengthening as the four principles guiding ACRC’s interventions.

She stressed that sustainable development could not be achieved through projects imposed on communities without the participation of the people expected to benefit from them.

According to her, the Okerube intervention adopts a co-production model under which residents participate in decisions on the facilities required and how they should be managed.

“The project was considering both governance and financial arrangements to ensure that facilities provided would remain functional beyond their initial installation,” Muraina said.

She said the framework would include community ownership structures, designated representatives responsible for managing the facilities and modest financial contributions towards maintenance and repairs.

Residents would also receive training in financial management, plumbing, water conservation, purification and filtration to equip them with the skills required to manage and maintain the facilities.

Muraina said the project was further exploring how successful community-led management structures developed in Okerube could be integrated into existing Lagos governance frameworks and potentially replicated in other informal communities.

She said the objective was to avoid the familiar situation in which public facilities are provided but eventually become unusable because of inadequate maintenance and weak ownership structures.

The forthcoming situation analysis, she added, would provide a comprehensive assessment of Okerube’s WASH challenges and help the project team, residents and government stakeholders prioritise interventions.

Project Co-Lead at SHEF, Kazeem Abiodun, said Okerube was selected because of the water and sanitation challenges identified through the organisation’s engagement with residents.

He said SHEF had previously implemented interventions in other underserved communities, including Ajegunle in Apapa, and was committed to developing lasting solutions to problems affecting vulnerable populations.

Abiodun stressed that the Okerube intervention was broader than the provision of water facilities, noting that it would address the community’s wider water, sanitation and hygiene needs.

“This project will improve the lives of the people here, the economy as well as their development. We are not just working for the people; we are working with them. We are not planning for them; we are planning with them,” he said.

He urged residents to cooperate with enumerators expected to conduct the forthcoming situation analysis, saying accurate information from households would enable the project team to properly identify the community’s needs and design appropriate interventions.

Abiodun said the project had already improved access to water, with several water points established in parts of Okerube, making water more accessible and affordable.

He, however, maintained that the assessment would examine the community’s overall WASH situation rather than focus solely on water supply.

The Baale of Okerube, Riliwan Adio Salami, commended SHEF for the intervention, recalling the difficulties residents previously faced in accessing water.

Salami said the situation had improved since the organisation’s intervention and expressed the community’s readiness to support additional development initiatives.

The councillor representing Ward B, Abara-anje, Okerube, Igando-Ikotun Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Prince Olawale Hassan, described the project as a welcome development that complements government efforts in the area.

Hassan said the local government had assured the project partners of its support, particularly in securing project facilities and ensuring their maintenance.

He disclosed that government officials had participated in discussions with the project team and assured residents that facilities established under the intervention would be protected from demolition.

He added that the community and local authorities had worked together to secure the required land and complete the documentation necessary for the project.

A community representative and Chairman of Oremeji Street, Ifesowapo CDA, Lukman Olayinka, said the intervention had provided significant relief to residents who previously walked through four or five streets in search of water, especially during power outages.

He said the water facilities established through the project had substantially reduced the burden on residents, describing the intervention as an opportunity to address some of the community’s long-standing development challenges.

With the planned situation analysis expected to provide a clearer picture of Okerube’s WASH deficits, stakeholders are now looking to translate the growing community-government partnership into sustainable infrastructure, effective local management and improved living conditions for residents.

World.title: AFCON 2027: Super Eagles Aim to Consolidate against Tanzania

Duro Ikhazuagbe

After narrowing Nigeria’s disadvantage to just one point against Group L leaders, Guinea-Bissau last week, Super Eagles will need to consolidate today as the three-time Afria Cup of Nations(AFCON) champions battle hosts Tanzania inside the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar.

While Super Eagles will be aiming to win to consolidate, Tanzania’s Taifa Stars who have already qualified for the AFCON 2027 as one of the three hosts nations along with Kenya and Uganda, will need to prove before their home fans they are not in the race just for the fun of it.

Tanzania have only one point from three matches. Taifa Stars who lost 1-3 against Eagles in Uyo last Friday, will be eager to make a statement in front of their supporters. For Tanzania, Tuesday’s encounter presents an opportunity to respond and perhaps, win their first match of the qualifiers.

Under their Argentine Head Coach, Miguel Ángel Gamondi, Tanzania will hope to capitalise on home advantage, maintain defensive discipline and exploit opportunities that come their way.

Super Eagles, on the other hand, will be looking to build on their recent victory and strengthen their position in Group L. With six points from three matches, the Super Eagles are currently second behind Guinea-Bissau, who have seven points. With only one qualification spot available from the group, the Super Eagles cannot afford any more setbacks. Not even here in Zanzibar.

The stakes are, indeed, high with Nigeria eager for three points to keep their qualification chances on even keel and Tanzania keen to make home advantage count. An exciting encounter is expected in Zanzibar from 2pm Nigeria time today.

The Super Eagles possess the quality, experience and attacking options to secure another victory, but they must demonstrate discipline and avoid complacency against a side determined to respond.

Three points in Zanzibar, against a side that had never beaten them in any of their previous 14 encounters, would represent another important step towards securing Nigeria’s place at the AFCON 2027 in East Africa.

World.title: MTN Nigeria Hosts Flamingos, Gifts U17 World Champions ₦150m
World.content:

Kunle Adewale

Telecommunications giant MTN Nigeria has hosted Nigeria’s triumphant Under-17 women’s national football team to a celebratory reception in Lagos, rewarding the newly crowned world champions with a cash gift of ₦150 million.

The special event was held to honor the squad following their historic conquest at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, where they became the first African nation to lift the trophy after a thrilling 2–1 victory over Japan in the final.

Arriving at the MTN Plaza headquarters amid cheers and music, the players, coaching staff, and team officials were welcomed by top executives of the telecommunications company.

Speaking at the reception, the Chief Executive Officer of MTN Nigeria, Karl Toriola, praised the young athletes for their resilience, discipline, and unmatched patriotism on the global stage.

“You did not just win a trophy; you shattered a glass ceiling for African football and inspired millions of young girls across Nigeria,” the CEO stated while presenting the ceremonial cheque. “As proud supporters of Nigerian football, we are honored to reward your hard work and dedication with ₦150 million to celebrate this unforgettable milestone.”

According to the breakdown announced at the event, ₦115 million of the total sum was allocated directly to the players, while the remaining ₦35 million was dedicated to the coaching crew and backroom staff.

In her remarks, the team captain, Chidi Harmony, expressed profound gratitude to MTN Nigeria for the warm reception and generous financial reward, noting that corporate backing plays a vital role in motivating young athletes to aim for global excellence.

Head Coach Akeem Busari also commended the telecoms provider for consistently standing by Nigerian national teams through thick and thin.

The reception concluded with a celebratory breakfast, photo sessions with the World Cup trophy, and renewed pledges of support from MTN Nigeria toward the development of grassroots and women’s football in the country.

World.title: Jobless, over 40 and no grant: South Africans reveal the decade nobody prepares them for
World.content:
South Africans over 40 say they are trapped in a no-man’s-land, shut out of jobs because of their age but still years away from qualifying for a SASSA older persons grant.

Their frustrations poured out in comments on The South African’s Facebook page, where many described struggling to survive with no income at all.

The 18 to 35 wall AND OVER 40

Several commenters pointed to youth-focused job adverts as the root of the problem.



Waseema Classen wrote: “Job requirements age is 18 to 35 so ipeople struggling to get work so can’t just start from 50.”

Sbish Sibongile shared the same view, saying: “As it said that working age is 18 to 35 years, then those who are 36 and up, we deserve grants as pensioners; R350 is not enough.”

Her reference is to the SRD grant, which remains at R370 and has been extended until 31 March 2027.



Reshma Mahabeer added: “This post is so right,, people struggle alot after 40.”

Living off one grant

For some households, a single grant now supports two adults.

Penny Snyman explained: “My husband gets SASSA, and I’m 50, desperately looking for work and can get nothing. We must live off his SASSA. How?”



Jonathan Pedro described how even manual work has dried up, writing: “55yrs is a fare age I’m also struggling to get a garden job.”

Shemane Mogotsi summed up the mood, saying: “Its true we are being sidelined.”

Calls for a petition

Some commenters want to turn their frustration into action.



Murphybrown Edmango wrote: “Wish there was a petition that we can sign, they will be amazed to see half if the population signing it and how they ignored maojority of people above 40.”

He argued that leaving this group out hurts the wider economy because they cannot take part in it.

Ayanda Mthethwa, writing in isiZulu, suggested that people over 40 are treated as though they do not count, questioning whether their votes still matter to those in power.



For this group, the message is clear: they feel the system has forgotten them, and they want government to address the gap between youth employment programmes and pension age.

World.title: Who designed the Miss SA ‘Burger King’ crown?

Miss SA organisers have set the record straight on the crown they enthroned new winner Tiyani Makamu with over the weekend.

The national pageant has come under fire after rejecting the use of the Mowana crown, designed by Nungu Diamonds.

Instead, organisers have invited designers to collaborate with them in creating a new piece.



WHO DESIGNED THE MISS SA CROWN?

In an interview with 702, Miss SA spokesperson Zawadi Dlamini addressed the controversy of the crown, which has been likened to a party favour from the Burger King franchise on social media.

Dlamini claimed that the makeshift crown given to Miss SA 2026 Tiyani Makam was called “Imbokodo” and was symbolic of the process the contestants were going through.

He said: “We are going through a process of metamorphosis which is demonstrated through the ladies’ journey. What is important to us is not to create a crown and say it’s representative, but a crown that the people themselves have chosen and been able to collaborate with us.”



He added: “What we’re doing needs to not only be aesthetically pleasing, but it has to benefit everyone we represent, which is the people”

Dlamini claimed that the crown was not designed, but acquired from a “supplier”.

He continued: “We engaged with our crown suppliers, who was able to supply us with one for that night”



Miss SA organisers stated that the new crown would be a collaboration with the public.

Dlamini said: “This is something we’re going to work on. And we look forward in the coming months to unveiling what the final product will look like.

He added that Tiyani’s crowning ceremony would be held “in advance of her finishing her reign”.

World.title: Rassie Erasmus questions what could be seen as ‘match-fixing’
World.content:
The Springboks slipped to defeat against France last Friday, and although South Africa were architects of their own demise in many ways, there were also some seriously questionable factors that didn’t go in their favour.

From the disallowed try to Kurt-Lee Arendse, to late scrum dominance going unrewarded, there were some inevitable question marks over the performance of referee Andrea Piardi and another Italian – Matteo Liperini – who did the TMO duty.

However, during a fiery press conference on Monday, Rassie Erasmus particularly pointed out that more than 15 ‘knee drop’ tackles from France went unpunished, despite this having been identified by World Rugby has something that would be strictly officiated this season.



“The other thing that was brought up at the World Rugby meeting was knee-drop tackles. Now, I give you my word, there were (at least) 16 against us against France. 16 knee drop tackles,” he said.

“And again, I’m not saying the referee didn’t see it or the referee didn’t judge it wrong, but I don’t understand the narrative that people want the TMO to stay out.

“Because for me, and I’m gonna say it as it is, for me, if you want a TMO to stay out, and two things happen. Firstly, safety, which everybody in the Northern Hemisphere and South Africa and the world are promoting and saying, listen here, the safety of the game is a priority. Head knocks, concussions, people’s well-being must be protected.

“And then the second one is, fair, the right team must win. So if you see something where it should be penalised or yellow carded and you ignore it, but you see it and you ignore it, the conclusion must be you’re influencing the result of the team or you’re letting somebody get hurt, if you see it.

“If you didn’t see it, oh surely it’s a mistake, somebody made it. And I don’t understand why we had that meetings and then in our game, I’m honestly now saying to you, there were 17.

“Let’s say 11 of those was, I thought, at least a penalty and three I thought is at least yellow card. And not one was sanctioned. And not one was showed out or cited.



“And I’ll send you the playlist, but I’ll get into trouble, so I can’t send the playlist to anybody and we can only send five clips to World Rugby. So we’ll probably query it, but the answer will be, ‘Yes, it was a mistake.’ They should have penalised that.”

Rassie Erasmus mystified by mixed messages

Ultimately, Erasmus insisted he was not making an “accusation”, but simply making the point that it was incredibly difficult to understand why words don’t lead to action after hours of World Rugby meetings.

“Then there’s 17 knee-drop tackles and the TMO doesn’t come in once,” Rassie Erasmus added.

“I’m not saying he’s wrong, I’m saying if he didn’t see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing? Is that not interfering with the outcome of a game if you see this injury that happened there, a knee-drop tackle happened there, and it’s been decided that knee drop tackles are out.

“On numerous times, we mentioned to the referee ‘we think there’s (been) a knee drop tackle’.

“Now, I’m saying to you, my feeling is knee drop tackles is out. They happened 17 in our games. Not one was penalised even.

“And if the TMO didn’t see it, maybe then technology must be better. If he saw it and he ignored it, what does that boil down to?

“Manipulation of the game or the result or injured players getting injured. So all I’m asking, don’t take TMOs out and discourage them to get involved. Then the wrong team will win and players will get injured. That’s all I’m saying.”

The Springboks next face Ireland this Saturday, and there is no doubt that there will now be a renewed focus on the officiating.

World.title: OFFICIAL: Cape Town introduces Level 1 water restrictions from 1 December
World.content:
Capetonians collecting spring water in 2018 during the Cape Water Crisis. Image: Wikimedia

Cape Town is officially introducing water restrictions from 1 December 2026, as declining dam levels and rising consumption continue to put pressure on the city’s water supply.

The City of Cape Town confirmed the introduction of Level 1 restrictions on Monday, 16 November, following the National Department of Water and Sanitation’s latest assessment.

Residents, businesses and visitors will be expected to use at least 10% less water as the city heads into what is expected to be a longer, hotter and drier summer.



The announcement follows Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina’s decision to reduce water allocations across the Western Cape Water Supply System.

Domestic and industrial allocations will be cut by 7%, while irrigation allocations face a 15% reduction.

dam levels continue to decline

The City’s latest figures show combined dam levels at 70.4% on Monday, 16 November. This is 13.4% lower than at the same time last year.



Meanwhile, recent hot weather has pushed daily water consumption to 951 million litres.

That is more than 91 million litres above the City’s target of 860 million litres per day.

The City estimates that households need to reduce consumption by at least 10% this summer and into next winter.



“Level 1 restrictions give us the opportunity to manage demand early, protect our available water resources and reduce the risk of more stringent restrictions later,” said Leonardo Manus, the City’s Executive Director for Water and Sanitation.

What Cape Town’s Level 1 water restrictions mean

From 1 December, residents should aim to use no more than 85 litres of water per person per day.

This includes water used for personal hygiene, cooking, cleaning and laundry.



The restrictions also introduce specific rules for outdoor water use:

Garden watering: Sprinklers, hosepipes with trigger nozzles and drip irrigation are limited to one hour daily on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Watering is only permitted before 09:00 or after 18:00.

Sprinklers, hosepipes with trigger nozzles and drip irrigation are limited to one hour daily on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Watering is only permitted before 09:00 or after 18:00. Sports fields and public parks: Sprinkler irrigation is limited to one hour on Tuesdays and Fridays, before 09:00 or after 18:00.

Sprinkler irrigation is limited to one hour on Tuesdays and Fridays, before 09:00 or after 18:00. Paved surfaces: Hosing down driveways and other hard surfaces is prohibited.

Hosing down driveways and other hard surfaces is prohibited. Swimming pools: Pools may still be filled and topped up but must be covered when not in use.

Pools may still be filled and topped up but must be covered when not in use. Car washing: Private and informal car washes must use buckets or high-pressure, low-volume equipment. Commercial car washes must recycle at least 50% of their water.

These restrictions are in addition to the City’s permanent Water By-law regulations. Cape Town’s Level 1 restrictions are legally enforceable, with spot fines of R1 500 to R5 000 for applicable violations.

Manus urged residents and businesses to play their part, saying: “Every household, visitor, business and organisation has a role to play.”



The City says even small changes, including shorter showers, fixing leaks and running washing machines only with full loads, can make a difference.

Driest July on record

Cape Town witnessed a drier-than-usual winter in 2026, while large parts of the south-western Western Cape experienced their driest July on record as the global effects of El Niño are being felt.

Unlike other major South African cities, Cape Town has a ‘Mediterranean’ climate, with most of the rain falling in winter.



City officials are trying to avoid a repeat of the 2017/18 Cape Water Crisis, and the looming threat of a ‘Day Zero.’

World.title: R580 for nappies and milk? Child grant row splits South Africans
World.content:
The Child Support Grant has sparked a heated debate among South Africans, with parents demanding an increase while others question why taxpayers should fund it at all.

The clash played out in comments on The South African’s Facebook page under a post about social grants.

Parents say the Child grant amount falls short

Mickey Eagles made a passionate case for more support, writing: “Child support grant needs an increase please tell me how this ridiculously small amount of money is supposed to buy nappies and milk for small babies.”



She explained that parents often have to choose between essentials, and that costs only grow once children start primary school and need lunches and snacks.

She added: “There are parents out here without jobs that rely on that money to help sort for their children… This government is a joke honestly!!”

The grant went up from R560 to R580 in April 2026, an increase of just R20.

Critics question who should pay

Not everyone agreed. Pieter Duplessis argued that pensioners deserve support because of their years of work, writing: “The pensioners worked all their lives for this country paying tax so they deserve something back from government unlike child grants that’s a waste of money.”

Gerhard van Niekerk went further, asking: “And who made them? Why must we pay for their pleasure?”

His comment drew replies, showing how divided South Africans are on the issue.



What the grant is meant to do

The Child Support Grant is the largest grant by number of beneficiaries and is designed to help low-income caregivers meet children’s basic needs, including food, clothing and school costs.

Caregivers must pass a means test to qualify, and the grant is paid to the primary caregiver rather than the child.

Even after the latest increase, the Child Support Grant remains R216 below the food poverty line, a gap activist are pushing to close in the 2027 budget cycle.

For parents like Mickey Eagles, the debate is not about pleasure or blame, but about whether a baby has milk at the end of the month.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Bafana Bafana drop in FIFA rankings after Kenya draw
World.content:
Bafana Bafana have dropped one place in the latest FIFA rankings following their draw with Kenya.

Pitso Mosimane’s men are now ranked 49th in the world, while Harambee Stars have climbed to 11th.

Bafana will have another opportunity to improve their ranking when they face Kenya away from home on Tuesday in their fourth AFCON qualifier.



South Africa currently top their qualifying group with seven points from three matches.

Although Bafana remain inside the world’s top 50, their position could come under threat if the teams below them pick up wins while Mosimane’s men fail to beat Kenya.

Mosimane took over as South Africa head coach in August, finding the national team ranked 54th in the world.

Three consecutive victories under his leadership saw Bafana climb to 48th, their highest FIFA ranking since 2011, during his first spell in charge of the national team.

Why Bafana need to improve their rankings

Improving their FIFA ranking could also have important implications for next year’s AFCON.

A higher position in the rankings could strengthen Bafana’s seeding prospects ahead of the tournament’s group-stage draw, potentially helping them avoid some of Africa’s leading nations.



South Africa will first need to secure positive results in their remaining qualifiers while continuing to climb the FIFA rankings.

In the past 10 years, Bafana hardly made a difference in the FIFA rankings. They used to rank around 66 to 76 and only made progress under previous head coach Hugo Broos. Under Jingles, they will need to be ranked within the top 40 to be considered a top African side.

After the Kenya match, Bafana will only be in action again next year in March.
