World.title: Costa Rica President Says Jailed Gang Members Ordered Her Killing
World.content:
President Laura Fernández said Monday that she has received prison intelligence reports indicating that gang members held in Costa Rica’s prisons have ordered her assassination.

Fernández made the remarks while opening the International Congress Against Synthetic Drugs and Organized Crime at a hotel in San José, an event attended by Attorney General Carlo Díaz, Justice and Peace Minister Gabriel Aguilar and other members of the cabinet. She said the reports describe alleged plots against her originating in several prisons.

The president did not say how many reports she had received, which groups were allegedly involved or what security measures had been taken in response. Neither the Presidency nor the Ministry of Justice and Peace had released further details by Monday afternoon. Fernández told the audience she was speaking as a victim and did not need anyone to describe the threat to her.

She said she has seen relatives, neighbors and friends have their bank accounts emptied, which she tied to criminal groups operating both inside and outside the prison system. She said imprisoned gang leaders use their access to the outside to call their organizations and commission hit men. Fernández pledged to keep purging the police forces and to cut off communication between inmates and criminals on the outside.

The president said the threats had not weakened her resolve, which she credited to her faith, and called for a hard-line approach to transnational organized crime. She also argued that illegal mining should not be treated as a mere environmental offense, describing it as one of the engines that finance organized crime, an issue at the center of the debate over gold mining in Crucitas.

It is not the first reported threat against Fernández, who took office on May 8. In early June, the Ministry of Justice and Peace confirmed it had received a report of an alleged plan to attack the president but declined to comment on security, intelligence or any investigation.

An internal ministry alert dated May 29 said a confidential source had overheard two inmates held under maximum-security conditions allegedly planning the attack. The document did not describe any investigative or judicial steps, and no charges have been reported in connection with it. Local media reported at the time that the alleged plot originated inside La Reforma prison in Alajuela.

Monday’s remarks come as tensions inside the prison system have risen. The government’s new maximum-security prison, the Center for High Containment of Organized Crime (CACCO), has received more than 600 inmates since it began taking transfers, and Fernández has pushed tighter limits on visits to maximum-security prisoners, arguing that gang leaders should not be able to keep directing their organizations from behind bars.

Ombudswoman Angie Cruickshank recently visited CACCO following complaints of mistreatment. She said inmates raised allegations of physical assaults and of inadequate medical care for seriously ill prisoners, and that there was no mechanism for them to file complaints with her office. She said the claims will be investigated and warned prison authorities that retaliation against inmates who provided information is prohibited.

Attorney General Díaz, who joined the inspection, reportedly confirmed that some inmates had been beaten, following prosecutors’ findings of signs of abuse at the facility. The allegations remain under review, and no individual has been charged. Security has been the defining issue of Fernández’s government, which has clashed with the judiciary over the release of detainees and over her proposed judicial overhaul.

A Wall Street Journal report in late August noted that homicides in Costa Rica have risen about 50% since 2020, as drug-trafficking violence has spread across the country.

World.title: San José’s Festival de la Luz Swaps Floats for 10 Giant Balloons This Year
World.content:
San José will welcome the Christmas season with one of Costa Rica’s best-loved holiday traditions when the Festival de la Luz returns to the capital on Saturday, December 12, with giant illuminated balloons, marching bands, and live street performances. The Municipality of San José unveiled the 2026 program on Friday, confirming that this year’s parade will feature 10 balloons, 14 marching bands, and six ground-level shows.

The parade begins at 6 p.m. and will run from Plaza de la Democracia west along Paseo Colón to Torre Mercedes. That is a change from last year’s festival, when the parade looped around La Sabana Park. The biggest difference this year is the absence of floats. The municipality turned to balloons after six public institutions pulled their floats out of the festival in August, a withdrawal Mayor Diego Miranda has attributed to political differences with the central government.

The balloon lineup includes three blimp-style figures that will float above the route and seven illuminated inflatables. Four of the designs were chosen through a consultation with students from Escuela Metálica and Escuela República del Perú, giving local children a say in the celebration.

The six ground shows will bring characters, artistic performances, and moments of interaction with the crowd along the route. Bands in the parade are also scheduled to perform at the Band Fest the same day, and a street procession is planned ahead of the main event. Miranda said the municipality wants to offer a renewed experience that brings families together through music, creativity, and entertainment.

The municipality has not yet released road closures, public transportation arrangements, or security plans for the night. Officials said those details will be published through municipal channels as the date approaches. Last year, streets around the parade area closed from 11 p.m. the night before the festival.

The Festival de la Luz anchors a wider holiday calendar the municipality calls the Mes de la Luz, or Month of Light. On Monday, November 30, the municipality and the National Power and Light Company (CNFL) will switch on the capital’s Christmas lights at Plaza de la Cultura. Ten districts will also host community Christmas festivals between November 14 and December 20, with music, parades, local businesses, food vendors, recreational activities, and artistic performances.

The district festivals open Saturday, November 14, at the Zapote Sports Complex, followed by Catedral on Sunday, November 15. The other participating districts are San Francisco, Pavas, Hospital, San Sebastián, Mata Redonda, Merced, La Uruca, and Carmen. Most of the neighborhood festivals run from noon to 8 p.m., though some keep different hours. The last one is scheduled for December 20 at the Aranjuez Sports Complex in Carmen.

World.title: Flying Between Costa Rica and the US Today? Cancellations Have Dropped Sharply
World.content:
If you’re flying between Costa Rica and the United States today, the worst of the disruption from Friday’s nationwide US ground stop looks to be over. FlightAware reported 144 Monday cancellations and 641 delays as of Sunday afternoon. That’s a fraction of what travelers faced over the weekend. Of the 41,000 flights scheduled Saturday, more than 6,600 were canceled, according to FlightAware. On Sunday, FlightAware reported 2,291 cancellations as of 3 p.m. ET.

US officials say schedules should be close to normal today. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expects air travel to be “back to normal” by Monday, and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford had said airlines expected to recover by the end of Sunday. Check your flight before you leave for the airport anyway. When a ground stop strands planes and crews in the wrong cities, later flights can be delayed or canceled because crew members can’t get to them, and that knock-on effect can last a day or more.

Two airlines with major Costa Rica routes were among the hardest hit. American had the most cancellations on Sunday with 611, followed by JetBlue with 253. For JetBlue, that was about 27% of its schedule. At Juan Santamaría International Airport, the impact on Friday night was limited. Airport operator Aeris reported 12 departures and 11 arrivals affected, with six departures and four arrivals canceled, while the rest operated overnight and into the early morning. Aeris advised passengers to check flight status directly with their airlines, since schedules may change.

If your trip was affected, you may be able to change it without paying a fee. JetBlue’s fee waiver covers travel from Nov. 13 to 15, American extended its waiver through Nov. 18, and Delta is urging travelers with flexible plans to move their trips to Monday or later. Read your airline’s terms before rebooking, because waivers usually cover only certain dates and fare types.

The FAA has ruled out foul play. Bedford said the ground stop was caused by faulty equipment and that there was “zero evidence of anything nefarious.” Departures nationwide were halted for more than four hours on Friday after an equipment outage cut radar feeds and communication with aircraft, and the agency lifted the stop at 8:15 p.m. ET.

Duffy has given a more detailed account. He said the outage began during work to switch lines from copper to fiber at an FAA site in El Dorado, Arkansas, when turning on a new router there caused a router in Amarillo, Texas, to start flooding the system. The FAA has since disabled the broadcast feature on 69 routers of that type.

It could happen again as Duffy warned that further disruptions are possible until the copper lines are fully replaced at the end of 2028. With the busy holiday travel season about to start, turn on your airline’s app notifications and give yourself extra time on connections through US hubs.

World.title: Gusts Up to 80 km/h Hit Costa Rica’s Mountains as a Windy, Dry Week Begins
World.content:
Expect a windy Monday across much of Costa Rica. The strongest gusts will hit La Cruz in northern Guanacaste, at 50 to 80 km/h (31 to 50 mph), while the northern Pacific lowlands and the Central Valley will see 20 to 50 km/h (12 to 31 mph), according to the National Meteorological Institute (IMN). Gusts of up to 80 km/h are also forecast in the country’s mountainous areas.

The wind comes from the trade winds, which blow in from the Caribbean side. The IMN expects them to stay moderate to strong all week. As they cross the mountains they lose most of their moisture, which is why the Pacific side stays dry while the Caribbean side gets the rain. The IMN expects the trade winds to dominate this week, mainly over the Pacific, where they should keep conditions stable, while showers concentrate on the Caribbean side.

Gusts at the high end of that range can snap branches and blow loose objects around. Tie down patio furniture and anything else that could blow away. If you’re driving on mountain passes or open stretches in Guanacaste, expect gusts on exposed sections, especially in high-sided vehicles or on a motorcycle.

Most of Costa Rica will stay dry today. The northern Caribbean may get occasional rain at night and the southern Caribbean coast possible showers overnight. The Northern Zone could see occasional rain early and again at night, and the South Pacific may get afternoon showers.

It will be hot in Guanacaste and warm along the coasts. Forecast lows and highs are 19.1 to 27.6 °C in San José, 23.9 to 34.2 °C in Liberia, 22.9 to 32 °C in Quepos, 23.2 to 33 °C in Golfito, 23.7 to 29.1 °C in Tortuguero, 23.9 to 29.4 °C in Limón and 18 to 28.2 °C in Ciudad Quesada. In Fahrenheit, that’s roughly 66 to 82 °F in San José, 75 to 94 °F in Liberia and 64 to 83 °F in Ciudad Quesada.

The dry pattern may continue. The IMN’s extended outlook says the rainfall deficit would persist into late November and early December, with very dry conditions in the Central Pacific, North Pacific and Central Valley. That matters for water supply in a year when El Niño is already straining parts of the northwest.

Forecasts can change from day to day, so check the IMN’s updates before outdoor plans, especially in the mountains and in northern Guanacaste.

World.title: Masks Are Back at Some Costa Rica Hospitals. Here’s Where You Need One
World.content:
If you have an appointment at a Costa Rican public hospital or plan to visit someone who’s been admitted, bring a mask. Several hospitals in the Social Security System (CCSS) already require them, and the agency’s president is now urging a return to pandemic-era habits.

CCSS president Mónica Taylor warned about the rise in patients with respiratory illnesses. She called for mandatory masks in health centers, masks in other places, especially crowded ones and whenever you have symptoms, and proper handwashing, since rain may increase how much the viruses circulate.

The pressure on hospitals is real. Health centers report high numbers of patients with respiratory illnesses in their emergency rooms, and the intensive care unit at the National Children’s Hospital has been at its limit in recent weeks. Jerick Jiménez, head of the CCSS Health Services Network, said children and older adults are the most affected.

Here is where the rules are already stricter. At Hospital San Rafael in Alajuela, visitors must wear a mask and wash their hands before entering, a rule the hospital announced on Nov. 4. At Hospital Calderón Guardia, surgical masks and handwashing are mandatory before entering any area.

At the National Children’s Hospital, patients with respiratory symptoms and their companions must wear masks, as must companions who have symptoms themselves. Hospital México requires visitors to wash their hands before family visits and bars relatives who have flu-like symptoms.

At most other CCSS facilities, the requirement is narrower. Health centers require masks for patients who arrive with respiratory symptoms, not for everyone. According to CCSS posts on social media, the measures will stay in place until Dec. 31.

That patchwork comes from how the rules were written. An Oct. 27 memo from the CCSS medical management office tells centers to promote masks based on risk and on each patient’s condition, especially for patients with symptoms, their companions and exposed staff, rather than ordering masks for every visitor. Because each hospital sets its own rules, the simplest approach is to carry a mask whenever you go.

Some people need extra care right now. The CCSS is asking staff to pay particular attention to children under 5, adults over 70, pregnant women, people with weakened immune systems and people with chronic illnesses, and to step up flu vaccination in priority groups and RSV prevention for pregnant women and eligible children.

If you’re sick, wear a mask in public and put off hospital visits until you’re well. It protects patients who are already fragile, and at some hospitals you’ll be turned away at the door anyway.

World.title: Costa Rica Hemp Permits Are Free for Six Years, but Now You Must Apply Online
World.content:
If you want to grow hemp or medical cannabis legally in Costa Rica, there is now only one way to apply. Since November 12, every new grow application under the cannabis law must be filed online through the Single Investment Window according to the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock (MAG).

The ministry will no longer take new requests through any other channel. Applications that were already in progress, or that reached MAG before November 12, will still be processed outside the VUI until a decision is reached, the ministry said.

The change covers the two permits MAG handles under Law 10113, the 2022 law that legalized medical cannabis and hemp. The first is an authorization to import seeds and other propagation material, grow hemp and carry out primary production for food and industrial use. The second is a license to import propagation material and to grow and produce psychoactive cannabis for medical and therapeutic use.

According to MAG, the hemp authorization carries no fee and is valid for six years, renewable. The psychoactive cannabis license is also valid for six years but carries an annual fee, with differentiated rates for small businesses and small agricultural producers. The fee amounts were not included in the ministry’s announcement.

MAG made the switch through a administrative resolution and was published in the official gazette La Gaceta which orders the ministry and its attached agencies to move their procedures gradually onto the VUI. The ministry said it had also recently added agrochemical registration procedures to the same platform.

The VUI is run by PROCOMER, Costa Rica’s foreign trade promotion agency, and handles more than 40 procedures that companies need to set up and operate in the country. In February, the Health Ministry, MAG and the Costa Rican Drug Institute (ICD) opened a shared VUI channel for hemp and cannabis procedures, from production and processing to import, export and sales. The November measure makes the online route the only route for MAG’s grow permits.

Filing online does not mean automatic approval. Applicants still have to meet every requirement set out in the law and its regulations and then wait for a decision from MAG. PROCOMER warns on the platform that the VUI does not and will not ask for confidential information by phone, messaging apps or other channels. Applicants with questions can reach VUI support toll-free at 800-7762-6637 or at (506) 2505-4700.

The Law, approved in March 2022, allows cannabis only for medical and therapeutic purposes and allows hemp for food and industrial products. Recreational cannabis is outside its scope. Since then the industry has moved slowly but steadily. Authorities have issued new hemp licenses and approved medical cannabis sales, and in August the first medical cannabis manufacturing laboratory opened its doors.

For anyone following Costa Rica’s young cannabis sector, the change means the first step toward a legal crop now starts on a computer screen rather than at a ministry counter.

World.title: Costa Rica Bill Would Let Towns Cap Airbnb Rentals
World.content:
Costa Rica’s municipalities could limit how many short-term rentals operate in a neighborhood, a residential building or even on certain floors of a condominium tower under a bill filed in the Legislative Assembly by the opposition Frente Amplio party. The same bill would create a 10% tax on the commissions and service fees that platforms such as Airbnb earn from stays in Costa Rica.T

The bill, brought forward by Frente Amplio caucus leader José María Villalta, would overhaul Law 9742, the 2019 framework law that governs vacation rentals booked through digital platforms. It would also rename the law to emphasize coexistence between short-term rentals and the residents around them. The bill does not ban vacation rentals or set a national cap.

Under the proposal, local governments could limit the number, density, concentration and type of tourist lodging by district, neighborhood, zone or property. Any limits would have to rest on technical studies of housing, infrastructure, public services, the environment and mobility, with public participation and periodic review.

In mostly residential buildings, municipalities could restrict rentals to certain floors or sections if studies show they harm access to housing. The bill would also amend the Condominium Property Law so that building rules could not override those municipal limits, and it would recognize a right of residents not to be displaced by a disproportionate expansion of short-term rentals.

The 10% tax would apply to platform commissions, service fees and other income from stays in properties located in Costa Rica, regardless of where the platform is based. The bill as described in its filing does not say whether platforms could pass the cost on to hosts or guests.

Half the revenue would go to municipalities, in proportion to what each canton generates, for affordable housing and community infrastructure. Another 30% would go to the Banco Hipotecario de la Vivienda (Banhvi) for housing and affordable rental programs in cantons under housing pressure, and the remaining 20% would go to the Costa Rican Tourism Institute (ICT) for registry and oversight work.

Registration rules would also tighten. No property could be advertised without ICT registration, and each would receive a unique number that must appear in every listing. Hosts would have to prove ownership or authorization, comply with zoning and municipal licensing, be current on tax and social security payments, meet safety and sanitary standards, declare maximum capacity and provide an emergency contact. Platforms would have to register with the ICT, share information with state institutions and withhold and pay applicable taxes, with joint liability if they fail to do so.

Fines would be set in base salaries, the unit Costa Rica uses to calculate legal penalties. Hosts would face 1 to 3 base salaries for minor infractions, 4 to 10 for serious ones and 11 to 20 for very serious ones, along with possible suspension or cancellation of their registration. Platforms would face 20 to 100 base salaries for serious infractions and 50 to 200 for very serious ones. Publishing a listing without verifying its registration, leaving out the registration number or ignoring an order to remove a listing would all count as serious infractions.

The bill’s explanatory text argues that short-term rentals, especially those booked through platforms, have affected the housing market and the makeup of neighborhoods, and it cites a 2025 OECD study on housing pressure in coastal areas. It says the current law treats vacation rentals mainly as a tourism, commercial and tax matter without accounting for their effect on housing, and it states that the reform does not aim to restrict tourism.

Villalta has said the proposal seeks to balance tourism development with communities’ right to remain where they live and to find affordable housing. Law 9742 already requires owners of vacation rentals to register with the ICT and with the Finance Ministry’s tax administration, and stays booked through platforms are already subject to the 13% value-added tax. The ICT and the Finance Ministry would have nine months after the reform took effect to set up information-sharing protocols with municipalities.

The bill faces a long path. The Legislative Assembly is in extraordinary sessions through Jan. 31, a period in which lawmakers may only debate bills placed on the agenda by the executive branch, and the government’s latest agenda includes no bills from opposition parties, including the Frente Amplio.

To become law, the proposal would need to clear committee and pass two votes in the full Assembly.

World.title: Nearly Half of Costa Rica Driving Tests Failed in 2026, the Most Since 2015
World.content:
Nearly half of all practical driving tests for a standard car license in Costa Rica have ended in failure this year, the highest rate in more than a decade. Of 104,497 practical tests for the B1 license with a recorded result through Nov. 12, 51,050 ended in failure, a rate of 48.9%, according to the Road Safety Council (Cosevi).

That is the highest failure rate for the category since 2015, when it reached 52.5%. The rate fell to 28.4% in 2023 and 29% in 2024 before climbing to 37% in 2025. The figures count tests, not people, and leave out no-shows. A driver who failed twice is counted twice. Motorcycle tests were the next hardest to pass. The A1 category had a failure rate of 35.2% and A2 had 30.2%, while categories such as B2 and C2 came in near 18%.

Across all license categories, 74,946 of 202,714 practical tests ended in failure this year, or 37%. Cosevi’s records show one person has failed the practical exam 40 times, the most it has recorded, while the individual record on the regular written exam is 55 failures. The data released did not include reasons for the failures. If you are working through the licensing process, the numbers suggest planning for the possibility of a second attempt.

The figures come as Costa Rica marks the World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims on Sunday. The National Insurance Institute (INS) counted 535 road deaths through its October cutoff, up 13.6% from 471 at the same point in 2025. Motorcyclists accounted for 268 of those deaths, roughly half. They also made up about two-thirds of the injured, 27,182 of the 41,388 people hurt in traffic crashes from January to September, according to the INS.

The INS recorded 37,392 crashes in those nine months, and the number of people injured rose 9% from 37,974 in the same period of 2025. The Costa Rican Red Cross says it responds to a traffic crash about every eight minutes. The cost is borne in part by mandatory vehicle insurance. The INS said the compulsory policy, known as the SOA, has spent 50,576 million colones (about $112 million) this year on medical care and compensation for crash victims, or more than 185 million colones (about $411,000) a day.

With two months left in the year, the road death toll on Costa Rica’s highways and streets is already 64 higher than it was at the same point in 2025.

World.title: Police constable Mervin Mendez remanded after allegedly pulling gun on supervisor at Belize Family Court
World.content:
Police constable Mervin Mendez remanded after allegedly pulling gun on supervisor at Belize Family Court

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police Constable Mervin Mendez, 34, was remanded to the Belize Central Prison on Monday after pleading not guilty to an aggravated assault charge. He is accused of pointing his service pistol at his supervisor, Corporal Erick Watson, inside the Belize Family Court in Belize City.

Mendez appeared without an attorney and was denied bail. His next court date is January 11, 2027.

Watson told investigators that Mendez arrived late for guard duty at the court’s cashier area on Friday, November 13, and appeared to be under the influence of alcohol. Watson said he escorted Mendez to the cell block and asked him to hand over his police-issued firearm, but Mendez refused.

According to Watson’s report, the two argued before Mendez allegedly drew his 9 mm Taurus pistol, cocked it and pointed it at Watson as he moved toward him. Watson said he feared for his life and ran through a doorway, slamming the door behind him to take cover.

Police say Mendez later set the pistol down and walked out of the building, where Watson and another officer detained him. Watson recovered the weapon and a magazine containing 15 live rounds. Investigators took witness statements and reviewed the court’s surveillance footage before formally charging Mendez on Saturday.

At Monday’s police briefing, Assistant Superintendent Stacy Smith said Watson had asked for the weapon because he believed Mendez was not fit to carry it. Smith said Mendez eventually relinquished the pistol after removing its magazine and setting the weapon down, allowing police to secure it. She also confirmed that internal disciplinary proceedings are underway.

Breaking Belize News exclusively obtained the surveillance footage and published it on Facebook on Sunday. The video has since drawn nearly 125,000 views.

World.title: Why isn’t Southside calling for Bukele?
World.content:
Why isn’t Southside calling for Bukele?

The views expressed in this article are those of the writer and not necessarily those of Breaking Belize News.

By Nuri Muhammad: Why is it that some of the loudest voices calling for Bukele-style policing in Belize are not coming from the very communities supposedly living at the epicenter of gang violence? Where are the mothers and fathers, the grandmothers, aunties, sisters and brothers demanding that the police descend upon their neighborhoods with overwhelming force, round up hundreds of young men and lock them away?

Could it be that the people who actually live in these communities understand something that those calling for draconian police action do not?

I have spent more than fifty years working with young people and families in Belize, much of that time in the very neighborhoods now being portrayed as war zones. I know the pain that violence has caused. I know mothers who have buried their sons, children who have lost their fathers, and families who have suffered terribly because of the actions of a relatively small number of individuals.

But I also know that the people of Southside Belize City do not live in perpetual fear of every young man standing on a street corner. These young men are their sons, brothers, nephews, cousins and grandchildren. They know who is dangerous and who is not. They know that there are bad seeds or renegades in some neighborhoods who must be dealt with, but they also know that not every neighborhood is under siege and not every young Black man is a gangster.

And there is another uncomfortable question that those advocating the Bukele model should consider. What happens when the people themselves have reason to fear those entrusted with protecting them?

On January 7, 2013, four young Black men were brutally massacred in an apartment building at the corner of Dean and Plues Streets in Belize City. Their bodies were discovered the following morning. The brutality of those killings shocked the nation. There were serious allegations and suspicions involving members of the security services, allegations that the authorities denied. Yet, more than thirteen years later, no one has been brought to justice for those murders.

I am not presenting suspicion as established fact. But how can we ignore the damage that such an unresolved atrocity does to public confidence in law enforcement? How can we demand that communities surrender more of their rights and freedoms without first addressing their concerns about accountability and justice?

Perhaps the people who live in these neighborhoods understand that giving the security forces extraordinary powers, like Bukele’s police, does not automatically translate into greater security for ordinary citizens.

Let us not misunderstand the argument. There are dangerous criminals in Belize who must be apprehended, prosecuted and punished. The people of Southside want protection from violence just as much as anybody else. But wanting protection is not the same as demanding indiscriminate arrests, prolonged detention and the suspension of fundamental rights.

Belize is not El Salvador. We do not have the same gang structures, and culture, the same history or the same social circumstances. We must stop pretending that importing another country’s methods will somehow solve problems we have failed to address for generations.

We have to inject hope into these neighborhoods, not fear.

What would happen if we invested as much energy, money and national determination into education, employment, skills development, entrepreneurship and rebuilding families as we invest in emergency policing operations? What if young people could see a future beyond unemployment, frustration, the streets and prison?

I have long advocated for a comprehensive, multipronged **25-year National Crime Prevention and Community Development Plan**, implemented in five-year cycles, with clear objectives, measurable results and continuity regardless of which political party forms the government.

Such a plan must be administered by a permanent, statutory, quasi-governmental institution, staffed by trained professionals and supported by government, the private sector, civil society and the communities themselves. It cannot be another temporary political project that disappears with the next change of minister or government. We have rolled that stone up the hill many times only to start over and over again

Crime and violence are national problems requiring a national response, not just a police response. We need effective policing, certainly, but also serious investment in the social and economic conditions that shape the lives of our young people. We need a national commitment that rises above party politics and continues for a generation.

After decades of states of emergency, police operations, arrests and promises, surely, we should be asking whether we are prepared to do something fundamentally different.

Before we impose Bukele on Southside, shouldn’t we first ask the people who live there? Or are we afraid they might tell us that Bukele is not the answer?

World.title: Rumors of 72-hour global blackout debunked as U.S. FEMA clarifies November 17 emergency alert test
World.content:
Rumors of 72-hour global blackout debunked as U.S. FEMA clarifies November 17 emergency alert test

By Zoila Palma: Rumors circulating on social media about a supposed 72-hour global blackout that would disrupt electricity, internet access, banking services and artificial intelligence systems between November 16 and 17 have been debunked.

The speculation appears to have been fueled, in part, by a scheduled emergency alert test in the United States, but the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has clarified that there is no secret emergency or planned shutdown.

FEMA confirmed that it will conduct a routine test of the U.S. Emergency Alert System on November 17 at approximately 2:20 p.m. Eastern Time.

The exercise, required under the IPAWS Modernization Act of 2015, is intended to ensure that public warning systems are functioning properly. The test will be broadcast through television and radio stations only, with regular programming interrupted for approximately one minute. Cell phones will not receive alerts, and the public is not required to take any action.

Meanwhile, claims of a coordinated global blackout, cyberattack or shutdown of technological infrastructure have not been supported by verifiable evidence, Univision reports.

Cybersecurity specialist Juan D. Guevara described the claims as unfounded conspiracy theories, noting that social media algorithms can amplify fear and misinformation.

Recommendations encouraging households to maintain 72-hour emergency supplies have also been misrepresented, as these are general preparedness guidelines rather than warnings of an impending blackout.

Other online claims have referenced an episode of “The Simpsons” allegedly predicting a November 17 blackout, as well as the November 13 nationwide grounding of flights ordered by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration.

However, no evidence has established a connection between these events and the alleged blackout.

World.title: 39 public officers complete Advanced Certificate in Secretarial Studies
World.content:
39 public officers complete Advanced Certificate in Secretarial Studies

By Zoila Palma: Thirty-nine public officers representing 16 government ministries have successfully completed the Advanced Certificate in Secretarial Studies Programme, following a three-month training initiative conducted by the Ministry of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise, in collaboration with the University of the West Indies (UWI) Global Campus Belize.

The programme ran from July to October 2026 and covered five key areas: protocol and management of meetings, principles of supervision, effective communication, advanced keyboarding and document formatting, and minutes of meetings and report writing.

Delivered through a hybrid approach combining online and in-person instruction, the programme recorded a 97.5 percent success rate.

Two participants were recognized as top performers, with Keily Lisbeth Avila of the Office of the Auditor General placing first in Cohort I, while Alfreda Hemsley of the Ministry of Health and Wellness secured first place in Cohort II.

UWI Global Campus Belize representatives also highlighted the institution’s more than 15 years of partnership with the Ministry in delivering the programme.

Minister of the Public Service, Disaster Risk Management and Enterprise, Henry Charles Usher, emphasized that strong public institutions depend on the knowledge, abilities and commitment of their employees.

World.title: Belize strengthens Climate finance and resilience partnerships at COP31
World.content:
Belize strengthens Climate finance and resilience partnerships at COP31

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize, in partnership with the Green Climate Fund (GCF), continues to advance key initiatives aimed at strengthening climate resilience and sustainable development.

The Belize delegation met with representatives of the GCF at COP31 this week.

Priority initiatives include the Belize Climate Investment Platform, Maya-led pathways for climate resilience, strengthening the Belize National Protected Areas System, and advancing National Adaptation Plans.

“These efforts reflect Belize’s commitment to mobilizing climate finance, empowering communities, protecting ecosystems, and building a more climate-resilient future,” the Climate Change Department noted.

World.title: Belize highlights wildlife conservation at COP31 in Türkiye
World.content:
Belize highlights wildlife conservation at COP31 in Türkiye

By Zoila Palma: Belize’s delegation is highlighting the importance of wildlife conservation in strengthening climate resilience at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), being held from November 9-20, 2026, in Antalya, Türkiye.

Through its Wildlife for Climate Action initiative, Belize is emphasizing the role of species such as the Baird’s tapir, which supports forest regeneration through seed dispersal, and jaguars, which help maintain ecological balance.

The delegation is also highlighting the Wildlife for Climate Declaration as an opportunity to strengthen the link between biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration and climate action.

Belize continues to promote forest conservation, habitat connectivity and community-based conservation, recognizing that protecting wildlife is essential to preserving healthy ecosystems and strengthening the country’s resilience to climate change.

World.title: Team Belize prepares to showcase culinary talent at Taste of the Caribbean 2026
World.content:
Team Belize prepares to showcase culinary talent at Taste of the Caribbean 2026

By Zoila Palma: Team Belize is preparing to represent the country at Taste of the Caribbean 2026, scheduled for November 16-20 in Barbados.

The team will showcase Belize’s culinary talent, creativity and unique flavours while competing alongside other Caribbean participants.

The Belize delegation includes Senior Chef Anderson Morales, Junior Chef Anthony Tzalam, Pastry Chef Harry Canto and Bartender Ulises Alonzo, under the management of Chef Rob.

The team has spent months preparing for the regional event, honing their skills and getting ready to highlight the best of Belizean cuisine and mixology.

The Belize Tourism Board (BTB) and all Belizeans extend best wishes to Team Belize.

World.title: McNab Visual Strategies is hiring a General Manager
World.content:
McNab Visual Strategies is hiring a General Manager

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): One of Belize’s most recognized creative companies is looking for someone to help lead it into the future.

McNab Visual Strategies, home to Dots Per Inch and McNab Creative, is hiring a General Manager.

The company says it wants a resourceful, hands on leader to run its operations, work alongside its experienced team and help shape the next chapter of the business.

The ideal candidate is a natural problem solver with strong leadership skills, business experience and a passion for turning ideas into reality.

The position is full time and based in Belize City.

To learn more about the role and apply, visit www.mcnabvisual.com/jobs.

World.title: Fi Wi Land: Rooted in protection, Jamaica’s mangrove lifeline
World.content:
When Hurricane Melissa struck Jamaica in 2025, its devastating winds and storm surges left communities grappling with widespread destruction. But along our coastlines, one of nature’s most powerful defenders had been quietly at work: our mangrove forests.

More than just trees growing along the shoreline, mangroves play a critical role in protecting Jamaica’s coastal communities. From absorbing wave energy and reducing coastal erosion to providing habitats for wildlife and nurturing marine species, these wetlands are essential to the health of our environment and the livelihoods that depend on it.

In this week’s episode of Fi Wi Land, National Environment and Planning Agency (NEPA) Coordinator of Ecosystems, Chanel Raynor highlights the importance of Jamaica’s mangrove ecosystems, noting their role in strengthening coastal resilience against increasingly powerful storms and supporting the island’s rich biodiversity.

Discover the different types of mangroves found in Jamaica, the growing threats posed by climate change, pollution and human activity, and the simple steps Jamaicans can take to protect these vital ecosystems, as the Jamaica Observer, in association with NEPA, presents another episode of Fi Wi Land.

Catch the latest episode on the Jamaica Observer’s YouTube channel and other digital platforms.

World.title: ATL Vikings eye first Business House basketball title
World.content:
Members of the 2026 ATL Vikings squad

ATL Vikings are one win away from claiming their first Business House Basketball League Division Two title after taking a 2-0 lead in the best-of-five final series against Sagicor B.

The team, making their first appearance in the finals since entering the competition in 2024, will look to complete the job when the third game is played at the National Stadium basketball court on Monday at 6:30 pm.

The team brings together employees from across the ATL Group, including Appliance Traders Limited, the Jamaica Observer and ATL Automotive.

Khenielle Cooper, team manager of ATL Vikings, said the team advancing to this stage of the competition is a demonstration of unity across the group.

“It’s very significant, especially because we’re pretty new. The team is new, the idea of playing basketball as a company is new, just about three years. It’s pretty young, but we’ve excelled beyond what we’ve expected because when we would have started in 2024, we would have come second to last in the league and then in 2025, we had a major improvement, coming third, and now 2026, we are in the finals playing to win the Business House League for Division Two,” she said.

Cooper also credited the team’s improvement to the work of coach Nyron Hurd.

Among the players leading the charge are Vaughn Chevannes, Kevin Williams, Eric Smith, Darryl Reid, Onario Blidgen.

The team manager said the players were confident heading into their match Monday evening, having won the first two matches of the final.

“It’s been a long time coming. There has been a lot of blood, sweat and tears, a lot of injuries, a lot of pain and I know that the team has really worked hard and the gentlemen truly deserve this win,” Cooper said.

The cost for admission to the game is $200, with an additional $200 for parking at the stadium.

World.title: Buju, Shaggy, Chronixx, Protoje, Runkus and Ziggy vie for Grammy Best Reggae Album
World.content:
Buju Banton’s Too Too Bad, Shaggy’s Lottery, Chronixx’s Exile, Protoje’s Art of Acceptance, Supernova by Runkus and Brightside by Ziggy Marley are the nominees for Best Reggae Album for the 69th annual Grammy Awards.

The nominations were announced Monday morning.

Too Too Bad is Buju Banton’s eight nomination. He was previously nominated in 1999 for Inna Heights, 2004 for Friends for Life, Too Bad in 2007, Upside Down in 2020, Rasta Got Soul in 2010, Born for Greatness in 2024 and Before the Dawn (which won in 2011).

Exile has given Chronixx his second nomination. He got a nod in 2018 for Chronology.

Brightside gives Marley his seventh solo nomination in the reggae category. He won in 2014 for In Concert, the self-titled Ziggy Marley in 2017, Love is My Religion in 2007 and Fly Rasta in 2015. His other nominations were for Rebellion Rises (2019), and Wild and Free in 2012.

As the lead singer for Ziggy Marley and the Melody Makers outfit, the group was nominated seven times but only won three times: Conscious Party (1989), One Bright Day (1990) and Fallen is Babylon (1998).

The Art of Acceptance, the latest effort by Protoje, gives the St Elizabeth-born artiste his third nomination. He earned nods for 2019’s A Matter of Time and 2023’s Third Time’s The Charm.

Supernova is the first nomination for Runkus, while Lottery is the eighth nomination for Shaggy. Shaggy won in 1996 for the platinum-selling Boombastic and again in 2019 for 44/876, a collaborative effort with Sting.

The 69th Grammy Awards ceremony is scheduled for February 7 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles.

World.title: More beach access
World.content:
Jamaica Labour Party Leader Dr Andrew Holness arrives at Montego Bay Convention Centre on Sunday for the party’s 83rd annual conference. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Responding to growing local and international concern about the level of access Jamaicans have to local beaches, Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Sunday announced that he has mandated Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett to tackle the issue head on. Holness’s comments came as he addressed the 83rd annual conference of the governing Jamaica Labour Party (JLP).

“I know that in the public order and public spaces session the issue of beach access would have been raised, a sore topic for many Jamaicans, and a growing cause for international concern and indeed bad publicity for Jamaica,” the JLP leader said from the stage at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James.

In August, the tourism minister blasted people who he said are creating a false impression internationally that Jamaicans are being denied access to the country’s beaches, and the Government listed 60 beaches across the island that it says provides free access to the public. Now the prime minister has indicated a new course of action.

“The Government has been paying close attention to this, and while it is not my proposal to discuss the full issue here, your minister of tourism has been charged — they have assessed all the beaches in Jamaica — I am giving him a task to ensure that in the next budget at least 10 public beaches are improved,” Holness said during Sunday’s address.

“So that the average Jamaican can get not just access, not just walk on the beach, but can have a facility that is clean and a facility that is also safe; and thereafter, to execute a programme through the Tourism Enhancement Fund to ensure that every parish has at least two public beaches with free access,” the prime minister added.

At the podium for about two hours, Holness also announced plans to revitalise the country’s tourism sector.

“Our tourism product generally needs a refresh. Tourism has been growing and expanding — without question. Now we have to look at the quality of the product we offer and how that impacts the brand of Jamaica. That means we need some investment in the tourism infrastructure, but more importantly, in the tourism human resources,” he said.

“The first large-scale effort in this will be the establishment of tourism improvement districts. The first will be the Hip Strip in Montego Bay, then this wonderful elegant corridor [in Rose Hall],” Holness added. (See related story: Holness signals progress on MoBay master plan.)

He said similar initiatives are also planned for Negril, Ocho Rios, Portland, St Mary, Westmoreland, and St Elizabeth.

“These will have special municipal legislation for the areas declared, and they will come with some amount of fiscal incentives to incentivise investments in those areas. We must improve the quality of the product we offer,” the prime minister urged.

He also spoke of plans to clean up the country’s cities and towns, an initiative he said that took shape during the conference.

“One of the greatest complaints that we have here in St James, and indeed in all our town and our cities, is that the public space is not clean. The public space is not orderly…We will, in the next budget, launch an island-wide campaign to clean up all our cities and towns and public spaces, and to maintain them and keep them at that standard,” the prime minister said.

He then instructed Minister of Finance Fayval Williams to double, to 60, a request before her for new garbage trucks to ensure “more effective garbage collection throughout the country”.

“I will be calling in all the mayors of the municipalities because this is not just a central government problem; it is also a local government problem. Local government, the mayors and the councillors, need to play their part in ensuring not just the collection, but we have to now start talking to the homeowners about how you dispose of your garbage…This Government will mobilise and treat with the transformation of our country to make it more beautiful, more appealing,” Holness promised.

World.title: Holness signals progress on MoBay master plan
World.content:
Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness (right) being given a tour, Saturday, of an under-construction town house at Richmond Hill Club by developer John Surdeen. Joining them is state minister in the Ministry of Industry, Investment and Commerce Ministry, Delano Seiveright.

MONTEGO BAY, St James — After decades of Montegonians clamouring for a master plan to be implemented in an effort to breathe new life into the city’s major business districts and revitalise some of its most iconic spots, Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness has signalled that their lobbying has paid off.

“People want to be able to move around in the city and in the town seamlessly, and so that’s the next phase of the Government’s public thrust towards developing the area,” said Holness as he apologised for challenges faced in now moving around while a number of major infrastructural projects are being done.

He was speaking during Saturday’s ground-breaking ceremony for the US$125-million Richmond Hill Club mixed-use development on the hills above the resort city. The work being done on the water supply and the road network, Holness said, will pay off in the long run and is linked to the Government’s wider plans for the parish.

“All of that [is] to help with the seamlessness of coming to Jamaica. A major part of that will be the establishment of two tourism development corridors in St James. One will be the Hip Strip and the other will be the elegant corridor [in Rose Hall]. We have already started work on developing the legal and administrative framework of those business improvement areas,” the prime minister disclosed.

“It will involve some fiscal incentives, but it will also involve direct investments in the roadway, in the streetscapes, and it will also involve the creation of a new way of managing the municipal arrangements for those areas. The idea is to truly create an iconic public space for tourism in the tourism capital of the country,” Holness added.

Several hotels are among the major projects now under construction. These include the 165-room AC Marriott Montego Bay on the Hip Strip. The lifestyle hotel is on the site of the former Sandals Carlyle, or “Baby Sandals”, and marks a transformational shift from all-inclusive to a modern, European plan (EP) model.

Meanwhile, on the elegant corridor, Moon Palace’s 1,200-room US$700-million luxury resort is set to be the tallest hotel in Jamaica at 33 storeys. It will also include staff quarters that are reportedly being built on an area of land adjacent to the property. In the same area is the Unico 18°77° hotel, a 451-room, adult-only luxury resort. Then there is the under-construction US$850-million Hard Rock Hotel & Casino Jamaica. It will be a luxury, all-inclusive resort.

The Richmond Hill Club, located in the heart of the city, has now added another layer to its growth and development. Overlooking Montego Bay, it sits on land whose heritage dates back to the early 1800s. The property, which once housed a hotel with the same name, hosted diplomats, celebrities, and locals celebrating major milestones before it was destroyed by fire in December 2019.

Now, John Surdeen, through his JARRAN Developments, is looking to preserve that rich history while he repurposes the space as a lifestyle destination. There is a resort component, there’s an apartment component, and then there’s a low-density housing component. The plan includes 120 condos and 526 residences.

Amenities within its twin residential towers include a pool, gazebos, terraces, a health and wellness centre, rooftop terraces with impressive views of the city, and large living and apartment spaces with unprecedented access to the views via a bridge that connects both structures. There will be 202 one-, two-, or three-bedroom units. There will be about 700 parking spots available for the condos and towers, which will sit on nine acres of land.

Expectations are that the roll-out of properties will begin sometime in 2027.

World.title: Frugality and resilience
World.content:
A section of the crowd gathered at Montego Bay Convention Centre, Sunday, for the 83rd annual conference of the Jamaica Labour Party. Garfield Robinson

ROSE HALL, St James — Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness on Sunday unveiled “frugality and resilience” as the governing theme for the next four years, alongside major announcements regarding the sourcing of $9.65 billion in additional roof repair grants and plans to position Jamaica to seize opportunities made available through artificial intelligence (AI).

“Labourites, today I want to introduce to you the theme for the Government for the next four years. I told you about frugality. The next pillar of our theme is resilience,” Holness told party faithful gathered at Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James for the Jamaica Labour Party’s (JLP) 83rd Annual Conference.

He addressed the frustration of citizens still awaiting housing recovery assistance.

“It does break my heart every time I see someone saying, ‘My roof, I can’t put it on yet because I haven’t received my grant. I’m still waiting on my grant.’ And it becomes even more difficult when your neighbour has got the grant and you don’t get the grant yet. You wonder if the State abandoned you or forgot about you. Well, no,” assured Holness.

He said funds have been identified for a previously announced additional expenditure for the Restoration of Owner or Occupant Family Shelters (ROOFS) programme.

“I am pleased to announce that your minister of finance sharpened her scalpel and, like a surgeon, she went in and she cut out all the fat, and we were able now to find the $9.65 billion so that the remaining 50,000 Jamaicans who are patiently waiting on their grants, they will get their grants,” Holness stated.

The prime minister noted that 11,000 beneficiaries have already been verified and are waiting for funds to hit their accounts before receiving a text, call, or cheque. He said he has given Minister of Labour Pearnel Charles Jr a December 20 deadline to have 90 per cent of the grants distributed by Christmas.

The minister has also been given a mid-January deadline to ensure “that all persons who have been assessed and verified as being in need would have received their grants”.

Turning his attention to the issue of AI, Holness urged Jamaica to capitalise on emerging global technology, rather than trailing behind. He said the Government has taken concrete steps to attract AI investment locally.

“We have put in place an AI task force that’s advising the Government on what we need to do in this regard. But the announcement that I would like to make here today is that the Government has just approved an MOU with a group of investors to explore the establishment of artificial intelligence infrastructure right here in Jamaica so that Jamaica can have a footprint and not only be a consumer of the technology, but we can be a part of the creation of the technology,” stated Holness.

He said the initiative is aimed at ensuring future generations are equipped to secure jobs in the rapidly evolving AI-driven global economy.

World.title: Grammy predictions
World.content:
The nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards are to be announced today, Monday, November 16.

The Best Reggae Album category (formerly known as Best Reggae Recording) was first introduced in the 1985 ceremony, with Black Uhuru’s Anthem winning the first award.

Some 119 projects, including various artiste compilations, gospel, reggae, and dancehall albums, were submitted this year, compared to 73 the previous year.

Work that qualify for the submission period should have been released between August 31, 2025 to August 28, 2026.

It’s a very tough year to really nail down who may be the possible nominees in the Best Reggae Album category as so many notable releases created an impact both locally and overseas.

There were notable releases by Capleton, Buju Banton, Beenie Man, Burning Spear, Alkaline, Queen Ifrica, and Kabaka Pyramid.

Below are predictions as to which albums could make the cut in the Best Reggae Album category, when the 2027 nominees are announced:

Brightside: Multi-Grammy-winner Ziggy Marley was probably the only act who did any meaningful campaigns around his project. He could snag a nomination for

Brightside, which was released last May via Tuff Gong Worldwide.

Exile: Released last October to rave reviews, Exile by Chronixx is poised to possibly end up among the nominees. He previously secured a nod for Chronology in 2018.

Art of Acceptance: This work may give Protoje his third nomination. He was previously nominated in 2019 for A Matter of Time and Third Time’s The Charm in 2023.

Supernova: Critically acclaimed Supernova by Runkus was ranked among the 50 Best Albums released so far in 2026 a few months ago by respected music and trade publication Billboard. One of the better reggae projects released this year, it has the elements that could help steer it among this year’s nominees.

There is a toss-up among Masicka’s Forever Reign, Lottery by Shaggy, and God and Time by Vybz Kartel.

The truth is, Masicka has put in a lot of work and Forever Reign is a decent project that deserves a fair listen. It doesn’t hurt that the project was released by major label Def Jam Recordings that may utilise its connections to secure a deserving nod for the deejay.

Shaggy knows the system and is a favourite among voters in the Recording Academy. Lottery didn’t quite hit the spot sales-wise on the Billboard charts. But, truth is, voters don’t care if you were big on the charts or you’re the most popular. Lottery did spawn a few crossover hits on Billboard’s Rhythmic chart, and being a familiar name will probably help Shaggy in his bid for an eighth nomination in this category. Mind you, he has already won twice.

God and Time: Vybz Kartel has had a great year with several chart hits, songs that made an impact within the dancehall space and a Billboard-charting album with God and Time. A two-time nominee, it wouldn’t come as a surprise if the King of the Dancehall nabs his third nomination.

World.title: Gov’t to regularise squatter settlements via Jamaica Build
World.content:
Minister with responsibility for land, Robert Montague speaking during Sunday’s conference. Garfield Robinson

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) Chairman Robert Montague has announced plans for a new land regularisation initiative, Jamaica Build, which is aimed at addressing the country’s 527 informal settlements, home to almost 700,000 Jamaicans.

Montague, who is minister without portfolio in the Ministry of Economic Growth and Infrastructure Development, with responsibility for land titling and settlements, said consultations have already begun ahead of the programme’s launch.

Addressing the JLP’s 83rd Annual Conference at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James on Sunday, he said the initiative was being developed on the instructions of Prime Minister Dr Andrew Holness to find a lasting solution to the widespread problem of informal settlements.

“The prime minister has given strict instructions that we must find a way, and we have found a way. We have begun the consultations,” Montague said.

He said Jamaica Build would seek to regularise the settlements over time, allowing residents to secure legal titles to the land they occupy and pass the property on to future generations.

The programme’s name, he explained, reflects its broader objective of promoting unity and independence through land development.

“We call it Jamaica Build because it is building unity and independence through land development. We’re building Jamaica not for today only, but for the future,” Montague explained.

He said the initiative would provide a pathway for thousands of families living in informal communities to obtain greater security of tenure and establish a lasting legacy for their children and grandchildren.

Montague did not outline a launch date or provide details of the programme’s implementation framework.

World.title: French presidential rivals take aim at Le Pen in debate
World.content:
The most heated moment came when Le Pen detailed her plans to require charities that receive public money to refrain from meddling with politics.

“Your model is the same as that of your friends, Mr. Orbán and others, which is ultimately to shut up and stop those who do not think like you,” said Attal.

“You’ve got a list,” retorted Mélenchon, when Le Pen said she would deliver a list of charities she believed were too political.

Le Pen appeared to be playing it safe during the debate, trying to avoid being dragged into a damaging fight with her opponents. Her most pointed attacks targeted Attal, who is the leader of President Emmanuel Macron’s party Renaissance and was briefly prime minister in 2024.

“I don’t have any lessons to learn from someone who spent 10 years creating the biggest debt in the history of this country,” Le Pen said to Attal.

Le Pen and Mélenchon, who is polling in second place and could end up facing the far-right leader in the presidential runoff, avoided directly confronting each other during the debate.

World.title: Brexit diminished us, Burnham says as he tees up closer EU ties
World.content:
The U.K. prime minister set out his ambition to build a closer U.K. relationship with the EU at his first Labour conference as leader in September — confirming weeks later his desire for the U.K. to rejoin the EU within his lifetime.

But he is treading a fine line with some members of his own Cabinet, who hold differing views on how far the U.K. should realign with the bloc and whether red lines — including rejoining single market or the customs union — should be crossed.

“This is not about re-running the arguments of 2016,” the U.K. prime minister said, while stressing any new arrangement in this parliament will not breach Labour’s 2024 manifesto, must improve the existing Brexit deal, and benefit working people struggling with the cost of living.

Lamenting Brexit as “exactly what our enemies wanted,” the British prime minister said the U.K.’s withdrawal from the EU had been the “first domino to fall in a global move towards isolationism and protectionism.”

“In the decade since Brexit, our standing in the world has diminished,” he said. “We treated both allies and institutions with insufficient care, and the effects went beyond Europe.”

Burnham joked during the speech that it was a stretch talking about the “Makerfield test” — a reference to the views of his Brexit-voting constituents in Greater Manchester — while wearing white tie and having just received a trumpet salute.

World.title: Concurrence : l’UEFA et une fédération de grands clubs de football européens visées par une plainte
World.content:
“La question est simple : qui a son mot à dire sur les règles qui déterminent l’avenir de chaque club ? Aujourd’hui, une seule organisation détient ce pouvoir pour l’ensemble des clubs européens, alors que la plupart d’entre eux n’y ont aucune influence réelle”, a pointé Dennis Gudasic, directeur exécutif du Lokomotiva Zagreb en Croatie et secrétaire général de l’UEC.

Reste qu’il sera difficile de convaincre Bruxelles d’ouvrir une enquête. La DG Concurrence, le puissant organe de la Commission chargé de l’application des règles de concurrence, s’est toujours montrée réticente à ouvrir des enquêtes dans les affaires liées au football, les considérant comme politiquement toxiques, selon des hauts responsables actuels et anciens de cette administration.

L’UEFA entretient également de bonnes relations avec la Commission. Son président Aleksander Čeferin et le commissaire européen chargé des Sports, Glenn Micallef, ont renouvelé un accord de coopération lors d’une réunion qui s’est tenue à Nyon, en Suisse, la semaine dernière.

En comparaison, les relations entre Bruxelles et la Fifa sont habituellement glaciales, selon trois responsables actuels et anciens de la Commission. Pourtant, Bruxelles s’est montré réticent à ouvrir une enquête officielle en matière de concurrence à l’encontre de l’instance dirigeante du football mondial au sujet de son calendrier des matchs internationaux, malgré la pression de députés européens.

“La mission de l’UEFA est de veiller au football européen dans son ensemble”, a déclaré l’instance dans un communiqué. “Nous l’accomplissons grâce à un modèle de gouvernance inclusif, qui associe toutes les parties prenantes : les fédérations nationales, les ligues, les clubs, les joueurs et les supporters ont tous voix au chapitre, et les décisions sont prises par le dialogue et le compromis. Dans le cadre de ce modèle de gouvernance, le memorandum of understanding UEFA-EFC, publiquement accessible, offre depuis 2008 un cadre stable et transparent pour la coopération avec les clubs à l’échelle européenne. Il garantit que les clubs participants prennent véritablement part à toutes les décisions concernant les compétitions européennes de clubs.”

Contactée par POLITICO, EFC n’a pas répondu à nos demandes de commentaire au moment de la parution de cet article.

World.title: UK hands Palantir two-year reprieve on NHS contract
World.content:
In a bid to regain “public trust” and open up opportunities for “U.K. sovereign capabilities,” Frith said “interoperability, resilience and trusted common standards” will be “baked into” the new procurement round, though non-U.K. firms will also be encouraged to bid.

Palantir’s contract has attracted considerable scrutiny from campaigners, health professionals and MPs over controversial views expressed by the company’s founders and concerns about vendor lock-in.

Two parliamentary committees have called for its NHS contract to be ended in the last year.

“We want to give the health and care system more choice, greater resilience and less dependence on any single supplier, as well as the ability to adapt and evolve as new technologies emerge in future, with better value for taxpayers through time,” Frith said.

“These objectives require a new approach — an approach that will stimulate a more diverse and innovative supplier market, including greater use of sovereign AI as well as internationally developed capabilities,” he added.

This approach will encompass investment in strategic technologies, changing how novel technologies are procured, and developing open standards, Frith said.

World.title: Le bras de fer entre Le Pen et les constitutionnalistes
World.content:
Share on LinkedIn

Share on WhatsApp

Share on X

Share via email

L’initiative n’est pas habituelle : 110 professeurs de droit ont cosigné une tribune dans Le Monde, mercredi dernier, pour rappeler les règles prévues en matière révision de la Constitution. Leur message : modifier notre loi fondamentale via l’article 11, utilisé jadis par Charles de Gaulle, est irrégulier. Or, Marine Le Pen prévoit d’y recourir pour faire adopter par référendum ce qui constitue le cœur de son programme : la préférence nationale, la prééminence du droit national, ou encore la suppression du droit du sol.

Anthony Lattier évoque les enjeux de cette dispute juridique et politique avec le constitutionnaliste Benjamin Morel, maître de conférence en droit public à l’université Paris-Panthéon-Assas, qui a interviewé, il y a quelques jours, la candidate du RN pour la revue Le Grand continent.
