World.title: Will Croatia Finally Get a Break From Price Increases in 2027?
World.content:
November the 16th, 2026 – Will Croatia finally get a break from price increases and constant pressure on the public’s bank accounts and wallets in 2027? A slowdown is on the cards…

The finance minister also spoke about whether citizens can expect a better standard of living and what the Government’s offer is for increasing salaries in public and state services. Poslovni reports that price growth could weaken already in the first months of next year, but the realisation of the Government’s forecasts will largely depend on the movement of energy prices and the geopolitical situation.

Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Tomislav Ćorić expects that inflation in Croatia will begin to slow significantly already in the first quarter of 2027. Appearing on the central HTV News, he assessed that the economic projections for next year are optimistic, especially in comparison with expectations for the European Union and the Eurozone. According to the Government’s projections, inflation in 2027 should fall to 2.7 percent on an annual basis, while economic growth of 2.1 percent is expected.

when can we expect a price slowdown?

Ćorić believes that the beginning of the year should bring a weakening of inflationary pressures thanks to the gradual disappearance of base effects from previous price increases and the expected calming of oil prices. These are factors that should contribute to slower price growth, although this does not mean that products and services will necessarily become cheaper. The minister considers the greatest risk to the realisation of these expectations to be a possible deterioration of geopolitical circumstances, primarily the continued escalation of the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

If there are no new disruptions on international markets, he believes that the planned economic indicators could be achieved.

will quality of life actually improve in 2027?

Asked whether he expects that the general public will live better in 2027 than currently, Ćorić replied that he hopes so and believes in it. He bases such expectations on the reduction of inflationary pressures, an increase in the standard of living and the continuation of economic growth. He also believes that the investments envisaged in the new state budget should further strengthen the resilience of the Croatian economy.

The minister also commented on the negotiations on salaries for employees in state and public services. For 2027, the Croatian Government has offered an increase in the base for calculating salaries of a total of 3.5 percent and the gradual introduction of a meal allowance, which would reach 50 euros per month by the end of the year. Ćorić considers this a realistic offer, aligned with the possibilities of the state budget.

An agreement has not yet been reached, however. The public service trade unions rejected the offered increase in the base and initiated a mediation procedure, while the state service trade unions still need to consider the offer in their bodies.

further spending on defence

Speaking about increased defence expenditure, Ćorić said that economic results enable higher budget revenues and expenditures, which is why it was not necessary to reduce funds for other sectors in order to finance security investments. Around 1.5 billion euros is envisaged for defence in the budget proposal for 2027, and the minister confirmed that spending should continue to grow due to the obligations Croatia has assumed within NATO.

At the same time, the Government plans to keep the general government deficit at the level of 2.9 percent of GDP and to continue reducing the share of public debt. Ćorić emphasised that stable public finances and the rise in Croatia’s credit rating enable more favourable borrowing conditions. As an indicator of citizens’ confidence in government securities, he singled out the latest issue of one-year treasury bills, in which the desired amount of one billion euros was reached after only five days. The minister also expects that a budget rebalancing could follow after the summer of 2027, but he does not foresee major changes compared to the current plans.

World.title: Seismic Stations Cover All of Croatia for the First Time
World.content:
November the 16th, 2026 – Seismic stations cover all of Croatia for the first time ever, with 125 stations currently measuring earthquakes, and a further 55 planned.

As part of the much wider EU CROSSNET project, Croatia has installed 125 seismic stations and plans another 55, which would bring the network to around 180 stations. Zrinka Gabelica Toplek reports for Poslovni that project leader Tomislav Fiket emphasised that for the first time, the entire country is now covered from Ilok all the way down to Cavtat. He did however duly warn that further implementation depends on the employment of nine young experts.

rapid warning systems

CROSSNET modernises and significantly expands the system for monitoring seismic activity in Croatia. A dense network of stations enables more precise determination of the location and magnitude of earthquakes, faster data processing and better information for the public and the competent services. At the conference “From the 1880 earthquake to the modern seismic network – how we monitor ground shaking today”, held to mark the 146th anniversary of the great Zagreb earthquake, Fiket said that the general public, wherever they live, should now be able to receive equally high-quality information.

“For the first time in history, all of Croatia has been successfully covered by seismic stations. It’s extremely important to us that every single person, wherever they live, has the opportunity to receive equally high-quality information,” Fiket emphasised. Earthquakes can’t be predicted, but rapid warning systems can react after the arrival of the first, non-destructive wave. A dense network of stations makes it possible to send a warning to citizens before the arrival of the destructive second wave, which can reduce the number of victims and the extent of damage. Data from the stations arrives at the central system in near real time, and people can also follow 24-hour records of the seismic stations and an interactive earthquake hazard map.

a 13.6 million euro project

The CROSSNET project is otherwise worth around 13.6 million euros. Of that, 75 percent is financed by the European Union through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NPOO), and 25 percent comes from the state budget itself. It was launched back in November 2021 and was supposed to finish at the end of June, but has been extended until the 31st of December 2026 because the employment of nine young experts participating in its implementation has not been secured.

The problem arose after the financing of the Seismological Service of the Republic of Croatia was transferred from the state budget to programme contracts of the Faculty of Science (PMF) at the end of last year. “Those nine jobs were missed in the negotiations and were not negotiated,” Fiket said, emphasising that the Faculty of Science was supposed to ensure the employment of these experts, but this has not been done so far.

World.title: Photos: Truck crash jams outbound traffic on Tallinn's Tartu maantee
World.content:
A truck crashed into a lamppost on Tartu maantee and got stuck under an overpass Monday afternoon, disrupting outbound traffic at a busy Tallinn junction ahead of rush hour.

Two outbound lanes on Tartu maantee have been closed due to the crash, backing up traffic near Ülemiste, T1 and Sikupilli shopping malls, Ülemiste train station and Tallinn Airport.

Police received a report of a crash at around 2:30 p.m. on Monday.

Initial information suggests the truck and its trailer struck part of the overpass, bringing down an overhead road sign gantry onto the roadway.

The driver, a 37-year-old man, was sober and licensed to operate the vehicle. No one was injured in the crash.

Police at the scene have been redirecting traffic via Peterburi tee.

World.title: Mayor: Narva fears humanitarian and economic consequences of the border closure
World.content:
Narva Mayor Jaan Toots (Center Party) says that if the Estonian-Russian border is completely closed, border controls should also be reinstated on the Latvian border.

He also calls on the government to allow humanitarian crossings for Estonian residents who still have relatives in Russia.

In an interview with ERR in Narva on Monday, Toots said he learned about the government's plans to completely close border crossings with Russia starting December 1 from the news. According to him, the interior minister had previously discussed possible border closure scenarios with him, but city authorities were not informed in advance about a specific decision.

Russian flag at Ivangorod Fortress, opposite of Narva at the Estonian-Russian border. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

Toots has several concerns

Toots highlighted three main concerns related to the potential closure of the border.

The first concerns security. In the mayor's view, if the authorities consider the threat serious enough to close the border with Russia, they should also restore controls on the Estonian-Latvian border. He noted that recent incidents involving illegal border crossings were linked to people arriving from the Latvian side.

The second concern is humanitarian. Jaan Toots believes it is necessary to find a way to allow Estonian residents to travel to Russia when they need to visit elderly relatives, attend funerals, or deal with other urgent family matters.

The third concern is economic. According to the mayor, closing the border could further harm employment in Narva, since border guards and customs officers are mostly local residents. In addition, the city could lose some tourists from Finland, Latvia, and other countries who have used local hotels and restaurants.

Jaan Toots said he has already contacted the interior minister and intends to present his arguments to him. The issue was also discussed at the morning meeting of the leadership of the Center Party, where the mayor of Narva serves as a vice chairman.

Asked about the future of the project to build a shelter for people waiting at the border crossing, for which funding has been allocated in the city budget, Toots replied: "Everything is on hold now."

Urbo Vaarmann. Source: Sergei Stepanov/ERR

Vaarmann: Estonian state should support the affected region

Narva City Council Chairman Urbo Vaarmann said that if the border is closed, he expects the government to provide support to Narva residents and local businesses.

According to Vaarmann, Narva and the whole of Ida-Viru County must remain places where people feel confident visiting, living, and investing.

"The announcement of the border closure may cause visitors and investors to reconsider their plans. Therefore, the state must help maintain confidence in our region, support local businesses, and attract new investments," Vaarmann said.

The chairman of the Narva City Council stressed that the assessments of Estonia's security agencies must be taken seriously. At the same time, he noted that the state has a duty to protect people and prevent security threats, and that responsibility also includes having a concrete plan for supporting the region most directly affected by such decisions.

"Our people must feel that the state stands by them. That means a safe hometown, jobs, warm homes, and affordable utility bills," he added.

The Estonian government announced its intention to close all border crossing points with Russia from December 1 following the attempted arson attack on defense company Threod Systems in Viimsi on November 14. According to the Internal Security Service (ISS), the attack was organized at the direction of Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. Eight Latvian residents were detained on suspicion of involvement in preparing the attack.

World.title: Professor: New power generation should accompany data center construction
World.content:
Large data centers planned for Estonia could end up consuming a significant share of the country's electricity, says Mart Landsberg, a professor at Tallinn University of Technology. The most important question is how much added value can be created with that energy.

Professor Landsberg pointed to two data centers planned in Estonia, one near Tallinn in Hüüru and another in Risti. Both are designed to have a capacity of roughly 200 megawatts.

For comparison, Estonia's peak electricity demand during this past winter's highest-demand hour was about 1,700 megawatts. A single 200-megawatt data center would therefore account for more than 10 percent of that figure. In terms of annual electricity consumption, such a facility could use approximately 1.3 to 1.6 terawatt-hours of electricity, equivalent to roughly 20-25 percent of Estonia's annual electricity consumption.

"What matters about energy is not where it comes from or how much it costs. What matters is how much added value we can create with that energy," Landsberg said.

According to him, even cheap and clean energy may bring limited benefits to society if it is used for low-value-added activities. Conversely, more expensive energy can make economic sense if it generates sufficient wealth and raises people's incomes.

Landsberg said data centers differ from many current industrial and household consumers because their electricity consumption does not depend as heavily on whether conditions are warm or cold. As a result, they can be valuable customers for the electricity system because their demand is more stable.

At the same time, he noted that a growing share of electricity system costs consists of fixed costs, while the cost of the electricity itself, such as the wholesale market price, makes up an increasingly smaller share of total expenses.

Eestisse rajatava AI-tehase Nebius andmekeskus. Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

"Energy itself no longer costs very much, but capacity and access to energy are worth their weight in gold," Landsberg said.

The problem, according to Landsberg, is that electricity consumption among households and commercial customers in Estonia is growing while industrial electricity consumption is declining. This means there are fewer consumers helping to share fixed network costs, potentially shifting a larger burden onto households and businesses.

For that reason, he said the impact of data centers on electricity costs for Estonian consumers cannot be viewed as purely positive or negative. The overall cost of energy supply must be considered, along with the broader economic benefits data centers bring to society.

Important factors include the jobs created, tax revenue generated and the extent to which data centers use goods and services produced in Estonia. Landsberg cited local industry as an example of a sector that could benefit from new opportunities created by data center development. In his view, the presence of local data centers could also support product development by speeding up innovation processes and creating competitive advantages for companies.

Data center connection requests exceed Estonia's current electricity demand

Asked whether Estonia's electricity system is prepared for the addition of several large data centers, Landsberg said everything depends on how quickly and on what scale those projects are implemented.

He referred to data from Elering showing that Estonia's current peak demand is around 1,700 megawatts, while connection requests from data centers and other large consumers total approximately 3,000 megawatts.

If all of those projects were realized simultaneously, the resulting change would be enormous and could not immediately be accommodated by the existing electricity system. However, connection requests do not automatically translate into completed projects. Landsberg cited Finland as an example where, according to him, there are far more interested developers than signed connection agreements.

In addition, data centers are typically built in phases rather than all at once. One module is completed first, followed by the next. For that reason, development of the electricity system and the regulatory environment must keep pace with project development.

Landsberg argued that investments in electricity networks required for data center projects should not be borne solely by other electricity consumers. Data centers themselves should shoulder a larger share of those costs.

New power generation should accompany data center development

One of the biggest questions, Landsberg said, is how to avoid a situation in which new data centers push up electricity market prices by introducing major new demand that competes for existing generation capacity.

That effect could be reduced by requiring data center developers to ensure additional electricity generation capacity alongside their projects. This could take the form of building their own power plants or entering into long-term agreements that support the development of new generating capacity.

Landsberg pointed to a regulatory change currently being discussed in the Finnish parliament that would require data centers seeking grid connections to ensure additional electricity generation capacity on a long-term basis.

"If done intelligently, data centers could certainly help drive the construction of new power plants," he said.

In his view, it is not enough to rely on market forces alone and assume new generating capacity will automatically appear in response to increased demand. Appropriate mechanisms need to be designed in advance.

"Landsberg estimated that the average lifespan of computing equipment may be around five years or slightly longer."

As one example, he highlighted plans for the Risti data center, where the project is being developed alongside solar and wind generation as well as battery storage. Power purchase agreements and other obligations may also form part of the solution.

According to Landsberg, the goal should be to ensure that existing electricity consumers benefit rather than lose out from the arrival of data centers.

He also noted that the investment horizons of data centers and power plants differ significantly. Power plants are long-term investments. Wind farms typically have a lifespan of around 20 years, while nuclear power plants can operate for about 60 years.

Data centers, by contrast, have shorter investment cycles because the computers they use require relatively frequent replacement. Landsberg estimated that the average lifespan of computing equipment may be around five years or slightly longer.

This means that if energy costs rise significantly, a data center could relatively easily decide to relocate elsewhere. If the project also includes investments in power generation or energy infrastructure, however, lasting value remains in Estonia even if the data center eventually leaves.

Data centers require a continuous electricity supply, which means their operations cannot rely directly on the variable generation of wind and solar energy. According to Landsberg, one solution is battery storage, which can store energy from wind and solar power and release it when data centers need it. Batteries can help manage fluctuations within and between days.

The unresolved issue remains seasonal fluctuations. Estonia receives little sunlight during winter, raising the question of how electricity generated from solar energy in summer can be stored for winter use.

"At the moment, we do not have a better solution than fossil-fuel power plants, such as gas-fired plants, which can cover the shortfall during winter peak demand periods," Landsberg said.

Over the longer term, he sees an important role for hydrogen, both in hydrogen production and in converting hydrogen back into electricity.

Landsberg said Estonia's strengths include favorable offshore wind conditions and a relatively cool climate that provides efficient cooling conditions for data centers. Combined with hydrogen technology, these advantages could form one of Estonia's future growth engines.

Greenergy data center in Hüüru, Harju County in northern Estonia. Source: Tõnu Tunnel/Greenergy

Waste heat use depends on nearby demand

Data centers also produce waste heat that can potentially be reused. According to Landsberg, successful utilization depends largely on whether a sufficiently large heat consumer is located nearby.

He compared two planned Estonian projects: the data center in Hüüru and the planned facility in Risti. Because of its proximity to Tallinn, it will likely be easier to find a major heat user for the Hüüru project.

At the same time, utilizing waste heat requires additional investment, creates additional risk and lengthens project timelines for developers. This can increase costs and delay completion.

As a result, developers must determine whether potential revenues from selling waste heat outweigh the added costs and risks.

Landsberg said that while waste heat utilization may make perfect sense from society's perspective, what is optimal for society is not necessarily optimal for developers. In his view, the state can help by designing a regulatory framework that ultimately delivers the most cost-effective outcome for consumers.

Estonia must learn to capitalize on the electric age

More broadly, Landsberg argued that the world has entered the electric age.

According to him, the International Energy Agency has highlighted the growing shift toward electricity as the dominant form of energy consumption. In the coming decades, key technologies will increasingly be those powered by or connected to electricity.

Estonia's challenge, he said, is determining how to extract as much economic benefit as possible from this transformation. If the country fails to keep up, it may find itself among the losers. If it uses new opportunities wisely, however, it can increase both national and societal prosperity.

Landsberg compared current technological developments to the Industrial Revolution.

"If the first Industrial Revolution centered on transferring physical labor to machines, then the next Industrial Revolution now underway is about transferring intellectual labor to machines. The question for us is whether we want to be among the winners or the losers in this revolution. Energy exists to do work on behalf of people," Landsberg said.

World.title: Foreign Ministry summons Russian chargé d'affaires
World.content:
Estonia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has summoned Russia's chargé d'affaires to express its strong condemnation of the attempted arson attack carried out against defense industry company Threod Systems on Saturday night.

According to the Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS), the act of sabotage was ordered by Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU.

Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna (Eesti 200) said that Vladimir Putin has failed to achieve his objectives in the war of aggression against Ukraine and is now increasingly seeking to sow uncertainty among Ukraine's allies.

"Through various acts of sabotage, Russia aims to spread fear, divide our societies, and distract attention from supporting Ukraine," Tsahkna said.

"Estonia is, however, a difficult target for this type of inluence activity. We have many years of experience in detecting and preventing Russian sabotage, businesses are aware of the risks, and authorities act swiftly and decisively. The saboteurs who targeted Threod Systems have been detained and the threat has been eliminated," the foreign minister added.

According to Tsahkna, Russia's hostile actions come at a cost.

"We are preparing to close all road border crossing points between Estonia and Russia to vehicles and pedestrians starting on December 1. Together with our allies and partners, we will continue exposing and countering Russian influence activities. Nor will our pressure on the aggressor diminish. Just today, the European Union added 150 individuals and entities to its sanctions list. We will continue working to strengthen sanctions, tighten visa restrictions, and increase support for Ukraine, especially ahead of the coming winter," Tsahkna said.

Representatives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs also strongly condemned Russia's large-scale drone and missile attacks against Ukraine in recent weeks.

Over the past week alone, Russia has launched more than 2,300 drones at Ukraine.

The primary targets of these attacks have been civilian infrastructure, including critical infrastructure, hospitals, educational institutions, shopping centers, residential buildings, warehouses, and ports. During the past week alone, 55 people have been killed and 371 injured.

World.title: Auditor general: Pension hikes won't hinge on state budget being passed
World.content:
Pensions in Estonia will rise next year even if the Riigikogu fails to pass the 2027 state budget in December, says Auditor General Janar Holm.

Holm rejected claims by governing politicians that pensions and pay raises for senior public officials would be jeopardized if the budget is not approved.

Speaking on Vikerraadio's "Uudis+" on Monday, Holm explained that pensions are indexed each year on April 1 under the State Pension Insurance Act, making the annual increase a legal obligation independent of the state budget.

"To the best of my understanding, the pension amount does not depend on whether the state budget is adopted," he said.

The same applies to pay increases for senior public officials because those are also required by law. However, planned raises for teachers could be affected, as they are not statutory obligations and cannot be distributed without an approved budget.

"But as far as pensions are concerned, based on my understanding, I'd say that pensions are clearly a statutory expense and do not hinge on the passage of next year's state budget," Holm reiterated.

State won't grind to a halt

Holm explained that if the Riigikogu doesn't pass the 2027 budget, the Estonian government will have to use the previous year's budget as its basis, checking whether each expense was included and limiting monthly spending on it to one-twelfth of the amount allocated for that purpose in the previous year's budget.

He said that could affect investments, while new spending not included in the previous year's budget would not be able to go ahead until the new budget is approved.

If the budget bill allocates less for a particular expense than the previous year's budget, he added, spending must also stay within the lower proposed amount.

"The budget should still be passed, as the state operates on the basis of that budget," the auditor general said, but emphasized that the country will not grind to a halt if the Riigikogu doesn't pass it in time.

The Constitution and other laws, he noted, provide various mechanisms for handling such situations.

World.title: Saaremaa shipyard to launch largest Estonian-built warship
World.content:
An experimental 45-meter military vessel will be launched at the Baltic Workboats shipyard on Saaremaa on November 18.

EUROGUARD will be the largest military vessel built in Estonia since the restoration of independence. The project is led by Estonia and involves ten European countries and 27 industrial partners, said Ahto Pärl, member of the management board of Baltic Workboats AS.

Its total budget is €95 million, with €65 million provided by the European Defense Fund.

The ship has been developed as an experimental platform for the next generation of European naval vessels. The design includes capabilities for autonomous navigation and remote operation from shore.

The vessel is intended for maritime surveillance, mine countermeasure operations, protection of critical infrastructure, and search-and-rescue missions. It is designed to travel at a speed of at least 20 knots, has a range of at least 2,000 nautical miles, and can remain at sea for up to 10 days.

World.title: Kaspar Viilup: Pop culture wave of "GTA VI" will be felt for a long time
World.content:
The new "Grand Theft Auto" video game, more than a decade in the making, is just days away, and while the Estonian media still struggles to cover gaming as thoroughly as it should, the impact of this pop culture tidal wave can hardly be overstated, Kaspar Viilup writes.

If we try to briefly explain the phenomenon behind this video game, the most important foundation is its long history. Just like "Super Mario" or the legendary fighting games "Tekken" and "Mortal Kombat," "Grand Theft Auto," which first appeared nearly 30 years ago, has been a part of several generations' childhoods. Fathers have introduced the game to their sons and those same sons may now have children of their own, opening the door for them to this vast criminal underworld where players are given free rein to decide what kind of experience they want to have.

So at this point, we're not simply talking about a single game, but decades of expectations and experiences, nostalgia and anticipation, built up layer by layer. Add to that the fact that fans have had to wait more than a decade for a new installment and the fire has been continually fueled. Developer Rockstar Games is well aware of this, too, because although previous installments have also been massive undertakings, the scale is now on an entirely different level: Analysts estimate that the game's budget could reach $1.5 billion, while first-week sales revenue could climb as high as $5 billion. Yes, I know those numbers sound completely unrealistic, but that's precisely the kind of absurd, mind-boggling scale this game operates on.

Another key to understanding "Grand Theft Auto" is its lack of boundaries: Almost everything you can do in the game is either irrational or illegal, from stealing cars and recklessly speeding through the streets to engaging in mindless violence. While it's also possible to follow the game's storyline, my experience, and probably that of many others, has always been about seemingly aimless wandering. I vividly remember, for example, that my first encounter with country music as a teenager came while driving an SUV along rural roads in "Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas," with Hank Williams playing on the car radio. Once you've had a taste of that kind of escapism, you want to experience it again.

In other words, excitement over what this new release will bring has reached fever pitch and there's even widespread talk that when the game comes out, many people around the world will suddenly fall ill and fail to show up for work. In Estonia, however, the biggest challenge will be how the media manages to cover it all. Although "Disco Elysium" provided an initial trial by fire for more conservative publications that would otherwise run in the opposite direction at the mere mention of video games, its impact wasn't particularly long-lasting. When ZA/UM studio's new game "Zero Parades" was announced, everything had been forgotten and the silence in the Estonian media was deafening.

So I'll proudly get the ball rolling: Don't be afraid to talk about "Grand Theft Auto." It's perfectly fine to risk looking foolish and ask people who know more about it for help, because chances are there are at least a handful of people among your friends or even family members who will spend the coming days and weeks glued to their television screens, eyes darting back and forth. Even the major Hollywood studios know this, having pushed their biggest movie releases as far away from the "GTA" launch as possible, with the new "Hunger Games" movie the only one brave enough to remain. We'll see how these two giants fare against each other, but I can predict the outcome with considerable confidence: "Grand Theft Auto VI" will emerge victorious and we'll still be feeling its ripple effects at the end of this year and into the beginning of next year, perhaps even longer.

World.title: Kaja Kallas' role in Ukraine peace talks unclear
World.content:
Responding to an ERR question about her inclusion in Europe's negotiating team, Kaja Kallas said the decision was up to European Union leaders and that she would continue working on the substantive issues in the negotiations regardless.

Last week, European Union leaders agreed that Europe would be represented in Ukraine peace talks by the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and EU institutions. Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said the institutions would be represented by European Council President António Costa and either Ursula von der Leyen or Kaja Kallas from the European Commission.

I was a little unclear about the new agreement, specifically who will speak on behalf of the European Union and represent Europe. Will it be António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen, or will you also be involved?

It was the leaders' wish that António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen would be the ones involved, alongside the five countries.

After all, I meet with foreign ministers every month. I have the European External Action Service, which has experts on Russia and previous agreements. That expertise is also needed in these negotiations. So we are working on the substance, even if the format was decided on Friday.

Still, you have been very outspoken on Russia. Should we now be concerned that the European Union is unwilling to speak as clearly on these issues as you have? Is the European Union reluctant to choose the people who would present its positions in the clearest possible terms?

The European Union consists of 27 member states and representatives of those 27 member states, all of whom come from democracies, so to speak. That is why I think the work you do in the media is also very important — asking those negotiators questions at every opportunity. Of course, we do the same.

For example, when Russia has put forward various demands, have you asked for anything in return? If someone comes along saying sanctions must be eased, which is obviously in Russia's interest, what do we get in return?

Right now, we see that Russia has presented its maximalist demands, some of which are completely absurd. Together with the foreign ministers, we have prepared Europe's maximalist demands. Yes, you could say that some of those are also absurd, but they actually reflect two things.

First, they reflect the fact that Russia is the aggressor in this conflict. They also reflect the pressure being placed on Ukraine, for example, when it comes to limiting the size of its military. The problem, after all, is the size of Russia's military, not Ukraine's. We are trying to keep the focus on these substantive issues and we hope the free media will do the same.

A quick question about Estonia as well: There was an attempted arson attack on a building belonging to defense industry company Threod over the weekend. What is the European Union doing to support Estonia in this situation?

We will, of course, discuss all these hybrid attacks today. I also feel that the word "hybrid" is far too mild and that we should actually describe these attacks more specifically for what they are. Naturally, we will also propose various sanctions in response.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia begin replacing Iranian oil in China
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Saudi Arabia have begun replacing Iranian crude oil in China after Tehran’s shipments plunged under a US naval blockade, according to reports from Bloomberg and vessel-tracking data from Vortexa.

Iran’s oil exports to China fell to less than 100,000 barrels per day in October 2026 compared to roughly 1.4 million barrels per day before the outbreak of regional conflict in February.

The US maritime blockade imposed on Iranian ports along the Arabian Gulf in July 2026 severely restricted Tehran’s ability to export crude by sea.

Independent Chinese refiners have turned to trading houses like Mercuria Energy Group to source up to 20 million barrels of discounted Iraqi oil transported through the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraqi Basra grades have offered some of the most cost-effective alternatives for December 2026 arrivals, trading at significantly lower premiums over Brent than competing Russian barrels.

Saudi Arabia and Iraq are stepping in to cover the gap left by Iran, which previously made up roughly 13 percent of China’s seaborne imports.

Iraq’s oil supplies to China during September totaled 4.84 million tons, or about 1.18 million barrels per day, a 19 percent decline compared to the previous year and a 248 percent increase compared to August.

China’s crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia stood at 2.70 million tons, or about 660,000 barrels per day, marking a 62 percent decline compared to the previous year.

Chinese independent refiners increased recently their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives.

World.title: Internal rift splits Kata’ib Hezbollah over Jurf Al Nasr handover
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – An internal leadership rift has emerged within Kata’ib Hezbollah over the security future of Jurf al-Sakhar (Jurf al-Nasr) as high-stakes negotiations unfold with Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s government amid escalating military mobilizations around the northern Babylon subdistrict.

According to exclusive disclosures obtained by the 964 Network, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) Chief of Staff Abdul-Aziz Al-Muhammadawi (“Abu Fadak”) favors reaching a negotiated settlement with the Al-Zaidi administration that would permit federal forces to enter and assume security responsibility over sectors of the area.

Conversely, Kata’ib Hezbollah Secretary-General Abu Hussein Al-Hamidawi remains firmly opposed to granting security concessions at this stage, holding Abu Fadak directly responsible for the political and legal fallout triggered after a government investigative committee entered the restricted zone for the first time in 12 years.

Sources familiar with the ongoing talks revealed that the faction’s Al-Hamidawi wing proposed deferring any handover of Jurf al-Sakhar until June 30, 2027, aligning the transfer with the scheduled expiration of the national deadline for restricting weapons to state control.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi, however, rejected maintaining the status quo for that duration, insisting on the immediate deployment of federal security forces to hold all or key parts of the subdistrict and actively participate in security decision-making.

Al-Hamidawi’s posture reportedly hardened sharply over the past several hours due to the unanticipated consequences of Abu Fadak’s earlier understanding with Baghdad.

That initial agreement permitted federal investigators to inspect the closed territory, culminating in official findings of illicit oil smuggling, public disclosures, and judicial referrals—an outcome that left Al-Hamidawi deeply wary of authorizing any further security compromises.

The leadership split has sown operational confusion among Kata’ib Hezbollah’s field commanders and brigade leaders stationed inside Jurf al-Sakhar. Historically, the group’s chain of command relied on Al-Hamidawi setting broad strategic policy while Abu Fadak issued operational directives and execution mechanisms; their conflicting stances on a federal handover have left local units without unified instructions at a critical juncture.

Meanwhile, federal military preparations continue to intensify around the perimeter:

World.title: Rival reinforcements converge on Jurf Al Nasr as Al Zaidi sets deadline for Kata’ib Hezbollah
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Armed personnel reinforcements—believed to belong to allied armed factions—arrived in the Jurf al-Nasr (Jurf al-Sakhar) subdistrict of northern Babylon Governorate on Monday evening, November 16, 2026, to bolster Kata’ib Hezbollah positions against a potential armed confrontation with state forces, according to a security source.

In immediate response, federal command dispatched additional detachments from the Federal Police and the Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) stationed in neighboring provinces to reinforce military units already massing around the subdistrict.

The dual mobilization follows consecutive overnight troop deployments toward northern Babylon after Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi formalized a directive ordering official security forces to enter Jurf al-Nasr and assume full security jurisdiction.

Government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi confirmed that Baghdad has issued a strict deadline for Kata’ib Hezbollah to withdraw from the subdistrict—reportedly expiring on Friday, November 20—while Coordination Framework figures, including Nouri Al-Maliki, Hadi Al-Amiri, and Humam Hamoudi, pursue eleventh-hour mediation to secure a phased handover and prevent open hostilities.

The standoff stems directly from the formal findings of the government investigative commission dispatched to Jurf al-Nasr on November 13, which inspected six intelligence-flagged coordinates and documented clear pipeline tampering, two clandestine refining facilities, and underground storage tanks.

Based on the report, Al-Zaidi referred implicated suspects to the judiciary, ordered security forces to block all unauthorized fuel tankers from exiting the area, and dismissed nine senior security, military, and administrative officials in Babylon—including the Provincial Police Chief and the provincial Hashd al-Shaabi commander.

Kata’ib Hezbollah flatly rejected the smuggling allegations, asserting that the field inspection uncovered no pipeline breaches and claiming that the tanks and processing equipment found on site were strictly used to supply fuel for military vehicles. Escalating its defiance on Monday via its official Telegram channel, the faction published photographs of fighters preparing drones and declared that its weapons remain an inviolable right in the hands of its fighters.

World.title: Iraq claims fourth place globally at 2026 Youth Muay Thai World Championships in Greece
World.content:
Olympia (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s national youth Muay Thai team secured fourth place globally at the 2026 IFMA Youth World Championships held in Ancient Olympia, Greece, capturing an impressive 25-medal haul against competitors from 109 countries.

According to an official statement issued by Iraqi Muay Thai Federation President Mustafa Jabbar Alak, Iraq’s medal tally broke down as follows:

Gold Medals: 11

Silver Medals: 5

Bronze Medals: 9

Staged from November 6 to 16, 2026, the tournament brought together more than 800 athletes aged 8 to 18 competing across 154 divisions in full-contact ring bouts, semi-contact technical events, and traditional Wai Kru and Mai Muay disciplines.

Alak credited the fourth-place world finish to sustained preparation by the athletes, coaching staff, and administrative leadership. He underscored that the achievement represents a major milestone for Iraqi combat sports, demonstrating the technical caliber and international competitiveness of Iraq’s rising generation of fighters on the global podium.

World.title: Zaidi invites German firms to invest in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi met with Germany’s Federal Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development, Reem Alabali-Radovan, and her accompanying delegation in Baghdad on Monday, November 16, 2026, renewing his call for German corporations to enter the Iraqi market and participate in major infrastructure and industrial projects.

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Media Office, discussions centered on expanding bilateral cooperation across economic, commercial, and investment sectors. Al-Zaidi emphasized the depth of Iraqi-German ties and underscored that the federal government is prepared to grant extensive incentives and administrative facilitations to streamline operations for foreign investors entering Iraq.

Highlighting Iraq’s strategic push to build a diversified, non-oil economy, the Prime Minister pointed to the flagship Development Road Project as a primary catalyst for bilateral partnership, noting the substantial commercial opportunities embedded in its planned industrial and economic cities along the transit corridor.

For her part, Minister Alabali-Radovan reaffirmed Berlin’s backing for the Iraqi government’s reform and development agenda, expressing Germany’s readiness to expand joint initiatives across key priority sectors:

Climate, Environment & Agriculture: Expanding technical and developmental cooperation to address environmental stress, climate resilience, and sustainable agricultural modernization.

Institutional Development Financing: Moving forward with signing a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) linking Iraq with the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) and the German Development Bank (KfW) to anchor long-term bilateral projects.

The Baghdad meeting builds directly on Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s official visit to Berlin in mid-September 2026, where he held talks with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz to deepen European trade ties and attract German industrial investment into Iraq.

World.title: Iraq seeks implementation of land transport deals with Jordan, Egypt
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani announced the push two weeks ago during a regional transport summit in Alexandria, Egypt.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The announcement took place during the 39th session of the Arab Transport Ministers Council, which was held at the Arab Academy for Science, Technology and Maritime Transport in Alexandria.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Earlier in August 2026, Iraq and Egypt also reached a specific agreement allowing empty Iraqi cargo trucks to re-enter Egyptian territory.

Officials emphasized that activating these corridors is a priority to protect trade flows amid ongoing regional disruptions.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad launches crackdown against Kataib Hezbollah
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has launched a major crackdown against the Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah over an illicit oil-smuggling network operating in its stronghold of Jurf al-Sakhr.

Iraqi officials estimate the scheme has stolen hundreds of millions of dollars from the state since 2021, with monthly illicit revenues reaching up to $30 million.

Investigators uncovered concealed pumping equipment inside hangars and a hidden oil refinery in Jurf al-Sakhr, located about 50 kilometers south of Baghdad.

The network illegally tapped into strategic pipelines—including a 26-inch pipeline carrying at least 200,000 barrels per day—to siphon crude oil onto tanker trucks.

Following the investigation, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security and oil-sector officials and referred suspects to the judiciary.

Those removed include the Babil provincial police chief, local intelligence and security commanders, and the director of the state-run Oil Pipelines Company.

According to Reuters, al-Zaidi has ordered senior military and security commanders to deploy additional forces around Jurf al-Sakhr. Troops are preparing to enter the militia-controlled town, raising the risk of direct armed confrontation.

Kataib Hezbollah has denied the smuggling allegations, claiming the storage tanks and workshops found by investigators were used to fuel military equipment. The group characterized the government probe as a campaign of “blackmail” designed to force it to surrender its weapons.

The crackdown comes amid heightened US pressure on Baghdad to curb Iranian influence and illicit oil networks in Iraq, following US sanctions imposed earlier this year on Iraqi officials and militia-linked entities.

World.title: Iraq orders nationwide ban on Telegram due to security concerns
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities ordered on Wednesday a nationwide ban on the Telegram messaging application due to security concerns, regulatory violations, and the platform’s failure to address unlawful content, incitement, and extremism.

According to the Iraqi Communications and Media Commission (CMC), the directive was issued by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, providing the platform with 30 days to comply with national laws.

Reports mentioned that Telegram failed to comply with Iraqi laws and regulatory requirements. The CMC cited national security concerns, cybercrime, hate speech, extremism, and incitement to violence and unrest.

The CMC gave Telegram’s operator 30 days to regularize its legal status and cooperate with Iraqi authorities on content moderation. Officials have not yet specified the exact technical steps required or whether the block will be lifted early if the company complies.

The announcement comes on the same day Jordan banned Telegram over similar concerns regarding extremism and national security.

In April 2026, Iraqi authorities suspended Telegram. On May 9, the CMC lifted the ban after Telegram’s management promised to abide by national laws and user safety requirements.

World.title: Ties with Asean crucial for India's Act East Policy: PM
World.content:
As he arrived in Manila for the India-Asean and East Asia Summit meetings,

said his visit will impart new energy to India's partnership with the political and economic union of southeast Asian nations and reinforce the collective commitment to a peaceful, prosperous and resilient Indo-Pacific.

Modi attended a dinner hosted by Philippines President Ferdinand Marcos Jr soon after his arrival, and ahead of the main multilateral and bilateral engagements Tuesday. While no bilateral meet with US President Trump had been scheduled till late Monday, official sources confirmed the Quad leaders' summit would take place Tuesday evening.

Trump is expected to spend only a few hours in Manila, before taking off for Shenzhen in China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.



Modi will attend a groundbreaking ceremony at a gurudwara Tuesday morning before participating in the 23rd Asean-India summit.

In his departure statement in Delhi, Modi said India's relationship with Asean countries is at the heart of India's Act East Policy and occupies a central place in its MAHASAGAR vision. "Our ties, rooted in centuries of civilisational exchanges, have grown into a dynamic partnership spanning trade, connectivity, maritime security, technology and people-to-people relations," said Modi, who did not mention Quad in his statement.





All eyes on Quad as Modi to hold bilateral with Marcos

Modi also said that at the ASEAN-India Summit, he was looking forward to working with fellow leaders to build on the progress of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and give further momentum to the shared aspirations for growth, connectivity and prosperity.

The PM also spoke about the East Asia Summit, saying it provides an important platform for dialogue on regional and global challenges. "I look forward to exchanging views with participating leaders on strengthening peace, stability and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific," said Modi, adding he would interact with the vibrant Indian community in the Philippines, whose contributions strengthen the bonds between the two countries.

Modi will also have a bilateral meeting with Marcos on the margins of the multilateral events, before returning to India late Tuesday.

The meeting that will likely draw maximum attention in India and possibly Japan is the Quad leaders' summit - the first such meeting since Trump returned to the White House. Amid speculation that Trump might have downgraded Quad, the summit is expected to reaffirm commitment, if not announce fresh initiatives, in shared areas of interest like maritime security, critical technologies, supply chains, connectivity, health and economic security.

New Delhi: Self-enumeration for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 began on Monday in UP, Punjab, Goa and non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand. It will run till Nov 30, followed by house-to-house enumeration from Dec 1. The exercise will collect data across 40 fields, including caste. The question is open-ended and reply will be recorded as declared by the respondent. No documentary proof or verification is required.MHA's Sept 5 notification advanced the exercise in the four states ahead of assembly polls early next year. It will run till Jan 4, 2027, followed by a revisional round from Jan 5 to 9.Though Manipur is due for assembly polls, the census there has been postponed until further notice amid demands for a National Register of Citizens (NRC) exercise first. World.title: At Sonia's book launch, Gandhis open up about love, loss, and bad chicken
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "And listen, if you want to fall in love, go to Varsity Restaurant in Cambridge. But never eat the chicken chasseur, okay?"

jokingly delivered this piece of advice at the launch of his mother

's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', in Delhi on Monday.

Years after hearing the story about his parents' first meeting in Cambridge, he recounted how he went to the Varsity Restaurant with his girlfriend to see where they had met.

When Rahul told the man at the entrance that his parents had met there, the man said he knew exactly who they were and recommended the chicken chasseur from the menu. However, the meal did not live up to its romantic legacy. Rahul contrasts his parents' memories of the restaurant with his own experience.



"They seem to remember that the food was fantastic. The food's horrible!" he said as the audience laughed.

The anecdote was part of a series of family recollections the leader of the opposition shared after saying he had been instructed to avoid politics. However, many read a political subtext into the seating arrangements. In the front row was an array of opposition leaders such as Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav; Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee; National Conference president Farooq Abdullah; Supriya Sule of NCP-SP; Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren; and Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay.





Also in the front row was former Punjab CM Captain Amarinder Singh, who left Congress in 2021 following a bitter falling-out with the Gandhis.

Rahul name-checked Amarinder and mentioned that he had seen his parents fight only once. Rajiv Gandhi was speaking to Amarinder on phone when Sonia tried several times to tell him something. Rajiv was stressed and eventually got angry. "We saw them argue many times, but that was the only time we ever saw them fight," Rahul said.

Sonia Gandhi too kept the conversation away from politics. Asked why she chose to write a memoir when she had guarded her privacy fiercely in the past, she said she wanted to set the record straight about her family amid "unreal stories" woven around them. "So much has been said about my mother-in-law, husband, son, daughter, and myself; and most of it is unreal. It has really nothing to do with the way we are. Stories are woven around you, untruths are woven around you, and hurtful things are said which are nowhere near the truth.

And I thought, well, perhaps this was a way of bringing out my feelings, what I know of my family, and maybe people will be open to listening to my story too," the Rajya Sabha MP said.

She recalled feeling like an outsider when she first moved to India, conscious of making mistakes. She connected that experience to Indian women who enter a new family after marriage and have to adjust to its ways. The memoir's title, she said, reflected "the effort to be accepted and to belong, to finally belong."

While she recounted a story of how she and Rajiv would go to India Gate to have ice cream (she had a favourite Sardarji ice cream vendor), Rahul spoke of his parents' affection and a habit he had assumed was common in every home: "Every meal there would be Papa and on Papa's lap there would be Mama." He said he realised it was unusual only when he visited friends' homes.

But things changed after the assassinations of Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, he said, "The fun-loving mother, the smiling mother disappeared."

Sonia, once an extrovert, withdrew into herself.

Rahul also spoke of his mother's resilience in the face of cancer, saying he had never seen her afraid or back down. He ended by telling her how proud he believed Rajiv would have been of her: "Mummy, Papa loved you. But I cannot even tell you how proud he would be of you."

World.title: Terror suspect in CRPF attack case killed in Kulgam, 1 flees

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: Wanted terrorist Mohammad Latief Bhat, carrying a Rs 15 lakh bounty, escaped an extended security cordon in south Kashmir's Kulgam district with bullet wounds, while his aide Umar Nasir was killed in a gunfight Monday, security sources said.

The duo was allegedly behind last week's attack that wounded three

personnel at Mir Bazar in Kulgam.

Latief, an A category terrorist, was believed to have fled into nearby forests after being hit by bullets during the gunfight. Nasir, classified as a B category terrorist, was killed and his body retrieved, police said. A woman who witnessed the operation confirmed Latief had been wounded.

Security forces have killed 16 terrorists in J&K this year

A police officer said intensive searches were under way to track Latief after the November 11 attack on a CRPF post at Mir Bazar. The attack ended a prolonged lull in strikes against security forces and triggered one of the longest search operations in Kulgam. A local overground worker was arrested for allegedly facilitating the two terrorists.

World.title: Amid China rivalry, India joins move to shield AI tech chain
World.content:
Pax Silica is the US State Department's flagship effort on AI (File photo/ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has joined United States and eight other Pax Silica initiative partners in signing the San Francisco Declaration to jointly protect critical infrastructure and supply chains essential for artificial intelligence (AI).The declaration is an international agreement that is being seen as an attempt to protect the full technology chain needed to build AI - from essential raw materials to manufacturing and energy networks.Amid intensifying rivalry with China, the agreement reinforces the importance of coordinated efforts to address economic coercion, supply chain disruptions, and non-market policies and practices and their market-distorting effects, while protecting private investment and ensuring a level playing field for innovation and growth.It treats the hardware, digital systems and logistics powering AI as vital national assets that partner countries must protect together for "economic security and enduring prosperity".Pax Silica is State Department's flagship effort on AI, renamed Super Intelligence or SI by President Donald Trump, and supply chain security, advancing new economic security consensus among allies and trusted partners."We affirm that the safeguarding of these sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure is a shared endeavour; that the security of each participant is strengthened by the vigilance of all; and that we engage in this common cause as aligned partners - in defense of prosperity and independence of our peoples," said the declaration.India joined US-led Pax Silica initiative in Feb this year, as both sides hailed a growing geopolitical consensus that "economic security is national security, and national security is economic security".State Department had then said India brings to Pax Silica a deep talent pool, processing and refining capacity for critical minerals, investments in AI infrastructure and an understanding of the importance of trusted technologies.The declaration was signed at a meeting of the founders of Pax Silica initiative convened by US Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg Sunday. It was released by govts of US, Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, UAE and UK.

World.title: Govt plans to set up visual library of stolen artefacts, deploy AI for verification

We have some incredibly interesting ones in India too that deserve a visit or two. Here are ten must-visit museums in India that offer unique and profound insights into the countryâs past and present:

NEW DELHI: The culture ministry plans to create a visual library of antiquities and artefacts stolen from India and use AI to track these globally, conduct preliminary verification of their photographic evidence, and seek repatriation.The ministry of culture plans to give shape to a provenance mission for antiquities wherein an artifact's ownership and collection history is traced back to its place of origin. Under this mission a database of stolen objects is proposed to be created based on information available across states where FIRs are lodged by law enforcement agencies regarding smuggling of antiquities.Culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal shared that they propose to use AI to expedite the verification process of photographic evidence available to establish that the object identified is the same as the one that is stolen and initiate action and seek repatriation after a physical verification.The images on the database created under the visual library will then be matched with information that may come on from museums, auctions and exhibitions from across countries.Aggarwal elaborated on the role of AI. âWhen a stolen object is spotted, you have to compare the dimensions and exact indentations with that of the original object. This kind of comparison of images can be done with the use of AI wherein the photo of the stolen object on display at some auction or gallery can be taken and put in the AI engine to get the exact details and establish that the object is the same or not,â Aggarwal shared.He shared that the ministry is also proposing to do a listing of museum objects where AI tools will be developed and deployed.Meanwhile, the ministry on Monday launched an AI based search and knowledge discovery engine on its primary website to enable people to access information on a wide-ranging issues at one place drawing from information from across 65 digital platforms related to the various institutions associated with the culture ministry which host extensive repositories of archives, manuscripts, museums, monuments, and the many programmes and campaigns.The search draws out relevant material from across 65 websites at once when a visitor types a question in the search section of the ministryâs website along with the source of the facts shared. Information can be accessed in all 22 scheduled languages.

World.title: News Analysis | Drone warfare leaves no safe zones in Sudan
World.content:
On October 18, there was a drone strike on a crowded transport hub near a market in Al-Dibab, a city in the West Kordofan State of Sudan. After ten minutes, a second drone struck the same place, and at least 139 people died in the attack. Eight days later, there was another drone strike in a market in Nyala, the capital city of South Darfur, killing over 100 people, according to the rights group, Emergency Lawyers.

These attacks point to the emergence of a concerning trend in the ongoing civil war in Sudan. What began as a fight for political supremacy between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in April 2023 is gradually evolving into a warfare campaign that heavily relies on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV).

World.title: BJP holds key party meeting in Mathura for Assembly polls
World.content:
Senior BJP leaders from Uttar Pradesh, including Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, attended a key meeting at the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Cow Research Institute in Parkham, Mathura, to discuss strategy for the upcoming U.P. Assembly polls.

The party announced the meeting to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and public welfare benefits, while also outlining electoral strategy and caste-based outreach to counter the Opposition’s renewed pitch.

“One goal, one idea... BJP government again for the third time... Today, in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, I participated in a planning meeting with National General Secretary (Organisation) B.L. Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and BJP Uttar Pradesh Incharge Shri Vinod Tawde,” wrote Pankaj Chaudhary, U.P. BJP president, on X.

“In the meeting, various important topics, including upcoming organisational programmes, booth empowerment, and providing benefits of public welfare schemes to every household, were discussed in detail. On this occasion, National General Secretary Irani, Deputy Chief Ministers Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya ji and Shri Brajesh Pathak, co-incharges of BJP Uttar Pradesh, Ministers of the State Government, public representatives, and state officials were present,” he added.

State Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya said the construction of a grand temple at Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi in Mathura will be a major poll issue in the 2027 U.P. elections, and that a grand Krishna temple will be built—through the courts or mutual dialogue, as with Ayodhya.

“If Akhilesh Yadav wants to join us in kar seva, we will take him along too to build a grand temple of Lord Krishna,” said the Deputy CM.

The meeting in Mathura is also significant amid the BJP’s emphasis on Mathura and western Uttar Pradesh. “The BJP holds meetings regularly to discuss organisational programmes, booth empowerment and other issues. Reach out to various sections of society is also part of our work,” said Dinesh Dubey, a senior BJP leader based in Lucknow.

Asad Rizvi, a political analyst based in Lucknow, said, “the meeting is significant as it is organised only a few months before the Assembly elections. Amid the main Opposition parties (the Samajwadi Party-Congress) pushing backwards, Scheduled Castes (SCs), Brahmins and marginalised groups through the PDA plank, the BJP will be recalibrating their policies and making a renewed effort towards them. ”

The SP president Akhilesh Yadav in a cryptic statement urged the BJP leaders to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. “I request them to take a dip in the Yamuna and sip its water before starting the event. It will be auspicious. If they fall ill, call a good doctor,” said Mr. Yadav.

World.title: Tribute to Kartar Singh Sarabha, Punjab free from drugs and unemployment, says CM Mann
World.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said on Monday (November 16, 2026) that the greatest tribute to the 19-year-old revolutionary and freedom fighter Kartar Singh Sarabha is to fulfil his dream of a Punjab free from drugs, unemployment, and injustice.

He was speaking after paying tribute to Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha on his 111th martyrdom anniversary at his native village, Sarabha, in Ludhiana district. The Chief Minister said his government is working to build the progressive Punjab they envision.

“Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha embraced the gallows at the tender age of just 19, proving that courage, conviction and love for the motherland know no age. At a time when youngsters today are planning their futures, this great revolutionary was planning the liberation of the country. He sacrificed his youth, dreams and ultimately his life for our freedom,” he said.

“On November 16, 1915, Shaheed Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail along with six other revolutionaries in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case. His fearless commitment to the freedom of the country remains a shining example of patriotism and selflessness,” he added.

As the Punjab 2027 Assembly election approaches, the drug menace has once again become a central campaign issue. In the run-up to the Assembly polls, the major political parties in the fray—the Congress, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), and the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)—are making the drug menace a key plank of their campaigns.

While the ruling party has been asserting that eradicating drugs is its “biggest priority,” the Opposition parties have accused the AAP of failing to curb the drug menace and instead patronising the drug trade.

World.title: Customers at some of the U.S.’ largest banks are reporting difficulty accessing accounts online
World.content:
Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some of the U.S.’ largest banks on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Bank of America, Chase, J.P. Morgan, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Zelle were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.

Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday (November 16, 2026).

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”

The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began on Friday (November 13, 2026) and lasted for hours, which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

Some Chase customers received a message that said, “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

World.title: Kishtwar killings aftermath: Remarks by Congress’ Karra, BJP’s Parihar spark protests in J&K
World.content:
Two separate remarks made by J&K Pradesh Congress Committee (JKPCC) president Tariq Hameed Karra and BJP legislator Shagun Parihar in the aftermath of the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar on Monday (November 16, 2026) sparked protests from different quarters.

In response to the statement by Mr. Karra that “two SPOs were killed reportedly by the Army in a mistaken identity case on November 11”, senior BJP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Sunil Sharma said, “The Congress is spreading misleading information to shift the blame from terrorists to our security forces. The SPOs were on duty and travelling to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah to relieve the jawans posted there. Calling two martyrs hunters is an insult to their sacrifice and to their grieving families.”

He demanded that Mr. Karra “immediately withdraw the remarks and apologise to the martyrs’ families, the J&K Police and the Indian Army”.

Scores of members of the BJP and BJP-affiliated organisations held street protests against Mr. Karra and the Congress in Jammu. Members of the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) also burn an effigy of Mr. Karra as a mark of protest.

BJYM leader Arun Prabhat, while condemning the statement of Mr. Karra, said, “It shows the hearts of Congress beat for Pakistan. The conspirators should face action. In case of any role of mosques, such places too should face action.”

Mr. Prabhat was seconding the controversial remarks of Ms. Parihar of the BJP, who claimed “announcements were made from the mosques in Kishtwar’s Dachhan area to identify the targets” allegedly ahead of the killings of two SPOs on November 11.

However, several religious organisations, including the Anjuman Islamia Bhaderwah and Kishtwar, in the Chenab Valley condemned the statement of Ms. Parihar and denied any role of mosques in the latest attack on the policemen. Ruling National Conference (NC) legislator Tanvir Sadiq said the BJP must be “held accountable for its MLA’s deeply irresponsible and inflammatory allegations against a mosque in Jammu”.

“Making communal allegations in the aftermath of a tragic killing is utterly unacceptable. The BJP leadership cannot hide behind silence or pretend this is an isolated matter. It must unequivocally condemn these remarks and issue an unconditional public apology. Stop playing with the communal harmony of J&K,” said Mr. Sadiq.

A spokesman of the All J&K Shia Association said the organisation “strongly condemn Ms. Parihar’s attempt to drag a mosque into the tragic killing of our brave SPOs”. “Terrorists are enemies of all humanity and terrorism has no religion. Unsubstantiated claims against a place of worship only weaken our fight against terror,” said the Association.

World.title: Christian community seeks West Bengal CM’s intervention over targeted attacks ahead of Christmas
World.content:
Ahead of the upcoming Christmas festivities, the representatives of Christian communities in West Bengal have expressed concerns about the rising attacks on churches across several districts in the State and have sought intervention from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.

During a press conference addressed by the Bengal Christian Council (a cluster body for Protestant churches), the Bishop of Calcutta, Reverend Paritosh Canning, said that the concerns of the people of the community are not without reason.

“West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony, where people belonging to different faiths and communities have coexisted in peace, mutual respect, and brotherhood. With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious. However, the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate festivals without fear or disruption,” the bishop said, speaking to media persons.

He added that such incidents have increased since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in West Bengal in May 2026. Attacks have been reported across several districts in South Bengal, on both banks of the Hooghly River, including South 24 Parganas, North 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, and Paschim Medinipur, among others.

Bishop Canning said that there are allegations of religious conversions in the churches, adding that “we can confirm that no conversion takes place at the churches operating under the Churches of North India.”

“All the minority communities used to live peacefully under the previous governments. However, it is not clear who the attackers are or why they are doing this,” he said.

In another development, representatives of Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) held a meeting in response to remarks by West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The State BJP president had on Sunday said that religious conversions are taking place across districts in West Bengal and issued a warning to Christian missionary schools in the State, claiming that they are targeting teachers wearing saffron sarees.

The Archbishop of Calcutta (Roman Catholic), Reverend Elius Frank, also participated in a meeting organised by BCP, though he did not speak to the media. In a letter addressed to Samik Bhattacharya, Herod Mullick, the founder-secretary of BCP, said that “if any institution or individual is found guilty of illegal or forced religious conversion through greed or deception, we strongly condemn such actions and stand firmly against them.”

“However, making broad, unsubstantiated generalisations without naming specific individuals or institutions unfairly casts a shadow of suspicion over the entire Christian community and the more than 800 educational institutions we operate across West Bengal,” the letter added.

World.title: West Bengal BJP supporters beating up own party members, says Union Minister as feuds rise in party
World.content:
Amid reports of growing feuds within the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in West Bengal, Union Minister of State and Bongaon MP Shantanu Thakur not only publicly acknowledged factionalism within the party but also said that BJP supporters are attacked by its members.

The Minister spoke about developments in his own constituency in North 24 Parganas, but reports of factional feuds within the BJP rank and file have surfaced across the State.

“Here, BJP workers are being beaten up, and those beating them are also from the BJP. The police administration has turned a blind eye and is not functioning impartially,” Mr. Thakur, who is the Bongaon MP and also a prominent leader of the Matua community, alleged.

The Minister, who hails from Thakurbari and is the religious head of the Matua community, said that divisions are emerging within the party, resulting in major problems. Differences between Shantanu Thakur, the Bongaon North MLA, and State Food and Civil Supplies Minister Ashok Kirtania have been going around in political circles.

On Sunday, BJP’s Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath, while expressing condolences over the death of a BJP worker, said that it would have been better “had the BJP not come to power in the State.” Arup Saha, husband of Ruma Saha—the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 Mandal (zone)—was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026), by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters. Saha succumbed to his injuries on Sunday.

Reports of an intra-party feud have surfaced between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after the Assembly election results in May 2026. Political observers say that the majority of the BJP leadership, including Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, had joined the party about five to six years ago.

State BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has repeatedly said that the doors of the party are closed for Trinamool supporters who want to join. Mr. Bhattacharya said that an FIR should be registered against elements who are trying to associate with the party and tarnish its image. “Register FIRs. Suvendu Adhikari is the police minister. Give me the papers; I will file them,” Mr. Bhattacharya said.

World.title: Murder of BJP worker by own party members sparks speculation of intra-party feud in West Bengal
World.content:
The violent death of a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) worker at Panihati, in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas district, on Sunday (November 15, 2026) has sparked speculation that an intra-party feud has broken out between long-time supporters of the ruling party in the State and former Trinamool Congress supporters who switched allegiance after Assembly election results in May.

Following the death of Arup Saha, the husband of Ruma Saha — the secretary of BJP’s Panihati-1 mandal (zone), Panihati MLA Ratna Debnath went on to say that she feels personally responsible for the death of the BJP worker.

“It would have been better had the BJP not come to.power,” Ms. Debnath had also said in the aftermath.

Ms. Saha’s husband was attacked on Saturday (November 14, 2026) by a mob that allegedly included some of the party’s supporters.
